Description En: The Gasthaus, which annexes the Kulturhof Stanggass located on the road between Bischofswiesen and Berchtesgaden, offers a culinary alternative to the restaurant Solo Du. Done out in light wood, the minimalist-style interior has a modern yet cosy feel. The glass façade affords views of the garden, which includes a children's playground. Book a spot at the "Stammtisch", a long handmade wooden table for 25 diners. The menu draws on the region and nature's bounty – the ingredients are locally sourced. The good food is complemented by friendly service.

Name: Gasthaus Waltz
Description En: This fashionable and lively restaurant in Munich's Glockenbackviertel is run by a dedicated young team. The secret of its success lies in its modern Alpine cuisine – it is by turns creative and traditional, but the sharp presentation is a constant, and the ingredients are the region's finest. Dishes such as "veal loin cordon bleu, Vulcano ham & potato salad with pumpkin seed oil" or "red veal lights, gherkins & Serviettenknödel (bread dumplings)" can be chosen à la carte or combined in a four or five-course set menu. The well-curated wine list is also surprisingly extensive – another highlight. In summer, guests are drawn to the terrace in front of the restaurant. N.B. Parking options are limited – it is best to get here by public transport.

Name: November Brasserie
Description En: This Japanese brasserie in a bustling neighbourhood of Prenzlauer Berg entices diners with an interesting range of Japanese specialities in the evenings – including sushi and sashimi, of course. The flambéed toro nigiri, for example, is a treat. Other draws of this place include competent service courtesy of a friendly and down-to-earth front-of-house team, and the pleasingly bright and modern minimalist-style interior, complete with a small sushi counter, where you can see the chefs at work. In summer, the outdoor tables shaded by trees are highly coveted.

Name: Holzgarten
Description En: The vibe of this charming, vibrant spot can be described as modern, understated and welcoming. Tucked away in the little Holzgartenstraße (after which it takes its name), the restaurant focuses on the use of seasonal ingredients in its kitchen, also embracing international influences. The dishes are often pared back to just a few components, carefully prepared for maximum flavour and nicely readable. Shining examples include "Traditional labneh, tomato, basil, parsley, spelt baguette" or "Two types of Ibérico, savoy cabbage, chorizo, mashed potato". Many dishes are also suitable for sharing. The menu, which is purposely kept short and changes frequently, is accompanied by a well-curated wine list. With its upscale, minimalist interior, including an open kitchen (with a handful of counter seats) and friendly, familiar service, the restaurant feels like a home from home. Lovely terrace. Be aware that bookings are possible for two time slots each evening.

Name: Kaufmann's Restaurant am Schlosspark
Description En: Set in a lovingly restored castle brewery, this restaurant serves freshly prepared, flavoursome dishes in an attractive space featuring exposed brickwork, vaulted ceilings and modern interior design. Friendly service. The cuisine has a regional dimension but also incorporates international influences, and stands out for its depth, flavour and confident execution. In addition to the frequently changing à la carte selection, there is the "Genießer-Menü", a set menu available in either a meat and fish or a vegetarian version, and the six- to eight-course "Gourmet-Menü", with optional wine pairing.

Name: Esszimmer
Description En: With its sleek, modern interior done out in warm hues, and friendly, professional waitstaff, as well as the regional and seasonal cuisine, this restaurant housed in a fitness centre a little out of town is very inviting. It's all about sharing here; tapas-style dishes are placed in the middle of the table for everyone to dig into – mix and match vegetarian, meat and fish options as you see fit. Perhaps you will be tempted by arancini stuffed with burrata and mushrooms, or samosa with locally hunted venison, sweetcorn and mint lassi. Be sure to try the wonderful spelt flatbread with one of the delicious dips! In keeping with the dining concept, dessert comes in the form of sweet tapas, such as salted caramel crème brûlée.

Name: Schatzhauser
Description En: Another iteration of the Finkbeiner family's Traube Tonbach suite of restaurants. The interior is minimalist and modern, airy and light, with a terrace boasting a great view of the valley. They serve a pleasant mix of international cuisine, seasonal dishes and regional classics, plus steaks cooked on the Lavastein grill. The service courtesy of well-trained staff is very friendly. Incidentally, the place is named after the good forest spirit from a Black Forest fairy tale.

Name: das asam
Description En: On the first floor of the former monastery building, the "Modlersäle" provide a striking setting with high ceilings, beautiful stucco work and paintings – tastefully combining a period backdrop with clean contemporary interior design. The cuisine is modern in inspiration and guided by the seasons. The menu balances international flair with regional roots – the "grilled octopus, textures of chickpea, tomato salad, basil essence" or the "duo of beef – roasted entrecôte & praline of braised shoulder" are fine examples. On warm summer days, the terrace in the cloister garden is idyllic! Service is well-organised, professional and highly attentive. Simple yet charming and well-kept guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Landgasthof zum Kaffelstein
Description En: Having already proven his talent at Kuno 1408 in Würzburg, Daniel Schröder has now struck out alone here with a dual concept: In addition to fine dining at La Boucherie, you can look forward to delicious seasonal cuisine in this lovely alternative. The menu is pared down to a limited number of dishes that focus on the essentials, leaving nothing to chance in terms of expression and flavour. In summer, the terrace in the courtyard is a pleasant place to sit. The hotel also has spruce, modern guestrooms.

Name: Die Krone
Description En: Chef-owner Markus Elison previously worked at Herrengass in Gschwend, where he proved his worth in the kitchen. Here, he cooks up delicious dishes made with high-quality ingredients. His cuisine is regional in spirit, occasionally accented with Mediterranean influences. The menu features options such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef in gravy, topped with crispy onions) in Pinot Noir jus with spaetzle, or pan-seared skrei fillet in a Riesling foam with creamy Filder cabbage. Dine à la carte or opt for the seasonal set menu or "Das Krone Menü". Friendly service. Sleek modern decor. There is also the Vesperstüble (small tavern) and a beer garden serving classics such as Strasbourg-style sausage salad or meat patties with a pepper cream sauce and croquettes. Comfortable modern guestsrooms are available, with simpler, more budget-friendly accommodation in the guesthouse.

Name: MASTAN
Description En: What a charming place! The classic bistro feel of this compact restaurant in Kreuzberg is inviting. Cordial, attentive and professional service also contributes to the pleasantly relaxed yet sophisticated atmosphere. In the kitchen, chef-patron Yann Mastantuono, who hails from southern France, gives expression to his passion for French bistro cuisine. Be sure to try the charcuterie, eg the "Bauernterrine". The "gambas tartare, citrus fruits and bottarga" or "veal tongue in charcutière sauce, grenaille potatoes in butter" are unfussy and delicious. In summer, head for the secluded terrace.

Name: Regional Friesoythe
Description En: "Regional" is more than just a name; it's a guiding philosophy in this tradition-steeped town-centre restaurant, run by Timo Plenter and Ina Stuke since September 2022. The chef-patron draws on locally sourced seasonal ingredients, and partners with regional suppliers to craft his flavourful dishes. There is a four- to six-course set menu, which also comes in a vegetarian version. A cheese course can be added on. The interior decor marries modern and rustic elements. Warm and attentive service. In summer, a few tables are set up in front of the restaurant for al fresco dining.

Name: Weinstube zum Engel
Description En: With his Weinstube (or "wine tavern"), Christian Beck, son of the owner of the hotel and restaurant Heiligenstein, also located in Neuweier near Baden-Baden, has brought a new layer of culinary enrichment to the village. The cuisine here comprises regional, seasonal and Mediterranean dishes. Vegetarian dishes and small bites are also available. Regional wines are offered. Friendly service in a cosy interior that blends tradition and modernity. The terrace is also lovely.

Name: Landgasthof zum Müller
Description En: In this well-established country inn, you can sense the dedication of owners Ingrid and Markus Buchner and their love for their profession. They serve fresh regional and seasonal cuisine with international and Mediterranean influences. "Müllers Küchengruß" – a creative amuse-bouche that changes daily – is a particular highlight. Contributing to the welcoming feel are cordial and personable waitstaff, as well as the rustic charm ambience of the dining rooms, not to mention the lovely verdant terrace with its gazebo ("Salettl"). For overnight stays, there are guestrooms done out in a modern rural style.

Name: Herrenhaus
Description En: Herrenhaus is located in the centre of the picturesque old town. A cloister, where you will find a quaint little terrace during the summer, leads you to the restaurant on the first floor. The historical setting adds to the warm and welcoming atmosphere. The delicious food is prepared using select in-season regional produce. The dishes are served à la carte or in the form of a set menu. Tip: Inexpensive lunch deal. The genial and obliging waitstaff will be happy to advise you on your choices. There is also an attractively priced wine list dedicated to German, Austrian and Italian labels.

Name: La Maison d'Avignon
Description En: Once the sommelier at Petit Amour on Spritzenplatz, Mathias Mercier has now realised his dream and opened his own restaurant just a short distance away. In a relaxed setting, diners are offered a small à la carte selection; if they wish, they can create a small set menu comprising three to six courses from the individual dishes. Alternatively, they can opt for the nine-course tasting menu – the value for money is excellent. The cuisine clearly draws on the chef-patron's southern French roots, featuring delicacies such as fougasse with a superb anchoïade (anchovy sauce) and pralines infused with lavender or pastis. A standout dish is the sea bass with peach, verbena and navy beans. The wine list includes some rare gems at reasonable prices. Friendly and attentive service.

Name: GRETA OTO Munich
Description En: For starters, the location right on the square known by locals as "Stachus" is nothing short of exclusive. GRETA OTO is housed within the luxurious and contemporary new Königshof hotel, on the ninth floor to be precise, affording fantastic views of the city of Munich and the Frauenkirche. The restaurant is no less chic and sophisticated than the hotel itself. Calm warm hues and dimmed lighting create an intimate atmosphere. The cuisine is Latin American with modern international influences, from Peruvian ceviche to Brazilian fillet steak and grilled octopus. The wine list to accompany the food is international. Tip: They have a private table – "La Mesa" – that you can book for special occasions. There is also a bar and a lounge terrace.

Name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
Description En: With this concept, Tim Raue has tapped into the zeitgeist. The ambiance feels like that of a French brasserie – stylish yet cosy. Service is well-organised, friendly and attentive, and the delicious food is prepared using select ingredients. Diners can order à la carte or compose their own four-course set menu, which can also be vegan. Classics such as beef Wellington (served for two) are available too, as well as seasonal dishes.

Name: Otto
Description En: Conveniently located in the city centre, a stone's throw from the cathedral and the Rhine River, this is the second maiBeck restaurant. In a trendy and chic setting, Jan C Maier and Tobias Becker serve up modern Italian cuisine with a focus on fish and seafood, although vegetarian options are also available. The pasta dishes are highly recommended. In addition to the excellent à la carte selection, the six-course "La Sera" set menu is available in the evening. The wine list is exclusively Italian. The front-of-house team are dedicated and attentive – the chefs also help to serve the food.

Name: Restaurant 1250
Description En: Even the drive up to the Boutique Hotel Blaue Burg is an exceptional experience: the view of the region is breathtaking, with a new photo opportunity at every turn. Against this sensational backdrop, the Schlachter family, known for their dedication to the job and their reliably good food, serves seasonally and regionally minded cuisine at Restaurant 1250 – making it a wonderful alternative to the fine dining restaurant, PAVO. The terrace with a view in the direction of the castle and Austria is simply divine. Good to know: they also serve lunch.

Name: Yabase
Description En: Calling all Japanese food aficionados! For an authentic experience, head to this restaurant in the centre of Düsseldorf's Japanese quarter. Behind a rather unassuming exterior an upscale minimalist-style space awaits. The service is friendly and professional. In the kitchen, top-notch fresh ingredients meet expert preparation techniques. The sushi and sashimi offer exceptional value, but more adventurous diners should try the unaju (rice bowl with barbecued eel) or the barbecued tuna head with vinegar for a real explosion of flavour. Complement your meal with some warm sake or Japanese beer. It is rare to get a table on the spur of the moment, so make sure you book in the evening. With a bit of luck, you can dine directly at the counter with its fish display case and watch the chefs at work. Lunch reservations are not possible – diners often queue at the entrance even before opening time.

Name: buffet Kull bar
Description En: A word to the wise: Book ahead to avoid disappointment at this trendy restaurant in the centre of Munich! The "French bistro meets New York steakhouse" concept is a hit. The atmosphere is lively, the tables are close together, and the service is both lively and attentive. But above all, it's the cuisine that impresses: Here, the focus is clearly on taste and ingredients – no visual frills needed. The cooking is precise and unpretentious. Mouth-watering options include the NY-style fillet steak with maître d'hôtel butter. For dessert, why not try the tarte Tatin served with vanilla ice cream and crème fraîche?

Name: Celia
Description En: For an authentic taste of Mexico in Düsseldorf, head to Celia in the bustling Bilker Kirche area. Rene Brauchle, of Mexican-German heritage and born in Venezuela, and Florentina Assis, a native Chilean, have been sharing their passion for Latin American cuisine here since summer 2024. The joy and enthusiasm of your cordial hosts is palpable, and they clearly love what they do: he is in charge of the kitchen, and she presides front-of-house. Once you have tried his mouthwatering dishes such as the taco pescado, the ceviche or the cochinita, you'll be hooked and eager to return. Fun fact: this friendly, modern restaurant is named after Rene's grandmother, who inspired his love of cooking.

Name: Restaurant Kurt im Gutshaus
Description En: A truly idyllic location. A cobblestone drive meanders through the stunning estate to the lovingly restored historical manor that houses this restaurant. Inside, contemporary design elements have been seamlessly incorporated into the classically elegant decor. The terrace overlooking the grounds is glorious in summer! Expect clearly structured modern cuisine made primarily with regional ingredients. There are two set menus: "Nachbarschaft" ("Neighbourhood") and the vegetarian "Ackerland" ("Farmland"), each comprising four to six courses. Dishes can also be ordered individually. Friendly service and astute by-the-glass wine recommendations add the finishing touch. The wine list features labels from around the globe. Tastefully furnished guestrooms are available at Gutshaus Stolpe hotel, where patrons can also relax in a heated outdoor pool and saunas.

Name: Acetaia
Description En: This delightful restaurant with a cosy atmosphere, Jugendstil decor and charming service has been around since 1999. It brings not only Italian joie de vivre but also Italian cuisine to the table – try the sheep's-cheese ravioli! If you are open to letting the kitchen surprise you, take a punt on the four-course "Giorgio's Set Menu". Alongside a good Italian selection, the wine list includes some rarities from France. Incidentally, you also have the opportunity to purchase the aged balsamic vinegar after which this place is named. In summer, head for the shady terrace. The location by the Nymphenburg Canal is conducive to taking a stroll.

Name: Atelier Gourmet
Description En: Small, intimate, lively and popular, Atelier Gourmet is quite simply a great little restaurant. The food is fresh, delicious and good value for money thanks to chef Bousquet. It is served in a casual, friendly atmosphere with efficient service and good wine recommendations from the female owner. Try the capon and duck crépinette.

Name: Gasthof zum Kranz
Description En: Built in 1769 and run by the same family for seven generations, the interior at Zum Kranz is modern and elegant in the minimalist style. The kitchens produce flavoursome, classic, international fare. If you come in the autumn, make sure you try the game!

Name: Freisinger Hof
Description En: Dating back to 1875, this traditional inn enjoys an idyllic location in Munich's Bogenhausen district, not far from the Englischer Garten. With its stylish yet cosy decor, the dining room oozes charm. The staff pull out all the stops to ensure a warm and personal atmosphere – the large number of regulars speaks volumes. Dishes are freshly prepared and full of flavour. The menu alternates between Bavarian and Austrian specialities – boiled beef from a fattened ox is as popular as Backhendl (breaded fried chicken), farmhouse duck or brook char fillet. Surrounded by greenery, the terrace makes for a wonderfully tranquil setting in summer. Reservations are recommended, not only at weekends! Immaculate, comfortable guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Le Schloss Halberg
Description En: The restaurant nestled in one wing of the castle, which was built between 1877 and 1880, has rightly proved to be a hit with diners. Its popularity is due both to the beautiful historical estate with its delightful terrace, and to the classic French cuisine – eschewing unnecessary frills in favour of full-bodied flavour, it is made with fresh top-notch ingredients. The speciality of beef fillet tartare with French fries and salad is prepared tableside. France also makes its presence felt in the savvy wine list.

Name: VOX Restaurant
Description En: Housed in Berlin's Grand Hyatt, very close to Potsdamer Platz, this is a modern and spacious restaurant with an open layout. Diners can enjoy an interesting fusion of authentic Japanese sushi and contemporary cuisine, either à la carte or as a five-course set menu. Friendly service completes the experience. Seats at the sushi counter are particularly popular. Tip: Alongside a fine selection of wines, there are creative cocktails, mocktails and a truly impressive array of whiskies from across the globe – the fabulous bar is not to be missed.

Name: Park Restaurant
Description En: Located at Parkhotel Bremen, this restaurant occupies an elegant conservatory overlooking the Bürgerpark and the lake (Hollersee). Frank Seyfried, previously at Gotthardt's in Koblenz, runs the kitchen, serving up a contemporary take on classic cuisine. Create your own three- to six-course set menu from a tempting array of dishes. The good food is complemented by friendly and adept service.

Name: Huber
Description En: Sandra and Michael Huber run their sleek, minimalist-style restaurant In an attractive residential area of Bogenhausen. Here, they serve flavoursome and ambitious contemporary cuisine that makes a pleasingly down-to-earth impression. There is a choice of two set menus (one of which is vegetarian), each comprising four or six courses, with dishes such as spinach with organic egg and Perigord truffle or skrei, beans and 'nduja. The wine list has a few gems in store, with plenty of appealing options for every budget.

Name: VINOTHEK by Geisel
Description En: Housed in the luxurious EXCELSIOR by Geisel hotel in the centre of Munich, not far from Stachus, Vinothek is a relaxed establishment done out in a cosy rustic style. The high cross-vaulted ceiling certainly has the wow factor, as does the array of decorative wine bottles. As you might expect from the name of this restaurant, delicious dishes that are inspired by the region and the Mediterranean – such as octopus carpaccio with fennel salad, potato, tomato and basil, or glazed veal cheek with truffle sauce, celeriac and mashed potato – are accompanied by a terrific selection of international wines. Comprising around 800 items, the list is dominated by German, French and Austrian labels. Tip: Check out their reasonably priced lunchtime set menu, which includes coffee and water. Cookery courses and "kitchen parties" are also organised.

Name: Weinhaus Neuner
Description En: With its cross-vaulted ceiling, herringbone parquet and wood panelling, this old restaurant has lost nothing of its traditional charm. The food is just what you would expect from an upmarket Munich inn – try the flaky pastry crust chicken fricassee pie. The Kaiserschmarrn for two is also a firm favourite! Nice wine list with a good selection of champagnes.

Name: Landhaus Hadrys
Address: An der Halberstädter Chaussee 1, Magdeburg, 39116, Germany
Description En: The name Sebastian Hadrys has been synonymous with quality cuisine since 2003. His seasonal dishes have a Mediterranean edge. In addition to an enticing à la carte selection, there is a sophisticated set menu comprising four to nine courses, as well as a special set menu to kick off the weekend on Friday evenings. The wine list is also very good. The pleasingly bright, modern space has a casual feel, plus a large terrace. Experienced staff provide friendly service. Tip: Cookery courses are also organised here.

Name: Zur Mühle
Description En: In their well-established restaurant – it’s been in the same family since 1895 – Hermann and Kerstin Berger prepare internationally inspired cuisine such as sliced salmon in a rocket and pesto crust with teriyaki beans, mashed potato and sweet mustard. The interior is cosy with a modern note.

Name: Gasthaus
Description En: Like the gourmet restaurant, Gasthaus also combines modernity and tradition, from the decor down to the menu. While things are a bit more casual here, the cooking is also really good – the quality of the sauces alone will convince you of that! You can put together your own menu – and even make it vegetarian. Friendly service.

Name: Locanda Grappolo d'Oro
Description En: It really is a joy to dine at this restaurant, which has been run by the same family with great dedication for years. The decor is bright and cheerful, and warm hospitality and service come courtesy of the lady of the house. The Mediterranean-inspired cuisine is fresh and delicious. The pasta, the gnocchi, the bread… It's all house-made. No wonder this place draws so many regulars from the region.

Name: Hebelstube
Description En: This establishment has been a familiar and beloved landmark for decades. Part of the long-established Hotel Alte Post, the restaurant serves seasonal cuisine made with regionally sourced ingredients, with dishes such as calf's head, risotto and chard, or Black Forest salmon trout and crayfish lasagne with spring vegetables, citrus-infused beurre blanc and verbena shellfish emulsion, available either as a set menu or à la carte. The wine list homes in on labels from the region. Add to that a friendly and charming atmosphere, and very attentive, solicitous service. The terrace is delightful in summer. Their contemporary-style guestrooms are ideal for an overnight stay.

Name: Johanna Berger
Description En: Tucked away in a fine 19C building in the centre of Lübeck, this restaurant has a charming interior with wooden flooring, chandeliers and an elegant feel. The pretty terrace enjoys an appealing location to the rear of the building. On the menu: a modern take on Mediterranean cuisine, available as a surprise menu or à la carte. Nice selection of German and international wines, also available by the glass.

Name: Weinhaus Anker
Description En: Run with great dedication, this restaurant is steeped in tradition. The original charm of the building has been beautifully retained in the dining spaces – eg the Alte Stube with its wood panelling and ceiling paintings, and Im Fachwerk with its combination of rustic old beams and modern design features. The cuisine is predominantly regional, but the menu also includes French-influenced dishes. Friendly service. Tip: The Holzfasskeller, a 400-year-old wine cellar, can be booked for events. Well-appointed guestrooms.

Name: handicap.
Description En: There is temporarily a change of concept here, with an amended menu, "Restaurant Würzburger Bau", being served until the end of June. From July onwards, fine dining cuisine will be back. As its name suggests, this tastefully decorated restaurant in a side wing of Hotel Anne-Sophie employs differently abled people, and the success of the initiative is clear to see in the great team. In the stylish decor, clean lines meet artwork, including a celestial painting by Markus Schmidgall on the high ceiling. The small terrace in the courtyard is delightful on a fine summer's day.

Name: schuberts
Description En: Located in the centre of town, right by the Lauter River, this popular restaurant has a casual brasserie feel and serves flavoursome regional and seasonal cuisine that draws on Mediterranean influences. The daily special, "Schuberts Schneller Teller" ("Schubert's Quick Plate"), is a hit at lunchtime. Entennest is a cosy and charming wine tavern that makes for a more rustic alternative – the menu is the same here in the evening. If you would like to stay overnight, the hotel of the same name has attractive individually furnished guestrooms.

Name: Hinterding
Description En: Dating back to 1904, this spruce urban villa has been known as a stylish culinary destination for aeons. Owners Klaus Weingartz (kitchen) and Elke Zeitner (front of house) have been running this establishment with great dedication since 2011. Ambitious classic cuisine made with select ingredients is served by charming waitstaff in comfortable and elegant dining rooms with high ceilings, or out on the gorgeous terrace. Set menus can even be pre-ordered to take home. Cookery classes and overnight accommodation are also available.

Name: Villa Feer
Description En: Owner Kathrin Bucher has been running this restaurant in an attractive old villa near Lörrach exhibition centre since 2012. Dine in the cosy, bright interior or, in summer, out on the wonderful terrace. They serve lunch only: until 3pm you can order the set menu or from a small menu compiled from favourite dishes of the last decade. After that, there are desserts and ice creams/sorbets until 5pm.

Name: Gasthaus Stappen
Description En: Steeped in tradition, this establishment is run with great dedication. Diners are drawn by the attentive service provided by the friendly and adept staff, as well as the excellent food. The regional cuisine is replete with international influences. The leafy terrace is delightful in summer. Ask about the wine tastings held in the wine shop. Tip: There are chic, modern guestrooms should you wish to stay overnight. N.B. card payment only.

Name: Planerts
Description En: Casual fine dining near the church (Nikolaikirche) and opera house (Leipzig Oper). The high ceilings, exposed ventilation shafts, urban design and open kitchen create an on-trend industrial-style interior in which to savour cuisine with Asian influences. The dishes can be combined to compose a set menu or chosen à la carte. Friendly service and good wine recommendations. Thu-Sat, lunch takes the form of a dish of the day or a three-course set menu.

Name: Hirsch Genusshandwerk
Description En: This lovely village inn serves dishes with classical foundations and modern inspirations. The seasons call the shots, and there is a preference for quality produce sourced locally or even grown in the restaurant's own garden. Led by the proprietress, the cordial and competent front-of-house team helps create the welcoming atmosphere. The terrace is delightful in summer. They also have their own distillery.

Name: ZEN Japanese Restaurant
Description En: Located in a residential area, this restaurant is a firm favourite with fans of Japanese cuisine. In a pared-back Far Eastern-style setting, diners can look forward to a pleasantly lively atmosphere, as well as friendly and professional service with an authentic Japanese touch. It is clear that a well-coordinated team is at work here. Your options include gyoza, tempura, grilled and pan-fried dishes, udon, sushi and sashimi, plus a large omakase set menu. Wine, sake and Japanese whisky to go with it.

Name: Caroussel Nouvelle
Description En: In the attractive Bülow Palais in Dresden's Baroque Quarter, the bistro and winter garden have been combined into Caroussel Nouvelle, with a stylish interior by acclaimed designer Carlo Rampazzi. At lunch and dinner, an appealing à la carte menu is available alongside a three- or four-course set menu. The cooking is inspired by both French and regional traditions and shaped by the seasons. The flavour, technical skill and quality of the ingredients are all equally strong. Classics feature as well as more modern creations. For an aperitif or digestif, head to the Palais Bar and Cigar Lounge.

Name: NeoBiota
Description En: Chef-patrons Sonja Baumann and Erik Scheffler propose ingredient-forward seasonal cuisine. The concept is strictly regional and forward-thinking: the majority of the ingredients are sourced from the surrounding area; some they even forage themselves. They draw heavily on produce from their own garden in Leverkusen and will gladly tell you about the provenance of all the produce. The food is predominantly vegan-vegetarian, with pescetarian and "omnivore" options available. The "Biota" evening set menu is composed of four, six or eight courses, including, for example, "grilled mushroom shashlik with broccoli & spruce" or "Eifel beef with blueberries, bitter lettuces & grapes from Cologne". The house classic, "Viking muesli", is often served as an amuse-bouche. The wine list homes in on organic, biodynamic and natural wines. A good selection of wines or alcohol-free drinks is available by the glass to pair with the set menu. The appealing space has a clean-lined, modern style; the terrace is also lovely. As Neo, they serve an enjoyable breakfast from 10am to 3pm.

Name: Gruber's Restaurant
Description En: Austrian cuisine is served in this charming restaurant with its various tastefully decorated rooms and pretty terrace. Whether traditional (such as the excellent schnitzels and memorable Kaiserschmarrn – shredded pancakes) or modern (Carinthian cheese noodles, pointed cabbage and blueberries), the dishes are always made from carefully chosen ingredients. More limited options, plus a schnitzel menu at lunchtime.

Name: Alfredo
Description En: If you are in the mood for authentic Italian cuisine in Cologne, Roberto Carturan is your man. His father, Alfredo, laid the foundations for upscale Italian cuisine in 1973, and the second generation of the Carturan family has cultivated a straightforward and minimalist style of cooking. Without a doubt, the house classic is the pappardelle with braised duck. The charming chef-patron is on hand and will talk you through the menu in person. The atmosphere is relaxed – the focus is on pleasure. You can feel that the whole team is genuinely invested in your experience. Besides cooking, Roberto Carturan has another talent: he is a trained singer – on Friday evenings there's the "musical culinary soirée": a six-course set menu with a performance by him as the finale! One practical tip: Parking is available in the Opern Passagen shopping centre located behind the restaurant. You might also take the opportunity to see the original 4711 store with its famous carillon.

Name: Alte Mühle Thomas Höreth
Description En: With this individual and thoroughly charming establishment the Höreth family have created a wonderful retreat. The guest lounges are lovingly decorated and the inner courtyard is idyllic. This is a real gem of a place, which also has its own wine estate. Slightly higher up, charming rooms are available for guests to stay the night.

Name: Oberländer Weinstube
Description En: This townhouse, built in 1826, is full of charm: inside you sit in a cosy, traditional wood-panelled decor, while the charming courtyard beckons outside. And in addition they take really friendly care of you. The kitchen turns out dishes that are adapted to the seasons and really tasty. At lunchtime you choose from a smaller menu.

Name: Weingärtnerhaus
Description En: Not only does this place promise good food, but the setting is also inviting: the restaurant is located in a lovely winegrower's house (named after the vineyards below). Built in 1542, it stands directly on the historical estate of Schloss Leitheim. Season-driven cuisine is served in a lovely, cosy interior. On Sundays and Mondays there is a more limited offering in the form of the Azubi-Menü devised by the trainee chefs. Tip: The wine list includes a number of South African vintages. Should you wish to stay overnight, the Schloss Leitheim hotel has inviting guestrooms.

Name: Landgrafen
Description En: The restaurant close to the observation tower, also known as the Balcony of Jena, serves regional cuisine and offers a fantastic view over the city. Three individual rooms are available: country, Art Deco or honeymoon.

Name: Alemannenhof
Description En: This historical Black Forest establishment in an idyllic location is thoroughly inviting. Inside, an attractive upscale dining space exuding bags of regional charm awaits. Affording magnificent views of the lake, the terrace beckons in summer. The menu takes its cue from the seasons and includes dishes such as Black Forest trout fillets with pickled cherry tomatoes, courgettes and parsley mashed potatoes or French corn-fed poularde breast, tender young beans and thyme pasta. There is also a "Gourmetmenü" comprising five or eight courses with wine pairings. Options are more limited at lunchtime. For overnight stays, the boutique hotel of the same name has guestrooms that seamlessly blend modern and traditional elements.

Name: Krone
Description En: Krone has been properly invested in: from the façade to the hotel rooms, everything is chic and high quality, the restaurant is modern and sleek. The food is very good, with select produce turned into aromatic dishes with plenty of flavour. At lunchtime, a smaller range of interesting options. If you are staying longer, Basel and Alsace are very close by.

Name: Gasthaus Spieker
Description En: In its tasteful, beautifully decorated dining rooms, Gasthaus Spieker serves regional cuisine with a Mediterranean touch. The appealing menu whets the appetite with dishes such as "Spieker's fish soup" with trout from the Ems River and prawns, or medium-rare lamb rump with rosemary and lemon zest, thyme and red wine sauce, French beans with bacon, and potato gratin. If you fancy enjoying an extra glass or two of wine, there are also a number of well-appointed guestrooms.

Name: SCALA - Das Turm Restaurant
Description En: At 128m above street level, the striking JenTower affords fantastic views of the city and surrounding area! The cuisine is modern and international: dinner takes the form of a sharing menu comprising three to five courses (vegetarian version available); the lunchtime selection is a little more streamlined. Tip: From the Neue Mitte multi-storey car park, take the lifts up to the restaurant (there is a sign). Hotel on the floors below the restaurant.

Name: Heinzler am See
Description En: Whether you are in the mood for regional comfort food or something more international, the Heinzler brothers have got it covered. Their wide-ranging menu includes Swabian Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy), Arctic char and whitefish fillets, and yellowfin tuna sashimi. There is also an appealing selection of barbecue dishes with a choice of side dishes and sauces. You can choose to dine in the cosy Jagdstube ("hunting lounge") with its winning blend of traditional charm and modern design, or the lovely Panorama-Restaurant, whose large windows afford stunning views. Not forgetting the fabulous terrace almost touching the water! The waitstaff are personable and attentive – service is clearly a serious matter here. Tasteful and comfortable guestrooms available at the hotel, which also boasts a private beach area at the lake and a private jetty.

The name of the game here is a culinary fusion of Peru and Italy. Drawing on his Peruvian heritage and inspired by life in Italy, head chef Matias Diaz weaves together produce from both countries in his "136 Experience Menü", a set menu that changes every two months. The restaurant's trendy vintage decor brims with charm. In summer, there are also tables outside.

Name: Freihardt
Description En: Eating here is a real pleasure! The cuisine is international and seasonal, the highlight being the Bavarian beef steaks. They also serve burgers on Wednesdays and Thursdays. Head here on a Saturday for a three-course surprise lunch or on a Sunday for a traditional home-style roast. A friendly atmosphere reigns in the restaurant and its conservatory, and the terrace on the busy street is a place "to see and be seen". Right next door is the restaurant's own butcher's shop, which for many years has employed so-called humane slaughtering methods.

Name: Ole Liese
Description En: Steeped in history, Gut Panker is a truly idyllic spot. The tranquil estate is the epitome of rural charm and is also known as a Trakehner stud farm – it forms the perfect backdrop for Hotel & Restaurant Ole Liese. The motto "Sunday cooking. Every day" underpins a menu of regional seasonal fare, which is served in the cosy, rustic interior, or out on the lovely terrace in summer. In addition, the estate's pretty café in the old night watchman's lodge serves coffee and cake from 2-5pm, and on Sundays, brunch is available by prior reservation. Overnight stays are possible in stylish, individually decorated guestrooms.

Name: aerde
Description En: Housed within the imposing building designed by architectural firm Robertneun in the Lokdepot development, this compact restaurant is well worth seeking out. In the kitchen, set on a mezzanine above the dining space, the chefs create modern dishes designed for sharing. Seasonal ingredients take centre stage, with fermentation playing a key role – a theme echoed by the decorative jars displayed throughout the pared-back interior, which features clean lines, wood finishings and earthy hues. Capacity is limited to a few small tables, a communal table in the middle and the bar counter. The atmosphere is neighbourly and personal; service is friendly and adept. The team are happy to provide drinks recommendations, drawing from an exciting selection.

Name: Teko by Lange Rodriguez
Description En: Teko refers to "culture" in Spanish. As the son of a German father and Bolivian mother, chef-owner Hans Robert Lange Rodriguez has a mantra of "two cultures, one flavour". His set menu incorporates influences from both South America and Germany, blending traditional and modern cuisine. Choose either the five- or seven-course format of the set menu, which features dishes such as "egg, cassava, ají amazónico, mustard" or "red trout, cupuaçu, parsnip, radish". There is also a vegetarian version of the set menu; vegan requests should be specified when booking. An interesting detail on the wine list: the Bolivian wines are labelled with the altitude of the vine-growing region. In addition to wine pairings for the set menu, there is an ambitious selection of alcohol-free pairings. Attentive and professional service. The cosy modern space is decorated with beautiful photographs from Bolivia and pleasant background music contributing to a South American vibe.

Name: Fa:me
Description En: This intimate little restaurant with a buzzing, neighbourly atmosphere calls itself a "gastrobar", and that pretty much hits the nail on the head, as food and drinks have equal billing here. Located in the Kreuzkölln neighbourhood, this place is run by the two owners, who divide their time between the kitchen and service. Although limited, the à la carte selection is well-devised, comprising ambitious modern dishes. There is also a 10-course tasting menu for two or more people to share. A glance at the drinks menu is enough to reveal their passion for carefully selected wines, their own cocktail creations and house-made kombucha – and guests are taken through the options by the charming and enthusiastic staff, who bring a pleasingly personal touch.

Name: Gasthaus zum Raben
Description En: This charming farmhouse dating back to 1604 is truly idyllic! Set at an altitude of around 600m, it boasts a beautiful location with views of Freiburg. Inside, low ceilings, rustic wooden seats and benches, wooden floorboards and an old tiled stove make for a cosy atmosphere and tap into the character of the region. Dedicated owners Melanie and Pierre Barrel are in the thick of the action here – she heads up the friendly and professional service team; he runs the kitchen. Diners are served a "carte blanche" menu of four or six courses, inspired by the seasons and the proprietors' French heritage. In addition to the restaurant, there is a bistro section with a short à la carte menu. The garden and terrace are real highlights – in summer, guests naturally gravitate outdoors. Those looking to stay a little longer and explore the wonderful Black Forest landscape can spend the night in one of the attractive, comfortable rooms available in the charming guesthouse.

Name: Schote
Description En: Now that Nelson Müller and his team have moved from Essen to Bergisch Gladbach, the affable restaurateur and celebrity chef is showcasing his dine dining cuisine at Diepeschrather Mühle, a converted mill set in beautiful natural surroundings. They serve a modern, ambitious set menu with seasonal influences. Great attention to detail and an unfailing sense of balance never fail to impress in dishes such as "Seabed" – turbot, roe sauce, morel ravioli, mandarin, caviar or "From the Bresse" – imperial quail, spring chicken, pointed cabbage, duck liver, grapes. The vegetarian version of the set menu needs to be ordered in advance. Consider opting for the wine pairings to accompany the set menu. Attentive and professional service is provided by a well-staffed team, and the chefs even get in on the act. Here at the new location, there is a brasserie as an alternative to the restaurant: Müllers in der Mühle. For a really chic overnight stay, this gorgeous property also houses an exquisite boutique hotel with tasteful modern rooms and suites, as well as an attractive wellness and spa area.

Name: Feine Kost
Description En: In August 2024 Mario Pattis established his Feine Kost restaurant, which entices diners with an appealing variety of modern-creative and classic cuisine. In a chic neighbourhood of Dresden Neustadt, the establishment serves dishes that are packed with flavours and interesting textures – these are organised into a set dinner menu with a choice of main course and dessert. The starter variation with various small dishes such as ‘duck liver, apricot jam, toasted brioche’ is a real delight. The wine pairing is also recommended. The decor is sleek and modern, with an eye-catching wall decorated with porcelain crockery. Large windows look out onto the beautiful terrace laid out in the charming courtyard, which is accessed via the restaurant. The atmosphere is relaxed and the service professional. For a simpler alternative, Kantine is a charming option on the same premises.

Name: Untere Apotheke
Description En: With its chic and trendy bistro feel and easygoing buzz, this restaurant right on Marktplatz is especially inviting. The food is in keeping with the modern setting, with a thoughtfully compiled menu featuring creative dishes based on classic recipes. Ambitious, precisely crafted and visually very appealing, these are prepared in a small glass-fronted kitchen – diners in the four counter seats are guaranteed some fascinating insights. In addition to the à la carte selection, there are two set menus. At lunchtime, the options are somewhat simpler and more limited. A fantastic initiative: In collaboration with a local vocational training centre (Berufsbildungswerk Waiblingen) , they run a garden project on Schmidberger Feld, embracing a farm-to-table approach. Tip for motorists: Marktgarage underground car park is nearby.

Name: Dallmayr Bar & Grill
Description En: Located next to the delicatessen on the ground floor, this Dallmayr restaurant is steeped in tradition and offers a lively and relaxed, yet stylish dining experience. At closely spaced tables, diners enjoy prompt and adept service provided by a courteous and well-staffed front-of-house team in white uniforms. From oysters and caviar to seafood and Bavarian ribeye with balsamic pearl-glazed onions, the international menu certainly whets the appetite. Be sure to sample the beef tomato with feta, honey and sesame. The bar is another highlight, perfect for unwinding with a pre-dinner drink.

Name: Marly Privé
Description En: The restaurant previously known as "Marly" has moved and is now operating under the name of Marly Privé. In its smaller space, this eatery serves classic French cuisine made from top-notch ingredients – chef-owner Gregor Ruppenthal's love for France is on full display. Accessed via Le comptoir 17, a cosy back room accommodates up to 12 diners who sit down to a five- or seven-course tasting menu – a four- or five-course version is served on Fridays. Dishes have names such as "Our octopus salad depuis 1999" or "Line-caught sea bass from Quiberon, leek, nori, pink onions", and are accompanied by a well-curated wine list. The service is friendly and attentive. Tip: Don't forget to reserve your spot!

Name: Silberstreif
Description En: The Naturresort & Spa Schindelbruch features an ambitious restaurant concept called Silberstreif ("Silver Lining"), named after the 2022 butterfly of the year. Head chef Eric Jadischke and the young team rustle up contemporary cuisine inspired by the Harz region and its seasons. Some of the ingredients come from the garden that was planted with the restaurant's needs in mind. There is a five- to seven-course set menu, with corresponding wine or non-alcoholic pairings on request. Service is friendly and attentive. You might be interested to know that the dishes are served on Ritter von Kempski collection porcelain, designed by MEISSEN exclusively for this restaurant. The impressive pieces by artist Johann Elias Ridinger draw the eye with their hunting and forest motifs – a nod to the restaurant's close connection with nature. The hotel has tasteful guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Aifach Reisers
Description En: On the site of the city's erstwhile covered market, Bernhard Reiser – inspired by that previous vocation – has brought to life a friendly, casual, seasonal restaurant concept. At lunchtime, a concise, reasonably priced menu including an enticing three-course set menu is served; in the evening, the cuisine is more ambitious and comes in à la carte or surprise menu form. Tables are laid out on the ground floor and in the gallery. From some seats you have a direct view of the action in the open kitchen on the lower level. In summer, head for the terrace overlooking the market square.

Name: Lido Hafen
Description En: The location in the MedienHafen (Media Harbour) is remarkable in its own right: the restaurant occupies a minimalist glass cube hovering over the water, accessible via a bridge. The dedicated owners are a husband-and-wife team, who some might know from the restaurants Fritz's Frau Franzi and Pink Pepper. Ramona Kriegel heads up the friendly and professional service team while Benjamin Kriegel prepares a modern set menu comprising five to seven courses. The chef takes pride in his ingredients, which are always in season and of the finest quality. Wine pairings available.

Name: MA PETITE CHAMBRE
Description En: Carina and Christoph Schmah now have a wonderful second eatery for their hotel and restaurant, Landhaus Halferschenke, in the form of this small fine dining restaurant. Behind the pretty quarry stone façade of this historical building, the space has a pleasantly calm and elegant atmosphere. Expert wine recommendations come courtesy of the cordial and proficient service team. The food is modern but grounded in the classics, with the chef-patron rustling up a six- to eight-course set menu out of top-notch ingredients. The restaurant has just four tables, for up to 12 guests, so be sure to book!

Name: Il Borgo
Description En: This Italian restaurant has been a mainstay of Schwabing's culinary scene since 1989. The interior is modern and elegant yet cosy, with the current decor successfully incorporating the old wall tiles and original bar. The menu sticks close to the seasons. In addition to the five-course tasting menu, there is an à la carte selection – from delicious pasta dishes to branzino al sale (salt-baked sea bass) for two.

Name: AL FORNO
Description En: For fans of authentic Italian food, this ristorante makes for a pleasing alternative to JUWEL and WEBERSTUBE, the other two restaurants to be found here in the Hotel BEI SCHUMANN. Soak up the atmosphere in the wonderfully cosy dining area, in which Italian background music brings that feel-good factor, while the team in the open kitchen conjure up delicious fish and meat dishes, as well as classics such as antipasti, pasta and pizza cooked in the brick oven – the pizzas are available in smaller sizes, too. Desserts such as the zabaione di Marsala are also delicious. Speciality in winter: spaghetti from the parmesan cheese wheel. In summer, head for the pleasant terrace overlooking the SEEWUNDERBAR.

Name: Weinwirtschaft Kleines Jacob
Description En: As soon as you enter this restaurant, you fall into the embrace of its inviting atmosphere: Charming tavern-style decor, soft candlelight and warm, attentive service make for a delightful setting – no wonder so many locals flock here as regulars. The Austrian cuisine is a hit – the "Schmankerl Brett" (snack platter) and stone-baked flammkuchen, as well as Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) and Wiener schnitzel are crowds-pleasers, not forgetting the caramelised Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake) with stewed plums. There is also an appealing three- or four-course set menu dubbed "Lütten Jacob Genusstafel". The wine list is exclusively Austrian, and some labels are available by the glass. No wonder this place has become a favourite of so many foodies!

Name: Einhorn
Description En: This handsome inn steeped in history has been given a successful modern makeover. Inside, the pleasant decor is characterised by clear lines, warm wooden finishings and a palette of neutrals; outside, behind the building, the pretty, secluded terrace is extremely inviting. The menu features typical Swabian dishes, but also more sophisticated international dishes. You can opt for a set menu or select dishes from the à la carte menu.

Name: Hippocampus
Description En: In the city's well-heeled Bogenhausen area, Hippocampus is no run-of-the-mill Italian restaurant; it is a ristorante with real character. The reins of this family business have now been passed on to the next generation, which is upholding the tradition of serving Italian cuisine. Order à la carte dishes or opt for the surprise menu. A two-course set lunch is available Wed-Fri. The impressive wine list features around 160 Italian labels. Expect attentive service, delivered with Italian charm. Add to this an attractive interior with stylish details such as half-wall panelling in walnut wood, marble floors and Art Nouveau lamps. The terrace is equally inviting.

Name: Galleria
Description En: This extremely pleasant establishment is an institution here in the city centre – the small restaurant near Marienplatz has been around since 1998. A friendly atmosphere is fostered by the modern decor, with pictures and wine racks adding a nice decorative touch – royal blue gives the whole place a maritime feel. They serve really good Italian cuisine, including classics such as vitello tonnato and house-made pasta. At lunchtime, diners appreciate the competitively priced lunch set menu. The extensive wine list featuring wines from Italy is on point. Staff are attentive and knowledgeable. In summer, a table on the small terrace is a tempting prospect.

Name: Blauer Bock
Description En: A cornerstone of the fine dining scene for years, this restaurant is housed in the spruce hotel of the same name, nestled in the centre of Munich – a stone's throw from the Viktualienmarkt and the city museum. The decor is tasteful, sleek and contemporary in style, with striking pictures adorning the walls. The cuisine is classic with a modern twist, and the menu includes mouthwatering options such as braised veal shoulder or sole for two. Outside, the tables overlooking the pedestrian area are in high demand.

Name: Little London
Description En: This lively steakhouse not far from the Isartor is fronted by a classic bar of impressive dimensions – there are over 320 types of gin to choose from here! The attractive interior design successfully brings together a certain rusticity and a touch of English elegance. Meat eaters can look forward to high-quality cuts cooked on the Montague grill – tantalising examples include US Black Angus Prime Beef and Wagyu Kagoshima A5. There are over 250 wines on the wine list. Tip: Why not sign up for one of their beef-tasting sessions? With its various lounges, the restaurant also caters to private parties.

Name: Matsuhisa Munich
Description En: In keeping with the high standards of the luxurious Mandarin Oriental, this elegant minimalist-style restaurant is run by Nobu Matsuhisa, a renowned restaurateur with a global presence. The menu features a fusion of Japanese and Peruvian cuisines. As well as sushi and sashimi, there are exciting options such as Peruvian rib eye anticucho (skewers) or the house classic, black cod. Dishes are intended for sharing, allowing you to discover a kaleidoscope of flavours. In summer, you can dine on the hotel's roof terrace and take in fantastic views over Munich.

Name: Jin
Description En: This restaurant that has been around for 20 years is certainly an institution. The many regulars appreciate the upscale minimalist-style interior inspired by the Far East, and the flavoursome pan-Asian cuisine, in which a distinct Chinese edge, as well as Japanese and European influences, can be detected. Diners can choose between the "Jins Degustation" set menu and an appealing à la carte selection. We particularly recommend the spring rolls, the bluefin tuna tartare and the handmade dim sum. The wine list is also excellent – connoisseurs will find something to their liking here.

Name: KOI
Description En: Fans of modern Japanese cuisine should head here for the extensive range of sushi, as well as meat, fish and vegetable dishes and snacks. Some items are cooked on the Robata charcoal grill. Tempting options include "beef fillet teriyaki, Jerusalem artichoke chips, wafu" or "grilled miso aubergine, daikon salsa". With its dark wood, warm lighting and stylish details, the interior has an elegant, urban atmosphere; meanwhile, the bar on the upper floor exudes a loungey vibe. On fine summer days, the terrace is highly prized.

Name: Landhaus Mönchenwerth
Description En: This inviting establishment has its fair share of regulars, and deservedly so. One of the main attractions is its location right by the Rhine – tables with a view of the river, as well as those on the gorgeous terrace, are in high demand. No less captivating are the creations of chef-patron Guy de Vries, whose French heritage shines through in work. Drawing from the bounty of each season, he concocts mouthwatering plates with a Mediterranean twist. The well-curated wine list includes an impressive selection of Champagnes. Friendly and adept service.

Name: Landhotel Donner
Description En: At the idyllically located Landhotel Donner, diners sit in snug dining rooms where warm wood and pretty fabrics create a charming, traditional setting. The cuisine is classic and regional with seasonal influences; tempting choices include house-made jellied knuckle of pork with remoulade sauce and fried potatoes, or braised leg of wild boar in a liquorice jus with parsley root purée. Order à la carte or opt for the four-course surprise menu. Service is friendly and attentive. In the summer, the terrace to the rear of the building is a lovely spot. Now run by the third generation, the Donner family's hotel offers well-appointed, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Gräfinthaler Hof
Description En: In this somewhat more remote part of the Bliesgau region, you will feel most welcome in this gorgeous location that was once home to a monastery complex dating back to the 13C. Inside, an elegant atmosphere prevails; outside, there is a charming terrace shaded by trees. Ambitious dishes are created with terrific ingredients – the roast dry-aged pork chop (matured on the bone for 21 days), with sage, Serrano ham, market vegetables and potato fritters, for example, is a wonderful meat option. There are two set menus – one meat, one vegetarian – or you can dine à la carte.

Name: Wettsteins Restaurant
Description En: This beautiful property is a little out of the way – on summer days, diners can enjoy sitting out on the terrace. The restaurant has been around for many years. In addition to cordial hosts and friendly service, the programme here includes regionally influenced cuisine, which you can choose to sample as a set menu or à la carte. The menu also features barbecued meat, such as rump steak, and classics like schnitzel and roast joint.

Name: Michaelis
Description En: Tasty and fresh food is served in this refined restaurant in a restored building from the Wilhelminian period, which also houses the comfortable hotel of the same name. The menu is seasonal – there are various set menus (one of which is vegetarian) and a sophisticated à la carte selection. Friendly and attentive service. In summer, the terrace behind the house is very appealing.

Name: Schuppen 13
Description En: The Pusceddu family’s restaurant is located right on the marina and from the outside looks a little like a boathouse. The food within is classic Italian cuisine meticulously prepared using fresh produce. Try the delicious baby squid braised in tomato stock with pan-fried polenta.

Name: Schweizer Wirt
Description En: This place has been synonymous with tasty cuisine for years. The fresh, regional dishes are made with excellent ingredients. Stripped back to the essentials, they eschew any frills. The atmosphere in the restaurant is charming and the waitstaff are friendly. This beautifully situated traditional inn also has a fabulous terrace. You can park directly in front of the building.

Name: RIVA
Description En: The fantastic location by the lake is a draw in itself – a spot on the lovely terrace with a view of the water is of course particularly sought after! But the interior of this bright, elegant restaurant inside the hotel of the same name is also appealing – the floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the lake can be opened up. The seasonal cuisine is predominantly regional, with international influences, Mediterranean or occasionally Asian touches. The menu also features classic dishes. Chic bar and relaxed outdoor lounge.

Name: Le comptoir 17
Description En: The addition of "Bistrot Parisien" to the name tells diners exactly what to expect. If you like a friendly, down-to-earth bistro atmosphere and classic French cuisine, then this is the place for you! Here, the emphasis is on the excellent ingredients that are used to make their house specialities such as blood sausage, beef tartare, mussels or fish soup. As well as the regular menu, there are specials written up on the blackboard.

Name: Schwanen
Description En: Here, the Swabian Jura theme is writ large. The menu changes with the seasons and puts the emphasis on top-quality ingredients, most of which are sourced from the surrounding area. A huge panorama of the Swabian Jura landscape is the most striking feature of the modern yet cosy dining area – it couldn't be more apt. Tip: Given the restaurant's proximity to OUTLETCITY, keen shoppers might consider an overnight stay in one of the hotel's stylish guestrooms.

Name: Lindenhof 1887
Description En: This North German family-run establishment is pretty as a picture! After being welcomed into the attractive inn built in 1887 with a lively local greeting ("moin"), you can expect good, attentive service in a modern and thoroughly chic ambience. Chef Tjark-Peter Maaß cooks tasty dishes of a regional bent. For example, the fried North Sea plaice, fried potatoes, cucumber salad, Tönning shrimps is a tasty and fresh option – one of the classics. There are also some appealing and cosy guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: Rôtisserie Jagdhof Stuben
Description En: The cosy atmosphere and rustic charm of the Rôtisserie at the upscale Jagdhof Glashütte hotel are hard to beat – the warm wood panelling, a roaring fire in the hearth and a decorative old kitchen. And then there is the amiable and attentive front-of-house team, and a menu packed with classics. Excellent recommendations include Wittgenstein venison ragout and Wiener schnitzel made from milk-fed veal.

Name: C'est la vie
Description En: This restaurant is dedicated to the French way of life. As you sit comfortably at your table in the stylish modern interior, looking out through the floor-to-ceiling windows, the dedicated team busy themselves in the open kitchen, cooking up modern interpretations of dishes such as sea bass with root vegetables and potato croissant or Bresse chicken with morels, shimeji mushrooms and vin jaune. The creations are organised into two set menus – one vegetarian, one with meat – and accompanied by exclusively French wine, which are charmingly and skilfully presented at your table with the aid of a map. The wines can also be purchased in the shop. Tip: There is parking in the garage right next door.

Name: Christoph Pauls Restaurant
Description En: No stranger to the Rhineland's restaurant scene, Christoph Paul runs this trendy modern restaurant with his wife Juliane. The striking religious imagery on the wall is a reminder of the site's former vocation as a chapel. A seasonal three- or four-course set menu with a choice of dishes is served. The terrace laid out beneath venerable old trees is delightful. A parking space can be reserved upon request.

Name: Tafelhaus
Description En: The tastefully modern restaurant of Neckartal business hotel is run with dedication. The regional cuisine draws on international influences and is made using top-notch seasonal produce. In addition to the menu, there are also daily specials presented verbally. Owner Bernd Nödinger brings not only professional competence but also a friendly and personal touch to the service. The beverage recommendations are also spot on – thanks to the Coravin system, you can even enjoy high-quality wines by the glass. There is a delightful terrace in summer, and that space gives way to the Tafelhütte event venue in winter. The restaurant is open for lunch on Wednesdays and Thursdays – please book in advance. Reservations for Sundays and Mondays are possible by prior arrangement.

Name: Villa Rothschild Grill & Health
Address: Im Rothschildpark 1, Königstein im Taunus, 61462, Germany
Description En: Located in a park, this smart bankers' villa dating from 1894 is home to a stylish boutique hotel as well as this chic, modern and elegant restaurant. Patrick Bittner, who previously made a name for himself at Frankfurt's Français, where he was head chef for many years, is now at the helm here. The classic cuisine has international influences, and the dishes are served à la carte. Good news for oyster enthusiasts: There are always three varieties to choose from. The modern and elegant interior is tastefully decorated, with a striking open fireplace in the centre of the room serving as the focal point and creating a wonderful atmosphere in winter. In summer, the lovely terrace beckons. Tip: Head to Titian's Bar for a digestif. Lunch is also available on Sundays – ideal for day trippers.

Name: Landgasthof Hirschen
Description En: The dedication of chef Verena Martin and her team is palpable. In a charming setting diners enjoy cordial service and good food that is made primarily with produce from the region and draws inspiration from the seasons. The kitchen staff put their heart and soul into their work – the motto here is ä weng eppis Feins, or "a little something fine" in the local dialect. Tip: "Unser badisches Menü" or "Unser großes Menü" (for two or more people).

The inscription "1906" is still to be seen above the timeworn arch at the entrance of this building in the centre of the old town. Having been completely gutted and meticulously rebuilt, the property now houses an invitingly chic, modern restaurant with large windows and an impressive open kitchen. The sophisticated dishes seamlessly highlight select ingredients with modern accents. Diners are offered a choice of various set menus; individual courses can also be ordered à la carte. Recommendations from the short, well curated wine list are always spot on. There is also a brasserie under the same roof.

Name: Atable im Amtshaus
Description En: Surrounded by the town wall, the Amtshaus hotel boasts a lovely location in Freinsheim's old town, which is well worth a visit. The courtyard with its idyllic terrace leads to this chic restaurant, which is distinguished by its white cross vaults supported by columns. Chef Swen Bultmann cooks classic French dishes made from fine ingredients and inspired by the seasons. Diners can choose between a three- to six-course menu (vegetarian version available) or order à la carte. The food is accompanied by a well-curated and extensive selection of wines. An appealing and reasonably priced set menu is served at lunchtime. There are also tastefully appointed guestrooms – as in the restaurant, the decor harmoniously incorporates modern design into the historical setting.

Name: Café Rapp
Description En: A visit to this delightful village is definitely worthwhile! Originally a bakery and café, this family-run establishment has evolved into a restaurant serving flavoursome, meticulously prepared dishes that take their cue from the changing seasons. As well as à la carte options, there is a choice of set menus. The upscale setting has a classic aesthetic. Attentive service comes courtesy of a well-organised and adept front-of-house team. A must in the afternoon: the delicious freshly baked cakes! Pretty guestrooms.

Name: Hanse Stube
Description En: The exclusive Excelsior Hotel Ernst, right opposite the cathedral, is home to this tasteful and extremely elegant restaurant. With its dark wood panelling, it is an absolute classic, and something of a home from home for Cologne society. Hanse Stube offers ambitious classic cuisine with modern influences, in the form of a four- to six-course menu or à la carte. The special caviar selection is also worth considering. At lunchtime, there is an additional short set menu. Excellent wine list, friendly, proficient service, and a beautiful terrace. The restaurant can be accessed via the hotel entrance.

Name: Ressmann's Residence
Description En: The modern decor, with its sleek design and light, warm tones, is a hit with diners, as are the ambitious, international, seasonal cuisine and fine wines. Tip: At lunchtime, you can put together your own inexpensive three-course menu or simply order à la carte. For those hot summer days, one of the dining rooms is air-conditioned, but if you would rather sit outside, there is a lovely garden terrace tucked away behind the building. Overnight accommodation is also available.

Name: Landgasthof Löwen
Address: Kirchdorfer Straße 8, Kirchdorf an der Iller, 88457, Germany
Description En: Alexander Ruhland represents the fourth generation of his family to run this traditional country inn, and his kitchen turns out top-notch dishes. Two set menus are proposed: a seasonal one comprising three courses and a more ambitious four-course fine dining menu. There is also an à la carte selection featuring classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) with Allgäu beef loin, as well as international dishes and vegetarian options.

Name: Das Obers
Description En: In the smart Gern neighbourhood, a short distance from Nymphenburg Palace, Jürgen Wolfsgruber – known for his restaurants in Schwabing, Sparkling Bistro and Das Tschecherl – has now opened another inviting establishment serving Austrian-inspired cuisine. Diners can either opt for the five-course "Ö-Makase" surprise menu or choose from the small selection of appealing à a la carte options such as Grammelknödel (potato dumplings stuffed with greaves) or soused brown trout. Attentive service comes courtesy of a well-coordinated team of friendly and adept waitstaff, who reliably provide astute wine recommendations. The well-curated wine list includes options by the glass. A laid-back bistro atmosphere reigns inside; outside, there is a lovely terrace.

Name: BECKERS
Description En: The atmosphere in this attractive historical corner-plot building is pleasingly casual. Featuring high ceilings, warm wood panelling, cosy booths and large arched windows, the pretty dining space has the feel of a classic bistro. There is also a bar, and in summer a terrace is set up out front, giving onto the street. The menu includes flavoursome dishes such as oysters, beef tartare, fine fish dishes and premium steaks. Tempting options on the shorter lunch menu include veal meatballs with carrots and mashed potatoes.

Name: die kleine Linde
Description En: This compact restaurant started out in autumn 2024 as a pop-up serving dishes à la carte. Today, it opens its doors in the evenings to present modern and creative cuisine in the form of two five- or seven-course set menus: "Eine Rundreise" and the vegetarian "Botanischer Garten". At the helm in the kitchen, Valentin Thesing (previously at Aqua in Wolfsburg) delivers expressive, harmonious flavour combinations in dishes such as "scallop, water spinach, coconut", complete with robust sauces and stocks. The restaurant is housed in the stately, lovingly renovated Jugendstil building of the Lindenhof. Historical details such as high ceilings and striking pillars, wood panelling, impressive old windows and lovely herringbone hardwood flooring have been tastefully incorporated into sleek, modern interior design. The atmosphere is pleasingly informal, and the service is attentive and professional.

Name: Bardele
Description En: A pleasingly vibrant restaurant and bar reminiscent of a traditional trattoria. In keeping with the Italian spirit, chef-patron Tyler Hanse serves up traditional yet ambitiously executed cucina italiana, with house-made pasta as the main event. The dishes are based on precise craftsmanship, creative expression and flavour – you can lose yourself in delicious dishes (some have a slightly more rustic presentation), eg gnocchi di patate con taleggio. Choose from the à la carte menu or put your trust in the surprise menu. The classic interior, peppered with more modern, designer touches, is appealing. Attentive and polished service.

Name: Feinkost Kantine Mario Pattis
Description En: This appealing concept combining delicatessen, café and bistro is the "little brother", as it were, of Feine Kost. Sharing the same premises, both belong to seasoned chef Mario Pattis. Kantine – open during the day – has a short menu that is supplemented by a handful of daily specials. The recipes stick close to the seasons and to products available in the delicatessen. Thanks to the open kitchen, diners are able to watch as delicious, meticulous dishes that won't break the bank are carefully prepared – the quiche is particularly popular. The service is friendly and down-to-earth. Tip: Choose a nice bottle of wine or something delicious from the extensive delicatessen selection to take home with you. The restaurant is slightly hidden away in a tree-lined courtyard, where tables are set up on the pretty terrace for al fresco dining in summer.

Name: Le petit CINQ
Description En: This is a pleasant alternative to the two-star restaurant Esplanade in the tastefully designed boutique hotel of the same name. Modern cuisine made with seasonal ingredients is served in two three- or four-course set menus; these change on a weekly basis and one is vegetarian. Le petit CINQ takes up residence in the beautiful rooms of the fine dining restaurant when the latter is closed – Sunday to Tuesday, you can eat both lunch and dinner here. David Wottke, long-time sous chef to Esplanade's head chef Silio Del Fabro, is in charge of the kitchen.

Name: Edda Brasserie
Description En: With this tasteful brasserie in the city centre, Alina Meissner-Bebrout offers a delightful alternative to her restaurant bi:braud. The cuisine takes its cue from the changing seasons. In an inviting and laid-back setting, diners can savour the freshly prepared dishes of the day, including classics such as buffalo tartare and Wiener schnitzel. Options are somewhat more limited on Mondays. In summer, the terrace seating overlooking the pedestrianised zone is inviting.

Name: Fachwerk
Description En: This restaurant takes its name from the half-timbered façade of Hotel Stadt Kassel, in which it is housed. Located in the town centre, the building dates back to the 17C. The cosy interior is a harmonious blend of modern design and historical elements such as exposed wooden beams and brickwork. In this setting, contemporary seasonal cuisine is served as a three- to five-course set menu or à la carte. To top it all off, you have a friendly and dedicated front-of-house team, as well as an exceptional wine list comprising over 1 500 labels, including some outstanding Rieslings from Germany.

Name: Ostseelounge
Description En: Housed in Strandhotel Dünenmeer, Ostseelounge has much to offer. In the clean-lined, chic restaurant, floor-to-ceiling windows afford wonderful views of the dunes and the sea – romantic sunsets included! Chef Christopher Huhnstock-Kerber presents a modern, seasonal set menu, showcasing predominantly regional ingredients with his own creative touch. Clearly structured and with refined contrasts, harmonious dishes such as "Alpine pasture-raised lamb, onion, apple" or "fermented whey, fennel pollen, dill" stand out. A three-, five- or seven-course menu is available, also in a vegetarian version. "Midweek Gourmet Special": On Wed and Thu, the various set menu options come at a reduced price. Service is warm and professional under the leadership of the team's sommelier, Bettina Huhnstock-Kerber. Tip: The chef's table right by the open kitchen is well worth considering. There is also a lovely terrace. For an à la carte alternative, the hotel has another restaurant: Kaminlounge.

Name: La Bohème
Description En: A pleasingly convivial and relaxed place to eat. If you appreciate high-quality steak cuts, then this restaurant with a trendy urban atmosphere is just the ticket. But the menu also whets your appetite with a host of other dishes and delicious desserts. The sharing options (vegetarian versions available) will give you a good impression of the cuisine here. Popular brunch on Saturdays and Sundays. Tip for car drivers: Public car park "Schwabinger Tor".

Name: Brasserie Cuvilliés
Description En: Brasserie fare inspired by Bavarian-Alpine cuisine is the order of the day at the restaurant of the Rosewood Munich hotel. Classic, modern and traditional elements come together here. In the evening, dishes such as bouillabaisse or chicken from Landshut with corn, spinach and a pepper foam grace the menu; at lunchtime, tempting options include "Cuvilliés Burger" or quark pizokel. Wiener schnitzel is a mainstay on the menu. The daily-changing lunch menu with a choice of dishes is also worth perusing. The space has a chic brasserie feel and an open kitchen that can be seen from the dining area. Qu'ils mangent de la Brioche by ceramic artist Angelika Maria Stiegler also draws the eye. In addition, there is the inviting Bar Montez, the winter garden for afternoon tea and the Palaishof terrace. The central location, not far from the Feldherrnhalle and opera house, is perfect for a stroll along the exclusive Theatinerstraße.

Name: Vinaiolo
Description En: Vinaiolo has brought a slice of la dolce vita to Haidhausen since opening in 1997. A charming, well-drilled team provides attentive service, with a spirit that is tipicamente italiano. The Italian cuisine includes dishes such as medium-rare veal chop, thinly breadcrumbed alla milanese, served with date tomato salad, crispy potatoes and basil mayonnaise. In the evening, diners can opt for a set menu or à la carte choices. At lunchtime, a tempting, keenly priced set menu is written up on the specials board. The wine list features an appealing selection of Italian wines. The cosy, authentic atmosphere is accentuated by furnishings salvaged from a Trieste grocer's shop dating back to 1904!

Name: Winzerhaus Rebstock
Description En: Following stints at various MICHELIN-starred establishments, Konstantin Keller has taken over this much-loved traditional inn. He is the youngest son of the Keller family, who run Schwarzer Adler across the road. "Down-to-earth, regionally inspired cuisine: the best of the simple things" – that's the promise here, and it could hardly be more apt. Eschewing superfluous creative flourishes, the cuisine is all about quality ingredients, meticulous craftsmanship and full, authentic flavours. In short: The food is just fantastic! This holds true for the exceedingly succulent, classically rolled cordon bleu served with lingonberries and potato salad, as well as the flame-seared Black Forest char with cauliflower and carrot sauce or the pâté de campagne. If steak is more your thing, the dry-aged saddle of Black Forest herb-fed pork is a particular standout. There are also daily specials and a short afternoon menu.
