The wine list features a selection from the family's own estate (Franz Keller) along with other German and international labels. In fine weather, be sure to make the most of the charming courtyard terrace.

Name: Bavarie
Description En: Regionality is a principle that underpins Bavarie, here at BMW Welt. This translates into combining elements of Bavarian and French cuisine with a focus on high-quality produce. You can dine à la carte or take the set menu – there is also a vegan option, plus a three-course business lunch deal. The atmosphere in the spacious, airy, high-ceilinged room is pleasant. Nice terrace with a view of the Olympic Park and Tower.

Name: Martinelli
Description En: If you’re looking for Italian hospitality and the food that goes with it, Martinelli offers seasonal, modern cuisine including dishes such as pecorino ravioli with walnut and balsamic vinegar or saddle of venison with quince. And to whet your appetite, there’s always a plate of air-dried ham and some delicious bread.

Name: Pfistermühle
Description En: Once a ducal mill dating from 1573, Pfistermühle delights diners with its stylish Bavarian setting (including a lovely vaulted ceiling). The "Pfistermühlen Brettl" lunchtime set menu (Mon-Fri) with its four small courses (including vegetarian options) is great value. Good location only a stone's throw from the famous Platzl.

Name: Schwarzreiter Restaurant
Description En: This fine dining restaurant boasts an exclusive location in the famous Maximilianstraße, more precisely within the legendary Munich luxury hotel Vier Jahreszeiten, complete with its own entrance from the street. The atmosphere is elegant without being stuffy; indeed, the sophisticated, modern and chic interior makes for a pleasingly urban ambience. The approachable and well-trained front-of-house team, who are always attentive and courteous but by no means intrusive, is the perfect fit. Then there is the cosmopolitan cuisine of Franz-Josef Unterlechner, who uses top-notch ingredients from the region and beyond. The Balfego tuna cheek, white onion, Alba truffle, for example, showed us how successfully he brings to life his own ideas. A good all-day alternative, should you need one, is the pleasant Tagesbar, where the food is cooked by the same team. Incidentally, the name ‘Schwarzreiter’ comes from a small fish from the Königssee.

Name: Bratwursthäusle
Description En: A trip to Nuremberg wouldn't be complete without trying the city's famous Rostbratwürste! Look no further than this little old stone house on Marktplatz next to Sebalduskirche. Sausages have been sold here since 1312. The interior is rustic and charming, the beechwood barbecue being the centrepiece. Their wonderful sausages are made fresh every morning in their on-site butchery. They are served with sauerkraut and/or potato salad – simply delicious! For the full experience, wash it down with a draught beer. If you're not in the mood for sausages, the menu includes alternatives such as pork shoulder, offal dishes and other snacks. In the summer, the delightful terrace is a popular spot.

Name: Frau Specht
Description En: "Dinner is ready" is the slogan here. You ring the doorbell before being escorted into this somewhat hidden little restaurant with a modern, minimalist decor. You are shown to your table in a pleasantly intimate living room-style interior – with a small open kitchen and just a handful of tables, it makes for a private atmosphere. The service comes with a personal touch: your cordial hostess, Yvonne Specht, after whom the restaurant is named, will also recommend just the right wines from the extensive list of top-draw international labels. In the kitchen, head chef Dirk Brendel cooks up an ambitious seven-course surprise menu in the evening, further embellishing it with a variety of additional small dishes. The menu is devised based on the season and the availability of the ingredients. The cuisine is classic and Mediterranean, but also includes international flavours.

Name: Käfer-Schänke
Description En: The name "Käfer" has become synonymous with Munich's gastronomy scene. The ace up the sleeve of this Munich institution: the restaurant and delicatessen being under one roof means you can be sure that you are dealing with top-drawer ingredients. These are used in classics such as beef tartare, lobster stew or roast duck for two, served in two courses. The atmosphere is cosy, the service professional and friendly. An additional feature is that they have a number of individually designed function rooms available for special occasions.

Name: Pageou
Description En: Located in the CityQuartier Fünf Höfe shopping centre, the chic restaurant of renowned TV chef Ali Güngörmüs is named after his hometown in the Turkish province of Tunceli. Here, his team serves Middle Eastern cuisine that draws on classic French influences and is available as a four-course vegetarian "Levante Menu" and as a five- or six-course "Chef Menu". A starter dubbed "Meze", for example, is a great option comprising various small dishes. A number of noteworthy Turkish labels are included in the extensive wine list. The lovely sheltered terrace is delightful on summer days.

Name: Nymphenburger Hof
Description En: Steeped in tradition, this charming establishment is the epitome of a classic restaurant, both in terms of its decor and cuisine, which draws on regional, Austrian, Mediterranean and French influences. The long-serving chef hails from Styria, which explains why the wine list is exclusively dedicated to Austrian labels. Delightful secluded terrace.

Name: Garden-Restaurant
Description En: With a fabulous light and high-ceilinged industrial-style conservatory by Belgian interior designer and art dealer Axel Vervoord, the restaurant in the luxurious Grand Hotel Bayerischer Hof is exceptionally chic. At the stove, Philipp Pfisterer certainly knows his craft. He and his team cook up classics such as beef tartare, as well as modern dishes such as "fillet of sturgeon from Lombardy with an almond crust & saffron cream" or "grilled flank steak with salsa verde". At lunchtime, the two- or three-course business lunch is a good deal. The very quiet location is also pleasant – and something of a rarity in such a central part of Munich.

Name: Lamm
Description En: For a start, the impeccable façade is inviting, and inside the decor is charming, the service extremely cordial and the food an absolute treat! Choose between the "Bodenständig", "Classic" and "Vegetarian" set menus, in either a three- or four-course format, or order individual courses à la carte – everything is prepared using selected seasonal ingredients. In summer, the delightful garden terrace is a real draw.

Name: Gasthof Widmann
Description En: You can clearly taste the enthusiasm that goes into preparing the food here. Seasonal and international dishes are served alongside regional fare, in a six-course set menu. A friendly front-of-house team presides over the two cosy dining rooms. Wed. - Sat. you are welcome from 6 pm.

Name: Gasthof Ochsen
Description En: This welcoming inn that is run with great dedication has been in the family since it was founded in 1763. This place is really inviting with its charming dining areas, gorgeous terrace and courtyard. Taking its cue from the changing seasons and Baden culinary tradition, the menu includes specialities of the house such as saddle of veal and offal. Comfortable overnight accommodation available.

Name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
Description En: This is MICHELIN-starred chef Tim Raue's take on a French brasserie. The restaurant mirrors the Colette brasseries in Berlin and Munich with an interesting modern dining concept: Diners can order à la carte or compose their own four-course set menu, which can also be vegan. Classics such as beef Wellington (served for two) are available too, as are seasonal dishes. The highlight here is the first-floor terrace overlooking the pedestrian area – but seating is limited, so you'd be well advised to book!

Name: Kurlbaum
Description En: Michael Kurlbaum has run his restaurant with great dedication since 1986. Spread over two floors, this place exudes a timeless elegance – in summer, a few additional tables are set up out front in the pedestrian zone. There are plenty of regulars who come for the classic cuisine. Lunch in the bistro area on the ground floor is popular too – they serve a moderately priced two-course set menu that changes weekly. This includes a bottle of water, and dessert is available as an optional extra. If you order in advance, you can also choose from the evening menu at lunchtime. Convenient for motorists: Kastell car park in Haagstraße close by.

Name: Zur Linde
Description En: The fifth generation is now in charge of this family-run establishment. Sandra and Marco Linden are committed to creating a charming atmosphere and serving good food here. She courteously and competently oversees the service; he cooks up tasty regional and seasonal dishes, which are always modern in inspiration – served as a set menu or À la carte.

Name: Von Korff's
Description En: This patrician house, successfully remodelled and extended, has an appealing feel of modernity with its clean, simple forms and abundant light. Good selection of Bordeaux wines.

Name: Fleur de Sel
Description En: This restaurant in a residential area in Maintal-Dörnigheim brings a slice of France to the Rhine-Main area. You can look forward to experiencing French-Mediterranean flair, both in terms of the feel of the place and Patrick Theumer's seasonally influenced cuisine. The three set menus, one of which is vegetarian, are particularly appealing. Friendly service headed by host Yasemin Theumer. It is also pleasant to dine on the beautifully verdant terrace.

Name: Gutsschenke
Description En: This restaurant's tasteful modern interior design has been beautifully integrated into the historical setting of the 150-year-old Monrepos estate. Outside, there is a delightful terrace under the shade of chestnut trees. The seasonally influenced cuisine is served in the form of a set menu (vegetarian version available) and à la carte. Options include classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) with champagne sauerkraut, as well as modern dishes such as wild garlic risotto with red prawns marinated in rosemary and burrata. Tip: Take a walk through the beautiful park and take in the view of the lake and golf course.

Name: Le Stollberg
Description En: This charming little restaurant is run with a very personal touch by chef-patron Anette Huber. She serves up good-quality, fresh cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons and draws on French and Mediterranean influences. The front-of-house team is friendly and well drilled, providing astute wine recommendations. Tip: The appealing lunch menu is great value for money! Plus light bites are served in the daytime bistro Le Petit Stollberg opposite.

Name: Brasserie Les Deux
Description En: If you like a lively, modern bistro, you’ll enjoy the seasonal, international dishes (such as gnocchi with asparagus and black tiger prawns) served here on the ground floor of Les Deux. Alternatively, try one of the “old” or “new” classics such as mini burgers or beef tartare with imperial caviar.

Name: Im Gütchen
Description En: This elegant modern restaurant is accommodated in a charming Baroque mansion within the historical Schlosspark. In an airy, high-ceilinged space, diners are served classic cuisine with regional and Mediterranean sides, for you to pick à la carte or as a set menu. The proprietor himself runs the kitchen, using good-quality ingredients to cook up tasty dishes, while the lady of the house takes care of diners in a cordial manner. On hot summer days, make a beeline for the marvellous terrace.

Name: Der Löwe
Description En: For years, the Sauters' well-kept establishment has been lauded for its delicious cuisine. Game from the region is one popular choice here, but their dishes with an international spin have also garnered favour with customers. Friendly, attentive service; tasteful setting. Tip: On Wednesday evenings, they serve a four-course surprise menu at an affordable price.

Name: Fegers Grüner Baum
Description En: It is delightful to sit in the shade of the large chestnut tree on the terrace to the rear of this inn, which dates back over 300 years, but the interior is also cosy. Either way, your dedicated hosts are always on hand. They serve Baden cuisine such as Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast) with red cabbage, or pikeperch on a bed of creamed sauerkraut.

Name: Spessarttor
Address: Wombacher Straße 140, Lohr am Main, 97816, Germany
Description En: This long-established family business is a well-run affair, with diners settling into the cosy dining rooms to enjoy regional fare. On the menu, tasty dishes such as roast venison with red cabbage and dumplings will whet your appetite. You can stay overnight in the inn or in the guesthouse located 300m away.

Name: Waldgasthof am Letten
Address: Letten 13, Lauf an der Pegnitz, 91207, Germany
Description En: This restaurant has various dining spaces with a charming rustic feel – including lovely cosy alcoves – where diners tuck into seasonal cuisine that is regional but also draws on international influences. Served by friendly and attentive waitstaff, the food is prepared with fresh, good-quality ingredients. Affording views of the verdant surroundings, the terraces in front and to the rear of the building are delightful in summer. This family-run establishment is also ideal for an overnight stay – on the edge of the forest, yet with good transport connections.

Name: Schaarschmidt's
Description En: This building on a corner plot with a gorgeous leafy façade is home to a cosy restaurant that is run with great dedication. Its many regulars come in droves to enjoy specialities of Saxon cuisine – the beef roulade is a firm favourite! The friendly waitstaff will gladly talk you through the options on the menu. Head for the lovely small terrace planted with trees.

Name: Backmulde
Description En: This is just the sort of restaurant you would like to have in your neighbourhood. At this lovely location in the Old Town, in the cosy atmosphere of a charming centuries-old half-timbered house, you can look forward to great food and select wines and expert recommendations. The ambitious food is rooted in classic French cuisine and courts modern trends. In addition to the seasonal menu, daily specials feature on the blackboard. The service is attentive and seamless – and the presence of the chef brings a personal touch. Tip: Take a look around the wine shop opposite.

Name: EigenArt
Description En: This restaurant is set in a spruce townhouse centrally located close to Marktplatz. It is hardly surprising that there are so many regulars, given the very pleasant atmosphere and friendly service. The cuisine is seasonal and can be enjoyed as a set menu or ordered à la carte. By prior arrangement, you can also make reservations for lunch and at weekends.

Name: Münsters
Description En: This extremely popular place boasts fresh and flavoursome cuisine in the form of a short menu that changes with the seasons. Tables without tablecloths, wooden floorboards and partly exposed brick walls, as well as appealing wine-themed decorative details make for a cosy bistro feel with a rustic touch. The service is laid-back, friendly and attentive. The chef also gets in on the action front of house, providing charming service and excellent wine recommendations. There's also a great beer garden!

Name: Hardthaus
Description En: In this listed building, you are immersed in the charming ambience of what used to be a shop selling goods from the colonies. The floor-to-ceiling dark wooden shelves lining the walls, laden with all manner of decorative items, and the rustic old floorboards are striking. Fuss-free yet flavoursome dishes are served in generous portions at the elegantly set, bare wooden tables. The cuisine embraces international influences, with dishes on the menu such as "creamy spicy" king prawn with pea shoots and mango, or crown of Scottish lamb with a potato and olive oil purée, wild broccoli and a thyme jus. In summer, the terrace on the market square comes into its own. The 600-year-old vaulted cellar is a fantastic venue, especially for private functions. The pretty little boutique hotel opposite boasts lovely guestrooms.

Name: Kitchen Library
Description En: A great team of two, Daniela and Udo Knörlein run this place together - she looks after the guests cordially, while he cooks up the international "Kleine Dinger" set menu. Available with either four or five courses, an eight-course version for sharing is also possible. The characterful decor is reminiscent of a library: rustic-style charm and over 600 collector's items related to cookery.

Name: Piccolo
Description En: You may not see the cathedral here in Porz-Langel, but you do pretty much have front row seats onto the Rhine! This restaurant serves classic cuisine with seasonal and Mediterranean influences, prepared using decent ingredients, most of which are sourced from the region. You can choose à la carte or put together your own three-course menu for a set price. The friendly staff also have plenty of good wine recommendations up their sleeve, drawing on the decent selection with a focus on Austria and Germany.

Name: ACHT
Description En: A trendy, urban establishment in the Spichern Höfe complex on the edge of the Belgian Quarter. Diners sit at wooden tables in a pleasantly unpretentious atmosphere; attentive service provided by charming waitstaff. Flavoursome, down-to-earth dishes based on regional and international ingredients are cooked up in the open kitchen. In summer, the gorgeous courtyard is much sought after.

Name: Hirsch
Description En: This upscale restaurant serves classic cuisine that draws on Baden's culinary tradition and is made predominantly with regional ingredients. Options such as braised veal cheeks or a tasty fish medley in beurre blanc are sure to whet the appetite. Abundant wood and decorative features provide a cosy backdrop. In summer, head for the lovely verdant terrace. Very friendly service. Given the proximity to Strasbourg, the Black Forest and Europa-Park, it is also worth considering staying in one of Hirsch's well-kept guestrooms or apartments.

Name: Schlegelhof
Description En: The charming boutique hotel Schlegelhof boasts not only elegantly appointed rooms, but also culinary excellence courtesy of Marianne and Martin Schlegel. The cuisine is rooted in classic culinary tradition and takes its cue from the seasons. Dishes showcase the finest ingredients, often sourced locally, alongside fruit and herbs from the hotel's own garden. There are various set menus and à la carte options. Classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) and Wiener schnitzel feature, as do more sophisticated numbers such as Atlantic monkfish with beetroot, capers, and potato mousseline. The waitstaff are laid back yet attentive. Decked out in light wood, the interior is sleek and inviting. Floor-to-ceiling windows look out onto the garden and splendid summer terrace.

Name: Zum Riesen
Description En: The Wenz family put their heart and soul into running this place, and quality is also a top priority in the kitchen. Good-quality regional and seasonal ingredients are used to rustle up modern-inspired dishes, which are also served in the form of a set menu. Choose a regional wine to go with your food. In summer, the terrace in the courtyard is a secluded spot. There are lovely individually decorated guestrooms too.

Name: Schloss Loersfeld
Description En: The centuries-old castle with its extensive grounds is a magnificent property, boasting stylish rooms and salons displaying period details behind its massive old walls. This stately backdrop makes for a fabulous setting in which to relish classic cuisine either à la carte or in the form of a three- to six-course set menu. Caviar or oysters are popular appetisers, followed by tempting dishes such as "smoked eel, eel glaze, beetroot, potato, radish" or "lobster tail, mandarin, kumquat, walnut, gin gel, bergamot beurre blanc". Friendly and attentive service. Tip: There is an interesting set menu at lunchtime. In an adjacent building, three pretty apartments accommodate overnight guests.

Name: Zum Ochsen
Description En: It is not without good reason that this 300-year-old restaurant has so many regulars. Here, they honour tradition while managing to keep up with the times – and that goes for both the decor and the food, which is not only beautifully presented but also of the highest quality. The Swabian cuisine follows the seasons and draws on international influences. The emphasis is on regional ingredients, including meat and sausage products made on site in their own butcher's shop. As well as à la carte dishes, a three- or four-course set menu is available.

Name: Poisson
Description En: Top quality products are deliciously prepared at this modern bistro with a fish orientated menu. The chef allows Asian, as well as Mediterranean and classic components to influence his food.

Name: Osteria La Fenice
Description En: A slice of Italy in Cuxhaven! Behind a rather unassuming façade on a busy shopping street, a truly welcoming osteria ambiance awaits – the decor features decorative wine racks, closely spaced marble tables and even a Vespa! Not to forget the authentic Italian cuisine made with high-quality, fresh ingredients – the sourdough bread and pasta are both made in-house. The wine list showcases Italian labels. Tip: Italian food items can be purchased to take home.

Name: LUISE
Description En: The beautiful landscape here is perfectly complemented by the elliptical shape of Luisenhöhe wellness and health resort, which gracefully blends into its surroundings. Inside, too, modern design and high-quality natural materials make for an attractive decor that pays homage to the region – that goes for the guestrooms, the spa and the restaurant. The latter has a pleasantly laid-back feel, and floor-to-ceiling windows look out over the Black Forest and the Schauinsland mountain – only the view from the fabulous terrace can beat it. Prepared in the open kitchen, the four-course vegetarian set menu can be supplemented with a fish or meat dish, or veganised. The emphasis on regional sourcing and top-quality ingredients is demonstrated by compositions such as "sunflower seeds/zucchini/tarragon + pasture-raised chicken from the Black Forest". The excellent wine list features a good selection of German and international labels. The futuristic design of the passage that leads from the multi-storey car park to the hotel is also impressive.

Name: Inzlinger Wasserschloss
Description En: With over 500 years of history to its name, plus a stylish interior, this moated castle near the Swiss border has for years been synonymous with classic French cuisine made from top-notch produce. You can dine à la carte or choose the set menu – there is also a vegetarian or vegan option. Accompany your food with one of the great wine recommendations. Our tip: The guesthouse 150m away has terrific rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Henrich HÖER's Speisezimmer
Description En: The 400-year-old half-timbered house, which houses Hotel Höerhof and this charming restaurant, makes you feel at home. The combination of historical surroundings and modern touches makes for a special atmosphere, to which the warm service provided by the owner also contributes. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace in the secluded courtyard! The excellent cuisine comes à la carte ("Kleine Schlemmerkarte", Tue-Sat), as a seasonal set menu (Tue-Sat) and a fine dining set menu ("Genusswelten", Thu evening-Sat).

Name: Nightingale Thai Cuisine & Bar
Description En: Having spent years in the bustling metropolis of Bangkok, Dominik and May Carqueville are bringing a slice of the Far East to Dachau. Born and raised in Thailand, the chef has an innate talent for working with authentic Thai flavours. She skilfully incorporates contemporary influences and locally-sourced ingredients into the traditional cuisine of her homeland. Using only the freshest ingredients, she crafts dishes such as Ma Hor (caramelised minced pork with peanuts, pineapple, coriander and chilli) or pan-seared sea bass fillet in a choo chee curry sauce with kaffir lime leaves. Dishes can also be ordered to share. The trendy and chic setting is a combination of restaurant and bar – the latter serves cocktails, beer, wine and house-made soft drinks, as well as finger food. The name "Nightingale" is a nod to Bangkok's vibrant nightlife.

Name: Stern's Restaurant
Description En: Housed in the long-established Zum Stern hotel, this restaurant has a charming rustic feel with its wood panelling and lovely white tiled stove. The cuisine is regional but draws on international influences. There are two set menus to choose from (one of which is vegetarian), as well as an à la carte selection including barbecued steaks. The options are a little more limited at lunchtime.

Name: Die Scheuer
Description En: Once known as the Hammelsche Scheune, this 17C barn converted into a pretty half-timbered building has bags of charm. This family business a stone's throw from the market square is run with great dedication, and attracts many regulars. In summer, there is a lovely terrace out front. The interior makes for a cosy setting in which to savour delicious food such as locally hunted game. The restaurant endeavours to source ingredients locally and knows its suppliers personally.

Name: Wirtschaft von Johann Gerner
Description En: The journey out here to the countryside is well worth it, because Detlef Gerner and his wife Tanja live and breathe hospitality par excellence in their cosy restaurant. The hand-written menu features flavoursome dishes based on seasonal and predominantly regional produce – incidentally, they bake their own bread. In summer, you can sit on the terrace out front. Overnight accommodation in the pretty "Häusla" (for two to seven people).

Name: KINK Bar & Restaurant
Description En: This easygoing urban dining concept places equal emphasis on modern cuisine and a vibrant bar culture. The food is pleasingly down to earth yet individual in character – the dishes are ideal for sharing, including as a dedicated sharing menu. This culinary experience is complemented by a standalone bar serving inventive drink creations. The welcoming, informal service matches the stylish, contemporary energy of the space. There is also a lovely terrace. This hip establishment is located at Pfefferberg – once a brewery site, now a cultural venue.

Name: Rutz - Zollhaus
Description En: This restaurant's location on the Landwehrkanal truly lends it something special. In summer you can make the most of the covered terrace but the interior of this former customs house is also appealing, with its tasteful furnishings and relaxed atmosphere. The menu puts a modern spin on classic German fare. Note the selection of high-grade cold meats, to be ordered as a starter or side dish.

Name: Marktwirtschaft Besigheim
Description En: This charmingly laid-back restaurant serves dishes made with regional and seasonal ingredients, drawing on influences from the Mediterranean and beyond. The best way to experience the culinary artistry is through the six-course set menu. There is also a popular lunch deal that changes weekly. In the summer, the terrace on the charming little market square beckons, whether for a meal, a glass of wine or a coffee. The service is friendly and attentive. Across the street is the Marktkeller brasserie and wine bar. They also put on regular themed evenings. Tip: Take a stroll through the enchanting little half-timbered town!

Name: Julius Ernst
Description En: This is not your average, run-of-the-mill restaurant – the concept is relaxed and professional in equal measure. It is, in a sense, the younger sibling of ernst, Dylan Watson-Brawn and Spencer Christenson's restaurant. Its interior is minimalist and sleek, the atmosphere youthful and laid-back. Service, courtesy of an exceptionally friendly international team, runs like clockwork. The kitchen, which is visible behind the counter, sends out creations that blend French and Japanese influences: delicate, refined and intensely flavourful dishes such as "Rose shrimp, nori, yuzu" or "Grilled scallop and Tetsukabuto squash with kale". In addition to the à la carte selection, there is an omakase menu. Breakfast and a small lunch menu are also served at weekends, along with coffee, pastries and snacks throughout the day.

Name: Oktopussy
Description En: At the restaurant of the New Wave hotel, the food is down-to-earth and delicious, and, while it revolves around the region, it also reveals international twists. On the à la carte menu, one dish that reflects the kitchen's characteristically harmonious flavour combinations is "octopus cooked sous-vide, aioli, olives, house-baked bread". There is also a selection specifically for children. The sleek, modern interior with a maritime feel, an open kitchen and a custom-built table for larger groups, is appealing. Service is cordial and laid-back. In summer, make a beeline for the secluded courtyard terrace. From May, the rooftop bar is open for delicious cocktails in a relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Atlantik
Description En: Located in the Dreimühlenviertel, this charming old brick building was a fish market back when it was set amid an abattoir and wholesale butchers. Now it has evolved into this attractive restaurant, which has been designed with an individual touch. Although seafood dominates the menu, it is far from being the only option. Those who prefer meat can indulge in a fillet of beef, to name but one example. Highly recommended for groups: a whole fish to share, eg. turbot, char or Atlantic lobster. Be sure to leave room for dessert – the chocolate cake is a tempting proposition! To accompany your meal, there is an extensive selection of fine wines to choose from.

Name: Nigrum
Description En: An impressive cross vault, elegant dark tones, designer elements, works of art – these former stables overlooking the city and a stone's throw from the New Castle have been stylishly converted. Drawing on modern influences, a three- to eight-course set menu is served – Beef tartare (classically prepared at the table) is available as an optional extra course. There is also a chic bar for an aperitif or digestif. Tip: You can reach the restaurant from the pedestrian area via the Burgstaffeln steps. There are several car parking spaces in front of the restaurant.

Name: ESTIMA by Catalana
Description En: Located in the heart of the Old Town, not far from the cathedral, this tasteful little restaurant prepares Catalan-inspired dishes in an open kitchen. At the helm in the kitchen is Jürgen Birth, who skilfully weaves both Spanish and French elements into his modern set menu. For example, scallops with brandade are followed by his "Hamburgesa 2.0" with Bellota Ibérico pork cheeks. His penchant for patisserie is also evident in the wonderfully refreshing mandarin sorbet pre-dessert. Choose between a conventional and a vegetarian set menu option – a pescetarian variant is also possible. Furthermore, the "Kennenlern-Menü" serves as an introduction to the restaurant's cuisine, as well as the shorter "TAPAS menu". To accompany the food, there are select Spanish wines, which owner Jan-Hendrik Feldner takes pride in presenting – diners are spoiled with attentive, personal service.

Name: ITO
Description En: In this trendy Japanese restaurant in the Belgian Quarter, Kengo Nishimi uses top-notch ingredients to create clearly structured dishes in which traditional Japanese cuisine is laced with modern European influences. In the evening, Japanese classics such as tempura, sashimi and sushi can be ordered à la carte, plus there is an extensive omakase menu. At lunchtime, a moderately priced set menu is available. In the front part of the restaurant, you can watch the chef at work at the sushi counter.

Name: Portomarin
Description En: Red-painted walls and light wooden flooring sets the mood for dishes from the Iberian peninsula. From tapas to dessert, the menu is Spanish.

Name: Diergardts Kühler Grund
Description En: Established in 1904, this family-run restaurant is now in its fourth generation, with Philipp Diergardt now at the helm. He is passionate about cooking up traditional, seasonal cuisine that draws on locally sourced ingredients. The extensive menu is extremely appealing, making it difficult to choose. In addition to the fairly priced set menu ("Heimatmenü"), there are also classics such as bouillabaisse or Wiener schnitzel, as well as weekly specials that change with the seasons and dishes for two or more people. Wine connoisseurs will find plenty to enjoy here, and all reasonably priced. The fine selection of high-end German wines and French vintages is of particular note. Then there is the tasteful country house ambience, gorgeous terrace and attentive service.

Name: Appare
Description En: Here, traditional Japanese food – washoku – is skilfully combined with modern influences, blending Far Eastern spices and cooking methods with European food. There is a short lunch menu and a more elaborate dinner menu. In Japanese "appare" is an exclamation of enthusiasm.

Name: philipps restaurant
Description En: A really appealing restaurant in the Schanzenviertel neighbourhood. A few steps lead down to this lively, modern establishment on the lower ground floor, where friendly and dedicated waitstaff serve fresh international cuisine. Tip: Be sure to make a reservation – this place is small and extremely popular!

Name: Gute Stube im Parkhotel
Description En: The modern and elegant restaurant complete with conservatory and roof terrace is housed in a pretty palace building near Herne's Stadtgarten. The contemporary cuisine takes the form of seasonal set menus and à la carte dishes, including vegetarian options. The chefs try to use regional produce as much as possible. Friendly service. For a simpler alternative in the evening, head to Das Stübchen for classic fare or to the beer garden. Parkhotel offers cosy guestrooms. Tip: Enjoy a short walk through the beautiful Stadtgarten. A longer route takes you to the debris field of the (closed) Mont Cenis colliery – right next to it is the viewing platform at the Mont Cenis Academy, which affords fantastic views.

Name: Clouds - Heaven's Bar & Kitchen
Description En: Just 50 seconds in the lift and you are up on the 23rd floor, from which the view is simply magnificent. Modern cuisine is served in an urban-style interior: enquire about the extensive selection of meats; vegetarians are also catered for. In addition, there's a good bar serving a snack menu from 5pm. In summer, weather permitting, head to the 24th-floor Heaven's Nest for drinks and light bites.

Name: Die Alte Schule
Description En: Torben Tönsing, scion of a well-known family of restaurateurs in Herford, took over this restaurant from his parents in 2017. He focuses on contemporary cuisine that draws on both regional and international influences. The 17C half-timbered building has a charming atmosphere – food is served on different levels, and in summer the secluded terrace comes into its own. Excellent wine selection – they even have their own wine shop.

Name: Belvedere
Description En: The culinary flagship of the A-ROSA Strandidyll Heringsdorf hotel. From your table in the fourth-floor dining area, which with its glass dome has an elegant modern feel , you can take in the wonderful view over the hotel grounds all the way to the Baltic Sea. The cuisine is classic in its foundations and partly based on regional produce. You are free to put together your own set menu. Friendly and well-drilled waitstaff. Tip: Your aperitif is best enjoyed on the gorgeous terrace.

Name: Papageno
Description En: Even after moving to the centre of Konstanz, Patrick Stier has remained true to his style. He serves up classic cuisine with Mediterranean influences – think sea bass grenobloise with artichokes and a saffron emulsion or saddle of venison with a sour cherry game jus, warm pointed cabbage salad, port wine cherries, macadamia nuts and Topfenknödel (curd dumplings). Diners can choose between the "Gourmet" and "Vegetarian Gourmet" set menus and à la carte dishes.

Name: Clinton's
Description En: Near the outskirts of Berlin, this restaurant is housed on the first floor of the European headquarters of the fashion company Clinton. The decor is up to the minute, as is the seasonally influenced cuisine – choose between a four- or six-course set menu and their à la carte "Signature" dishes, from "Berlin Blutwurst, sauerkraut, green back bacon, cassis, mustard" to "300g beef – roast beef, fillet, 16hr-cooked ox shoulder, truffle purée, teriyaki, vegetables from the farm". Fans of dry-aged steaks are also in for a treat. The service is attentive and the waitstaff professional. From some tables you can sneak a peek into the Clinton outlet.

Name: Fleher Hof
Description En: A little out of the way, this traditional restaurant has a cosy interior, with all the charm of wood-panelled walls, old floorboards and wooden tables. Then there is the tasty cuisine, which includes flavoursome classics with a modern touch. Choose from the à la carte selection, or opt for one of the set menus ("Hof Menü", "Bistro Menü" or vegetarian). This pleasant restaurant is popular, so be sure to book in good time! N.B. Although finding a parking space may not be easy, it's definitely worth coming.

Name: Kuro Mori
Description En: Kuro Mori is Japanese for"black forest", neatly capturing the "Black Forest meets Asia" concept here. In an open kitchen, modern dishes are conjured up from high-quality ingredients . Tempting examples include sea bass kinilaw with calamansi, carrot, tamarind and coconut, and veal – saddle and gyoza – with cauliflower, coriander, and pommes dauphine. The stylish urban setting is pleasingly laid-back, with striking details such as exposed brick walls and a cobblestone floor; the high ceilings towards the rear are especially impressive. The location in Freiburg's Old Town, with terrace seating along the pedestrian area in summer, is another plus.

Name: Das Bootshaus
Description En: The restaurant at lifestyle hotel Papa Rhein sports a tasteful vintage maritime look and serves good food made with the freshest ingredients. Each evening, a new three-course set menu is presented, in a vegetarian or omnivore version – the latter with options. Lunch is à la carte. The front-of-house team pulls out all the stops but keeps things informal. There is a wonderful view of the Rhine and the surrounding vineyards – in summer, the delightful terrace beckons! In the bar, sand underfoot brings that beach feeling indoors.

Name: mural
Description En: The location is special in its own right: This restaurant is tucked away inside MUCA (Museum of Urban and Contemporary Art), and this is the inspiration behind the interior design. The open kitchen allows you to watch the chefs prepare their modern and creative four-course set menu – available with meat and fish or in a vegetarian version. Sourced within the region, the ingredients are of outstanding quality. The high-end wine list is wide-ranging and features some excellent natural wines, too. There are also wine or alcohol-free pairings to go with the set menu. Service is friendly and personable. The restaurant is also open for lunch – dishes can be ordered à la carte or as a set menu comprising two to four courses.

Name: Fine Dining by Phillip Probst
Description En: Located in The Liberty hotel, this is a tastefully modern fine dining restaurant with floor-to-ceiling windows that afford a view of the small harbour. There is also a gorgeous terrace. Chef Phillip Probst and his team use excellent ingredients to create an interesting set menu comprising four to eight courses. The dishes are contemporary, yet classical in their foundations, and the wonderfully intense sauces deserve a mention. Shining examples are the cauliflower polonaise (served with an exquisite beurre blanc enhanced with Imperial caviar) and the beetroot with barbecued eel. The fairly priced wine list is another highlight. The well-drilled front-of-house team are friendly and attentive – they really pull out all the stops! Part of the same business, the restaurant next door, Mulberry Street, proposes a short menu of contemporary dishes.

Name: DAS GOLDSTEIN BY GOLLNER'S
Description En: It's quite unexpected to come across such a chic restaurant in a remote wooded area like this. But the journey is absolutely worth making. Set in the former rifle club house about 5km from the city centre, this establishment boasts a tastefully sleek and upscale interior. It serves freshly prepared, predominantly Austrian cuisine, but the menu also features international dishes, some with Asian influences. The walk-in wine cellar and extensive wine list are a draw in themselves.

Name: The Sakai
Address: Hedderichstraße 69, Frankfurt on the Main, 60596, Germany
Description En: With Hiroshi Sakai at the helm here, you're in the hands of a real sushi master. This basement restaurant is done out in authentic Japanese style: sleek and minimalist. From the seats at the counter, you can watch the food being prepared. They serve an omakase menu, which also comes in a vegan version. The service comes courtesy of a very friendly and professional front-of-house team. Great sake selection.

Name: Funky Fisch
Description En: Are you in the mood for fish of the uncomplicated and Asian-inspired variety? Then head to the trendy and lively Funky Fisch by The Duc Ngo. The centrepiece is the large fish counter, where you choose the fish you want to eat, which is then prepared in the open kitchen. A wide range of Asian food, from Chinese to Vietnamese, is served, with influences from all over the world.

Name: HEIMAT
Description En: Restaurant HEIMAT, Auerhahn Stuben, Bayern Stuben and Tiroler Stuben – the elegant hotel of the same name, which also has a spa, offers diners a variety of restaurant option, all of which are elegant and inviting. The terrace, in particular, with its panoramic mountain view is quite an event – it's a great place to soak up the idyllic surroundings! The cuisine is seasonal and regional; the majority of the ingredients come from within an 80km radius. The menu also features classics such as Wiener schnitzel or chateaubriand for two.

Name: Pure Wine & Food
Description En: The atmosphere here is pleasingly laid-back and trendy – in summer, the lovely terrace in front of the building gives you that holiday feeling. Using the freshest ingredients, the kitchen team serves up pared-back, modern Mediterranean cuisine. Diners choose between the "Chef's Choice" set menu, a vegetarian set menu and à la carte dishes. Given the restaurant's name, it is no surprise that wine plays an important role. The friendly and adept waitstaff will gladly recommend a suitable pairing for any dish. The terrific wine list comprises over 250 (organic) labels – also available to take away. Tip: Book a wine tasting.

Name: Bootshaus Bar & Grill
Description En: Bootshaus is located in the heart of Hamburg's HafenCity. From the comfortable "Boot" (boat) dining area, watch the action in the open kitchen or look out over the marina (Grasbrookhafen) from the light and airy bar area. In summer the waterfront terrace beckons. The Josper grill takes centre stage, with cuts such as New York strip, rib-eye and porterhouse cooked to perfection! There is also a large selection of side dishes and delicious sauces. Keep an eye out for the seafood specials and the "Chef's Choice" deal. The early opening times (from 5.30pm) make this an ideal spot for dinner before a concert at the nearby Elbphilharmonie – or perhaps a drink at the bar afterwards.

Name: POTS
Description En: Relaxed, chic and stylish! The eye-catching features of the Ritz-Carlton's restaurant are its striking decor and large open kitchen. The chefs put a modern spin on traditional German cuisine in dishes such as Königsberger Klopse (meatballs in a white wine sauce) with capers and yellow beetroot. There are also options for sharing. Alternatively, take a punt on the surprise menu. The lunch deal is also popular. Friendly and adept service.

Name: esskunst
Description En: The former hall of a bank is now a smart and sophisticated restaurant serving ambitious cuisine. Here, culinary tradition is tastefully combined with modern trends. On the menu, for example: char fillet, strudel dough, celery, turnips, kohlrabi. Tip: try the home-made pralines with your coffee. Charming, attentive and experienced service.

Name: Kaltwassers Wohnzimmer
Description En: It is little wonder this restaurant remains so popular. The cosy setting has a "living room" feel, enhanced by charming nostalgic touches that lend the space character. The service is attentive and friendly. The cuisine is modern and ingredient-led… Diners are presented with a "market basket" of the day's featured produce, which forms the basis of a surprise set menu available in three to six courses. For those who prefer to dine al fresco, the Atrium in the inner courtyard is an appealing option with its views into the glass-fronted kitchen.

Name: Terra
Description En: This restaurant in the attractive Ritz-Carlton hotel boasts a bright and elegantly modern interior with captivating views of the VW works and the harbour basin afforded by floor-to-ceiling windows. The cuisine takes its cue from the seasons and showcases quality produce from the region and elsewhere in the country. One of their signature dishes is braised veal cheek with mustard jus. Good vegetarian options.

Name: Lucente
Description En: If you are hungry for good Italian-Mediterranean cuisine in Rüttenscheid, then this ristorante is the place for you. On the menu, dishes such as "venison tonnato" or monkfish saltimbocca with ratatouille whet the appetite; in addition, daily specials are announced by waitstaff. The atmosphere is young, fresh, friendly – a sense of Italian joie de vivre is in the air here!

Name: Saxlers Restaurant
Description En: This restaurant is housed in the inviting Weinhotel St. Stephanus on the riverside promenade and not far from the old market square. In a refined setting, the friendly and committed hosts serve delicious food made with top-notch ingredients, vegetarian options included. The menu features classic dishes and regional specialities. Tip: Leave room for the delicious desserts! In the basement, the Braukeller serves Kloster Machern beer.

Name: Schimmel's
Description En: This restaurant's striking red façade draws the eye. The smart interior is modern and stylish, and the atmosphere is welcoming – the wooden tables are a nice touch. In the open kitchen, regional dishes are prepared, occasionally incorporating influences from around the globe. Diners can choose between the two set menus or order à la carte. The soups, for example, are delicious, but so is the fresh fish! The proprietress ensures cordial and attentive service. They also offer pretty guestrooms and holiday flats.

Name: ESSLIBRIS
Description En: ESSLIBRIS offers a relaxed, elegant atmosphere with a fine view of the garden. The food on offer is a mix of Mediterranean and regional. Try the suckling calf fillet and ravioli with carrots, parsley root and shallots. The kitchen is pleased to meet personal requests.

Name: Kaisers Eck
Description En: Right next to Ahlbeck's main church, this cosy restaurant has a charming and down-to-earth atmosphere. The proprietress manages the service with warmth, ease and expertise, while her husband takes care of the cooking. The cuisine is predominantly regional. Both of the three- to five-course menus (one of them vegetarian) and the à la carte options are popular – the decision won't be easy. If you wish to stay on, two holiday apartments are available.

Name: AnnA
Description En: This restaurant inside the luxury Hotel Elephant is bathed in natural light thanks to its enormous windows. Seated beneath the high ceiling, diners can take in the exclusive ambience, including decorative pictures in the entrance area. Head for the delightful terrace in summer. The cuisine is modern and creative with a regional twist. Mouthwatering options include cod and creamy leeks with pasta and tomato and, for dessert, apple and white chocolate bread pudding and vanilla ice cream. At lunchtime, diners can order à la carte. In the evenings, an interesting set menu is also available, which also comes in a vegetarian version. Be sure to take a stroll through the attractive old town.

Name: Schloss Monaise
Description En: With Hubert Scheid's cuisine, this place is nothing short of a culinary institution in the region. His signature style comprises pleasantly straightforward dishes made from excellent ingredients – served à la carte or as a set menu. The restaurant occupies stylish, high-ceilinged rooms that channel the stately flair of these premises dating back to 1783 – once a summer residence. Or you can dine on the wonderful terrace with a view of the surrounding nature and the Moselle. It's also worth taking a look at the wine list, which features many a big name.

Name: Schranners Waldhorn
Description En: Maximilian and Marie-Luise Schranner's establishment is a haven of comfort and calm. They have lovingly transformed this traditional inn with a tasteful interior design concept. At the helm, Maximilian Schranner specialises in classic cuisine and proposes three set menus: the "Menü Gourmet", the "Menü vegetarisch" and the "Wirthaus-Menü" – but you can also order dishes from these à la carte. There is also a very reasonably priced set menu at lunchtime. On warm days, the gorgeous terrace on the Seebach with its views of the castle is a particular highlight.

Name: Salt & Silver
Description En: "Wanderlust cuisine" is the theme at this St Pauli restaurant with views of the Elbe. Diners choose from a regularly changing à la carte menu that features dishes that draw on seasonal and regional ingredients, Mediterranean influences and international twists. Examples include "shiitake wonton, enoki, dashi, Szechuan oil" or "butterflied Arctic char, salsa verde, new potatoes". There is also a surprise menu for sharing and a carefully curated wine list. The pleasingly relaxed atmosphere is enhanced by polished and highly professional service, which is provided by a cheerfully charming and laid-back front-of-house team.

Name: Landhaus Halferschenke
Description En: In this beautiful quarry-stone building dating from 1832, the Schmah family serve ambitious cuisine that revolves around top-notch ingredients and the seasons – from sole and Aubrac beef to oysters and turbot from Brittany. You can opt to dine à la carte or go for a set menu. In addition to the food, diners can look forward to attentive service in a tasteful setting with a country-house feel. In summer, the gorgeous terrace beckons. In addition, MA PETITE CHAMBRE is a small gourmet haven serving a set menu. They have four well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Genussschmiede
Description En: This blacksmith's shop dating back to 1682 is now devoted to modern cuisine that follows the seasons and draws on fresh, mainly regional ingredients. The interior is pleasingly trendy and minimalist, with a dining area laid out beneath a high steel ceiling. Diners choose between a 5-course set menu and à la carte dishes. Vegetarians are also well catered for on the menu.

Name: Hohenhaus Grill
Description En: This is the second restaurant of the idyllically situated Hohenhaus hotel, a magnificent property steeped in history. The interior has a classic, rustic decor and a warm atmosphere – plus a lovely 18C tiled stove. The seasonal cuisine is based on premium ingredients, sourced from the region for the most part. Delicious options include barbecued wild game sausage made with meat hunted on site and served with Hohenhaus potato mash, or braised local mutton. It is a treat to sit on the terrace and take in the surrounding countryside.

Name: Chambao
Description En: This appealing restaurant is all about sharing. Good-quality ingredients go into imaginative dishes that you can combine as you see fit to create your own set menu. Another lovely idea is the "Heidelberg Menü": a culinary guided tour of the city, available in either a classic or vegetarian version. Some tables afford a view into the glass-fronted kitchen. The staff are friendly and professional, and you can trust the wine recommendations without hesitation. Chambino bar and bistro is located almost opposite. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous, lively terrace overlooking the Alte Brücke (Old Bridge).

Name: Hofgut Hohenkarpfen
Description En: This restaurant enjoys a wonderful location in the middle Baden-Württemberg's oldest nature reserve and boasts stunning views – it's well worth booking a table on the terrace. In what was once the dairy of the over 300-year-old farmstead, diners are pampered with delicious food and attentive service. The modern cuisine incorporates classic and regional influences, as well as international, sometimes Asian touches. The former barn of the heritage-protected estate has been transformed into a hotel with attractive and cosy minimalist-style guestrooms. Tip: Take the time to look around the art museum.

Name: Sansibar
Description En: A restaurant with cult status! This smart beach cabin is a much sought-after place to eat. It takes five minutes to reach it on foot through the dunes – or you can use the shuttle service. Fancy a Sansibar classic such as rice pudding with red fruit jelly? Or perhaps you'd prefer something more sophisticated? Superb wine list. No reservations taken at lunchtime. There is a playground for children next to the restaurant.

Name: Zur Schlupp
Description En: Isabelle and Michael Ehrhardt devote themselves with great enthusiasm to running their charming little restaurant in this house dating from 1608. The atmosphere is cosy and casual, with the building's original character beautifully preserved and enhanced by tasteful modern touches. The chef-patron's cooking is defined by freshness and seasonality – there are two set menus (one vegetarian) that change on a monthly basis as well as à la carte dishes. The hostess provides attentive service and recommends good wines, with the Rheingau Riesling selection being a highlight. Don't forget to book. Tip: The courtyard is a romantic spot in summer!

Name: Gocklwirt
Description En: What is it that draws regulars and day trippers here in equal numbers? The richly decorated space is wonderfully rustic and the remarkable collection of farm machinery is well worth seeing. Classic international and regional dishes such as Böfflamott (beef in red wine), rooster burger and saddle of lamb in a herb crust are served, as well as a seasonal set menu. Three individually decorated double rooms can be booked for overnight stays in the building next door.

Name: Gengs Linde
Description En: Christian Geng offers fresh and flavoursome cuisine that is traditional with international influences. His fashionable restaurant combines clean, modern lines with warm wood. Try the veal cordon bleu or the rack of lamb baked in a herb crust with peperonata and homemade gnocchi.

Name: Klebers
Description En: Whether you are seated in the pleasantly bright interior or on the delightful terrace in summer, you can look forward to friendly and charming service as well as international and regional cuisine made from excellent produce. There are various set menus (including a vegetarian one) to choose from, plus a selection of dishes à la carte. The restaurant is housed in the tasteful Kleber Post hotel.

Name: Gasthof Schütte
Description En: This region, which is a popular destination for hiking and cycling enthusiasts, is home to this traditional family-run country hotel with its own spa facilities and lovely restaurant. The regional, classic and international dishes can be sampled as part of a set menu or à la carte – examples include Sauerland red deer ragout, and skrei fillet with a tarragon and mustard sauce. At lunchtime, the menu is more streamlined and supplemented by nibbles and snack options. In the afternoon, choose from a selection of cakes, and in winter, an open fireplace in the charming restaurant adds to the atmosphere.

Name: Zum Ochsen
Description En: The atmosphere is really cosy in this restaurant, which is charmingly done out in the traditional style typical of the region. The kitchen serves up flavoursome, ambitious dishes with a regional and seasonal focus, as well as the occasional international twist. For overnight guests, this long-standing family-run establishment offers comfortable guestrooms and a spa with a range of facilities and treatments and a swimming pool.

Name: Gourmetrestaurant "1751"
Description En: Located in the heart of the city, in a wine merchant's house dating back over 250 years, this restaurant is considered one of the finest in the region. This delightful historical setting boasts a beautifully restored barrel vault ceiling, and the wonderful atmosphere is further enhanced by live piano music at weekends. The team led by chef Marcel Kube serves up modern cuisine, drawing on seasonal influences and using mostly regional ingredients. The ambitious plant-forward set menu also includes one fish and one meat option. Choose between the five- or seven-course format; it is possible to add an extra course. The wine list features some rare gems! Weinhaus Uhle hotel has tastefully designed guestrooms. Incidentally, the property has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2024.

Name: Gutshaus Kubbelkow
Description En: With its smart façade and stylish dining rooms, this listed manor house set in wonderfully peaceful grounds has lost nothing of its 1908 charm. It serves fresh, ambitious cuisine including lagoon-fished zander with jellied bouillabaisse broth and pan-fried asparagus. The idyllic location makes the tasteful upmarket guestrooms dotted with antique furniture all the more inviting, as does the excellent breakfast.

Name: Restaurant Quack in der Villa Weismüller
Description En: It's a treat to sit either out on the terrace overlooking the city or inside – in a tastefully decorated dining area blending elegance and trendy chic styling. The ambitious seasonal cuisine has distinct Mediterranean and regional influences. Various set menus feature dishes such as corn-fed Bresse chicken cooked with truffles and served with kohlrabi, chicory and gnocchi or Breton turbot, mashed potatoes with artichokes and baby spinach. The Chef's Table is an interesting affair: counter seating with a view into the kitchen, and a surprise menu. Good wine list. Comfortable apartments are available for a stylish stay. N.B. The property is accessed via a narrow private road.

Name: Lazarus Stube im Oberschwäbischen Hof
Description En: Do you fancy some really tasty seasonal regional cuisine, including classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) or house-made Maultaschen (Swabian dumplings)? Here at Lazarus Stube, good, fresh, often locally sourced ingredients go into appealing à la carte dishes and specials that change with the seasons. Friendly, attentive service. For more ambitious cooking, look to the tasting menu (vegetarian or omnivore) of the second restaurant, Esszimmer. The excellent, wide-ranging selection of wines is the same in both establishments. Modern and functional guestrooms available next door at Oberschwäbischer Hof.

Name: east
Description En: This restaurant, housed in the stylish hotel of the same name, is quite striking on account of the fantastic industrial architecture of the former iron foundry and the slick, chic interior. The centrepiece here in what was once the factory hall is the sushi counter. The menu features modern international dishes. A tip for meat lovers: fine steaks from the Southbend Grill.

Name: Grenzhof
Description En: At Grenzhof, chef Sebastian Andrée and his team are strongly influenced by the seasons and their produce in their modern cuisine, which is served as a three to six-course menu and an appealing à la carte selection. In nice weather, the Kastanienhof is absolutely idyllic; on less clement days and in winter, the Gutsstube with its rural-style decor is welcoming. At lunchtime, options are limited to a lunch buffet and a short lunch menu. They also rent out various spaces for private events. For overnight stays, they propose attractive and inviting country house-style and themed guestrooms.

Name: Landhotel Krone
Description En: Here, tradition rubs shoulders with current trends in cosy little spaces that feature an attractive blend of old brickwork, wood, steel and glass. The regional and seasonal cuisine is scattered with international influences. Medieval vaulted cellar for events. This family-run business also offers attractive, individually designed guestrooms and wellness facilities.

Name: Bayerischer Hof
Description En: In this well-kept restaurant run by the Leykauf family, you can expect a relaxed atmosphere and flavoursome, fresh cuisine prepared by the chef-patron, as well as friendly and attentive service overseen by the lady of the house – this is hospitality as it should be! The wine list predominantly features local produce. There are also reasonably priced guestrooms, varying in style from simple to modern.

Name: Weisser Bock
Description En: Pretty details such as wood panelling and historical photos contribute to the cosy atmosphere in this traditional establishment. The kitchen serves up a fine selection of dishes made from regional and international ingredients, from which you can choose a three- to six-course menu. The à la carte menu includes appetising dishes such as "beef tartare, anchovies, brioche, caviar" and "turbot, wild cauliflower, capers". The hotel of the same name has comfortable and tastefully decorated guestrooms. The central location is another trump card.

Name: Rehbergers im Schloss Hohenstein
Description En: This stunning castle, which is mentioned in written records as early as the 14C, boasts an idyllic location in beautiful grounds. In addition to their tastefully decorated hotel, Alexandra and Andreas Rehberger run this appealing restaurant with a winter garden overlooking the castle courtyard. The chef-patron – no stranger to the restaurant scene – turns his hand to cooking contemporary seasonal cuisine with ingredients from the region; the proprietress delivers Austrian charm and good wine recommendations.

Name: Die Kurfürstenstube
Description En: A classic of Heidelberg's dining scene! In the restaurant of the stylish grand hotel Der Europäische Hof Heidelberg, with its individually designed guestrooms and suites, the mighty coffered ceiling and wall panelling with beautiful inlays preserve a piece of history. The cuisine is based on the classics, and only the very best ingredients are used in the ambitious dishes. Choose à la carte or go for the set menu, available in various lengths. The wine list, specialising in German, French and Italian labels, is also excellent. The highly friendly, professional and attentive service is in keeping with the style of the place. In the summer months, a slightly simpler menu is served in the "Sommerrestaurant", which has a terrace and a pleasant, airy atmosphere.

Name: Magnifico da Umberto
Description En: Umberto Scuccia is a well-known figure in Heilbronn. Here on the 12th floor of the WTZ Tower he runs an upmarket, minimalist-style restaurant offering both pleasantly pared-down Italian cuisine with the accent on top-quality produce and a wonderful view of the city.

Name: Bachmaier
Description En: Ulrike and Otto Bachmaier have been running their restaurant for many years. The modern decor is delightful and you can watch the river traffic on the Neckar through the floor-to-ceiling windows, as well as from the terrace. Friendly and adept service comes courtesy of the lady of the house while the chef-patron delivers seasonal dishes such as Obsiblue prawn soup with ginger, or braised shoulder of locally hunted venison, glazed in the pan, with Swede, palm tree kale and celeriac. A vegetarian set menu is available by prior arrangement. Good wine pairings. Tip: Book well in advance.

Name: 20zwanzig
Description En: Nestled in a quiet location on the outskirts of town, Hotel Freiwerk's core building is a spruce half-timbered villa dating back to 1894. Its restaurant, 20zwanzig, is housed in the modern extension built in 2020. The chic, trendy interior has large floor-to-ceiling windows that affords a splendid view of the surrounding greenery. The cooking is contemporary and seasonally inspired. Classics on the menu include Oldenburg duck and locally hunted game. Diners can opt for a surprise menu of flexible length or order à la carte. Friendly and professional waitstaff.

Name: Intuu
Description En: Ensconced in the Freigeist hotel is this appealingly modern and lively restaurant. Diners have the option of sitting at the counter with views of the action in the open kitchen, as the team prepares a broad offering of Japanese and South American cuisine: dishes range from sushi and sashimi, tempura and yakitori to meats grilled in the Josper oven. These are also perfect plates for sharing.

Name: Chang Bistro
Description En: This smart and trendy bistro version of the main restaurant, Chang, in Grünwald features mostly Thai cuisine and dishes with influences from Japan. Here, too, the emphasis is on high-quality ingredients. The Thai curries as well as the sushi can be highly recommended. At lunchtime there is also a daily changing lunch menu. Lovely terrace, as well as covered winter garden-style dining space.

Name: Rubens
Description En: This pretty restaurant owned by friendly hosts Cornelia Stolzer and Ruben Baumgart – she is Austrian and he is German-Austrian – is something of an Alpine hot spot. Accordingly, classics such as Backhendl (breaded fried chicken), Alt-Wiener Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) or Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake), as well as modern dishes feature on the menu. Charming, well-trained waitstaff and a decent selection of Austrian wines. Incidentally, the pumpkin seed oil comes from the proprietress's village.

Name: Wintergarten
Description En: The tastefully designed conservatory restaurant of the long-established Brenners Park-Hotel & Spa is a light and airy space with floor-to-ceiling glazing that affords a splendid view of the leafy gardens – and the terrace is, of course, especially inviting. In the evening, the classic and seasonal dishes can be enjoyed as a set menu or ordered à la carte. Vegetarian options are also available. A three-course set menu is served at lunchtime from Monday to Friday.

Name: Puricelli
Description En: The location in the old castle ruins is glorious, and the view of the Rhine is spectacular – best enjoyed from the terrace. Inside, floor-to-ceiling windows frame the scenery beautifully. The kitchen takes its cue from the changing seasons and region, showcasing produce such as organic veal and venison from Oberheimbach, salmon trout from the Wisper Valley, zander from Lake Laach and vegetables and herbs from the castle's own garden. Alongside an excellent à la carte selection, there’s a choice of two set menus – one larger, one smaller. The wine list highlights local estates, including the castle’s own wine from its surrounding slopes. Burg Reichenstein hotel offers attractive, individually decorated guestrooms. Tip: Regular events are held here. A visit to the castle museum is definitely worthwhile.

Name: Staudi's
Description En: Once a butcher's, now a really pretty little restaurant with a bistro feel. Decorative relics of the past such as tiled floors and stained glass in the ceiling make for a charming interior. Diners also enjoy cordial service and modern, seasonal dishes, served in the form of a four-, five-, or six-course tasting menu. A vegetarian alternative is available, too. In good weather, you can make the most of the lovely terrace laid out in front of the restaurant. The Stube can be booked as a separate room for private events (Nov-Mar).

Name: Restaurant 1463
Description En: This building, dating from 1463, exudes rustic charm both inside and out. Dark wood finishings and low ceilings add to the cosy feel of the two small dining spaces on the first floor. The secluded terrace in the quiet courtyard is also delightful. Verena and Henning Weick, your cordial hosts, run the establishment as a team – she handles service, he is in charge of the kitchen. Diners can choose between two set menus (with optional wine pairings), and each course can also be found in the tempting à la carte selection. There are six lovely comfortable apartments for overnight stays.

Name: Überland
Description En: In less than a minute, the lift takes you up to the 18th floor of the BraWoPark building near Hauptbahnhof. People come here to enjoy modern cuisine in a trendy, chic setting – not to mention the view. Try the choice cuts of the excellent beef aged in-house. Incidentally, the concept is the brainchild of TV chef and food professional Tim Mälzer. NB: two sittings per evening. On the floor above, rooftop bar and terrace.

Name: Jan Diekjobst Restaurant
Description En: Dating from the 16C, Detmolder Hof not only offers comfortable classical accommodation, but it is also home to Jan Diekjobst's restaurant, which is worth seeking out in its own right. After stints at Victor's FINE DINING by Christian Bau in Perl-Nennig and The Table Kevin Fehling in Hamburg (and others), here the chef cooks up a modern take on classic cuisine. The dishes, prepared with carefully selected ingredients, are available as a three-, five-, or seven-course set menu; the vegetarian version has three or five courses. À la carte dining is also possible. From Thu to Sat, there is also a "Gourmet Lunch". Service is very friendly and attentive. The interior is done out in a tasteful brasserie style, with high ceilings, a striking chandelier and handsome hardwood floors, as well as an open kitchen. In summer, the terrace in front of the building beckons.

Name: Eiden Restaurant
Description En: Set in 10ha of parkland, Jagdhaus Eiden enjoys a wonderful location. The restaurant of the long-established hotel run by the Zur Brügge family specialises in modern cuisine with international influences. The menu is varied, making generous use of regional ingredients such as lake fish, game and vegetables. Diners are seated in a number of handsomely decorated rooms, including the bright, airy conservatory overlooking the lake. The gorgeous garden terrace is equally inviting. Tip: Combine your meal with a trip to the in-house casino.

Name: Gänsweid
Description En: In this carefully restored former garage, it is a case of ‘olive oil not engine oil’! Enjoy your meal in a relaxed atmosphere where you can watch the cooks preparing their fresh mixture of Swabian and Mediterranean dishes in the kitchen. Simple, good value menu only at lunchtimes.

Name: Berghotel Wiedener Eck
Description En: Marie and Lorenz Wissler represent the fourth generation of their family to run Berghotel Wiedener Eck, which enjoys an idyllic location at over 1 000m above sea level – the view of the valley is stunning! For overnight stays, there are attractive, cosy guestrooms, and the restaurant is brimming with traditional Black Forest charm, interspersed with modern touches. In the restaurant, you can look forward to friendly and courteous service, as well as regional cuisine and dishes that draw on the culinary traditions of France and the Mediterranean, all made from fresh high-quality ingredients – the chef even hunts his own game. In the evenings, there is a set menu that changes every day, plus the seasonal "Wiedener Eck Menü". You can also order the individual courses of both à la carte. Tip: The surrounding forests and meadows make this hotel a perfect starting point for hikes!

Name: CARALEON
Description En: This tastefully designed restaurant is housed in the small boutique hotel of the same name, which enjoys a fabulous location in the Wasserburger Bucht and boasts stunning lake views. It specialises in modern European cuisine infused with authentic Peruvian influences. There is a small selection of à la carte options as well as a five-course set menu (by advance booking only) – the chefs themselves serve the dishes, adding a distinctive personal touch. The 300 labels on offer showcase wines from Bordeaux to Slovakia. Alternatively, there is a good range of non-alcoholic drinks to accompany your food. Every Sunday from 12pm to 6.30pm is "Family & Friends", when à la carte classics are served, such as parihuela (Peruvian bouillabaisse), Wiener schnitzel or Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancakes). Tip: Head to the Sunset Lounge for a nightcap by the lake.

Name: zeit|geist
Description En: The centuries-old Walk'sche Haus in the heart of Weingarten abounds with charm. Outside it's the pretty half-timbered façade that catches the eye; inside, the combination of sleek modern design and a touch of rusticity makes for a particularly pleasing ambience. Sebastian Syrbe cooks up modern dishes based on classical foundations, such as "onsen egg, soy, spinach, nut butter" or "suckling pig, beetroot, horseradish, chives". You can choose à la carte or opt for a surprise menu comprising four, six or eight courses. Tip: In summer, be sure to get a spot on the gorgeous terrace overlooking the Walzbach stream! For a more wallet-friendly alternative, head to stil|bruch. There are also pleasant guestrooms, should you wish to stay the night here.

Name: Treibgut
Description En: As a sophisticated alternative to Seestern, Treibgut adds to the gourmet credentials of the Lago hotel. Modern cuisine is served in a trendy and exceedingly stylish setting. There are also dishes designed for sharing, such as steaks, whole fish or traditional grazing board. A fine selection of products from the in-house bakery, butchery and ice creamery is available. In summer, the lakeside setting is best enjoyed on the terrace.

Name: Zum Adler
Description En: Bearing its name of old, this modern restaurant carries on the tradition of the original 19C Zum Adler inn. Today it is lovely and light inside, with a smart and minimalist decor. The focus lies squarely on high-quality meat, such as Wagyu beef steak. Fish and vegan options also available. At lunchtime there is a smaller offer with a reasonably priced lunch menu - but you can also choose from the steak menu.

Name: Rindenmühle
Description En: Take a seat in the elegant yet cosy, country-style interior – or, in summer, out on the beautiful garden terrace – and choose from a seasonal menu. Vegetarians are also catered for. For overnight guests there are cosy contemporary guestrooms.

Name: Zum Storchen
Description En: This establishment is run by the Trienen family in a beautifully renovated old townhouse. The food here is exceptional; the cuisine is seasonal and regional, drawing on modern and international influences. Tip: Try the daily specials as a set menu. There are two pleasant terraces: one out on the pavement, and one in the courtyard to the rear of the building, which is quieter. Comfortable modern guestrooms.

Name: bistronauten
Description En: A word to the wise: make sure you book, as this really appealing restaurant is always busy! Housed in an old railway station dating from 1903, the atmosphere is laid-back, the decor modern with industrial charm and the food excellent. On the blackboard there is a seasonal set menu – choose between meat, fish and vegetarian for the main course. They also have a selection of German wines. Dine at the counter to watch the chefs at work in the open kitchen.

Name: Die Traube
Description En: In the centre of the village, this half-timbered house dating from 1647 is a real gem. It is home to this restaurant run by Anita and Stefan Schleier with great dedication since 2001. The cosy atmosphere and traditional decor are as compelling as the ambitious Mediterranean cuisine based on carefully selected seasonal produce. Mouthwatering dishes include salmon with wild garlic risotto and melted tomatoes or "variation of veal with peas and carrots". There is also a well-curated wine list. The terrace in front of the old barn is another lovely feature. Tip for motorists: Public car park just around the corner.

Name: Landgasthof Backers
Description En: The Backers family business has a long tradition to its name, stretching back to 1843. Today, the sixth and seventh generations are running the show with great dedication. The fresh and flavoursome food draws on the region and the seasons, and ingredients are sourced locally wherever possible, including the venison and Diepholz geese. The restaurant is a long-standing member of the Slow Food community. There are also a few comfortable guestrooms. Try the "Backers zum Kennenlernen" deal: four-course regional set menu with drinks, plus overnight accommodation.

Name: Die Achkarrer Krone
Description En: The culinary tradition at Zur Krone dates back to 1561. Today you can look forward to a plate of calf’s kidney, tripe or oxtail stew, and in summer, a delicious sausage salad. The Baden cuisine and wines can be enjoyed in the cosy dining room or on the terrace. Comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Pades Restaurant
Description En: Wolfgang Pade offers a constantly changing menu, which is based on the availability of produce and relies on regional producers. Please note that there are only two service times: 5.45pm and 8.15pm – so make your reservation in good time! The garden terrace behind the pretty patrician house is magnificent.

Name: BECKER'S Weinhaus
Description En: The original building, which houses this, the second Becker's restaurant, stands in contrast to the modern new hotel building. The abundance of pale woodwork makes it nice and cosy in this space, which leads into an adjoining vaulted brick cellar. Choose between a three- or four-course set menu and à la carte options. The "business lunch" deal and the "quick lunch" daily special are popular. Pretty terrace.

Name: Kräutergarten
Description En: Since as far back as 1983, the friendly and dedicated owners have been running this restaurant with its pleasant and elegant interior. It is easy to see why they have so many loyal regulars. The cooking, rooted in the classical tradition and using excellent fresh ingredients, is shaped by the seasons and Mediterranean touches. Diners can order à la carte or compose their own three-course menu from the same selection. The service comes courtesy of an attentive team. You'll certainly want to come back again!

Name: Forsthaus Ilkahöhe
Description En: The idyllic hilltop location with its fantastic view across Tutzing to the lake is a huge draw of this restaurant – the terrace is fabulous! This converted forester's lodge has an attractive, upscale interior that combines modern style and regional touches. The menu features seasonal dishes made with select ingredients. Mediterranean and international influences are as prominent as the regional classics. While only a small selection of simpler dishes is served at lunchtime, things take a more ambitious turn in the evening. There is also a self-service beer garden.

Name: Gasthof Kreuz
