Description En: This traditional hotel and restaurant located at the edge of the pedestrian area has a gorgeous terrace overlooking the Gut Betha Fountain. On the menu: regional and seasonal cuisine, including locally hunted game. In addition to à la carte dishes, there is an inexpensive three-course set menu ("Regiomenü"), to be relished in a pleasant atmosphere. The wine list has some surprising rarities in store, and the service is cordial and attentive. They offer several immaculate guestrooms in the building itself, plus holiday apartments within walking distance. You can park free of charge just a few minutes' walk away (Parkplatz Bleiche).

Name: La Maison Eric
Description En: This absolute gem of an old half-timbered house is tucked away in a side street. The interior is tastefully decorated and replete with charming details; outside, a gorgeous terrace gives onto the wonderful garden. Classic French cuisine is served as a four-course lunch menu. Fresh, top-quality ingredients go into dishes such as sea bass fillet with fennel risotto or Barbary duck breast with root vegetable purée. Attentive, courteous and committed to the well-being of his guests, owner Eric Grandgirard is always on hand and glad to recommend wine pairings from a list dominated by local and French labels.

Name: Nannina
Description En: In her tiny restaurant, host Giovanna Di Tommaso (known as Nannina) devotes herself tirelessly to her passion: Italian cuisine. Prepared with fresh high-quality ingredients, her dishes are ambitious and packed with flavour. As well as an extensive à la carte menu, there are three different set menus – one for two or more people and another for four. Delightful terrace to the rear of the building. Practical: The restaurant has its own car park.

Name: ZUM HIRSCHEN beim stöckeler
Description En: This family-run restaurant is firmly established in the village and surrounding area. The cosy, rustic dining rooms and pretty terrace in the shadow of the church making an ideal setting for its seasonal, regional cuisine. There is also a good selection of gluten-free dishes. The matching wines are offered. Overnight guests can look forward to pretty, modern Alpine rooms and a good breakfast – taken on the balcony terrace perhaps?

Name: möbius - das restaurant
Description En: Run by Tommy R. Möbius and his wife, this small restaurant makes a chic impression. In this modern and tastefully designed space, she leads the service with warmth, professionalism and a personal touch. In the evening, the chef-patron creates bold and ambitious cuisine based on classical foundations. Dishes such as "WALD.WASSER – wild mushroom consommé, stuffed paccheri, caraway crisp" or "TAFEL ABER SPITZ – grilled veal topside from Höllerschmid, spinach, rösti, apple and horseradish sauce, jellied stock" are served as a set menu or à la carte. Simpler menu at lunchtime. Tip: Delicatessen items can be purchased to take home. In addition, there are regular themed dinner menus and cookery courses.

Name: Habbel's
Description En: Habbel’s offers a fine-dining experience beyond compare. International dishes such as tuna carpaccio coated in wasabi-sesame seeds and saddle of lamb in thyme foam with grilled vegetables feature on the menu, while the wine list offers around 1, 000 wines and spirits from the Habbel in-house distillery, including a 1977-vintage whisky!

Name: Christophorus
Description En: For car enthusiasts who are fans of quality cuisine: here you can take in views of the Porsche Museum or Porscheplatz as you tuck into Mediterranean and international fare such as pluma bellota Ibérico taco with pineapple and pink peppercorn chutney, or barbecued US prime beef. You can also opt for a six- or nine-course tasting menu. The open kitchen offers some fascinating insights. Impressive wine list comprising over 500 items. A lift takes you straight from the car park to the restaurant on the third floor.

Name: Alois-Anton Kaminrestaurant
Description En: A good alternative to the fine dining restaurant of the Park-Hotel Egerner Höfe. The choice is yours: dine in the cosy Bavarian-style dining rooms dubbed "Alois" and "Anton" or in the more upmarket Kaminrestaurant. Just as charming is the terrace, which is sheltered from the wind and has a view of the pastures and mountains. Either way, you can enjoy cordial service and regional and seasonal dishes in a pleasantly laid-back atmosphere.

Name: Gasthof Hirsch
Description En: Set in the centre of this Black Forest village, this attractive restaurant dating back to 1748 is popular for its robust cuisine with classic foundations and plenty of flavour – the sauces are also fantastic! This is all testament to the skill of owner Thomas Zimmermann, who uses select ingredients in his dishes. The atmosphere, too, is just right, thanks to the lovely decor and the exceedingly friendly, attentive hostess. Tip: There are also some individually designed, upscale guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: HerR
Address: Herrngasse 20, Rothenburg ob der Tauber, 91541, Germany
Description En: The handsome herrnschlösschen hotel, located in the Old Town, is home to a delightful little restaurant whose stylish modern interior design seamlessly incorporates the building's historical architectural features – note the huge wooden beam dating back to 1526! Following the seasons, the five-course set menu features dishes such as "Norwegian skrei, celeriac, pak choi, sesame" or "Franconian lamb, Jerusalem artichoke, morels, Martini". The charming waitstaff will recommend the perfect wine accompaniment. Fabulous terrace in the baroque garden!

Name: Zur Sonne
Description En: Run by the Glück family, this place serves fantastic seasonal dishes and regional classics. From game to Altmühltal lamb and their unique "Sauerbraten 2.0", the menu is packed with delicious options. With a clear preference for local produce, the kitchen team serves up dishes that are beautifully balanced in flavour. The bright, modern conservatory is a delightful space, as is the splendid terrace in summer. Comfortable and attractive guestrooms.

Name: Krone
Description En: Nestled in the heart of Steinenbronn, this family-run establishment has been welcoming diners for many years. Here, modernity meets tradition in both the decor and the cuisine. The menu features timeless classics such as pork fillet in a creamy sauce, alongside more ambitious dishes, some made with game that they hunt themselves. For a pleasant, laid-back alternative, head to Krönle – the options written up on the board are very reasonably priced. Some house-made food items such as greaves lard spread, tripe, spaetzle, sauces and maultaschen can be purchased to take home. Decent guestrooms.

Name: Cube
Description En: The absolutely fabulous location is as much of a draw as the glass architecture, the design and the ambitious international cuisine. There is a simpler lunch menu, too. The o.T. Bar serves breakfast, cake and after-work drinks. The lovely terrace is positioned on Schlossplatz, a square in front of the art museum. Tip for theatre- and concert-goers: Ask about their "late-night" dining slot.

Name: Schweizers Restaurant
Description En: Originally opened in 1903 as Schweizer Hof, this restaurant is housed in a painstakingly restored listed building. In the aesthetically pleasing Jugendstil setting of this neighbourhood restaurant, the atmosphere is welcoming, thanks in no small part to the charming staff. A well-coordinated team in both the kitchen and front of house ensures a wonderful evening. Savour the five- to seven-course set menu, which also comes in a vegetarian version. The flavoursome dishes showcase precise technique and high-quality ingredients. There is a well-curated wine list, as well as pairings by the glass. The quiet shady courtyard terrace is delightful in summer.

Name: Königshafen
Description En: The journey up to the north of the island is well worth it! Here, family tradition dates back to 1881, with the fifth generation currently looking after this spruce house with a white-brick façade, serving good regional and seasonal cuisine. Nice garden terrace behind the house. Tip: They are always well booked, so you should book early!

Name: mundart Restaurant
Description En: Set in the heart of a quaint wine-growing village, the old house is an enchanting destination. The menu features flavoursome dishes with both classic and Mediterranean influences, such as grilled octopus with celeriac cream and lime, or veal loin and braised pork cheek with mashed potatoes. Dine in the charmingly rustic yet modern interior or out on the terrace in the lovely courtyard. The converted barn is perfect for private events.

Name: Hugenhof
Description En: Inside Hugenhof is every bit as attractive as its exterior suggests with its lovely high ceilings, cosy old beams and a roaring open fire in winter. Every evening brings a different 4-course menu, which chef Klaus Ditz will announce at your table. This is accompanied by expert wine selections from his fellow chef and sommelier. The rooms are simple but smart.

Name: Zur Sonne
Description En: Hanspeter Rombach attaches great importance to organic ingredients in his cheerful and inviting restaurant. At lunchtime and in the evening, local cuisine is served à la carte; the evening features more elevated fare – diners can choose between two set menus or an additional à la carte selection. Tempting highlights include "red cabbage baked in a salt crust, marinated with linseed oil and red onions, a fine bitter-orange sauce, and toasted sourdough" or "St Peter kid goat from from Ernst's farm, served in its own jus with mushrooms, fig compote, baby vegetables and Schniederspätzle (Black Forest spaetzle)". The on-site shop, Heimatladen, sells delicious treats such as organic vegetables, bread, honey, wine and more for you to take home. For overnight guests, this long-established family business has cosy guestrooms and a lovely sauna area. Tip: Pay a visit to the monastery with its Baroque church.

Name: Reck's
Description En: Cuisine, art and accommodation are combined in this long-running family business. Three sisters run both the hotel – with some classic, some stylishly modern guestrooms – and the restaurant, which offers really good seasonally influenced cuisine. There are three cosy dining areas inside; outside, there are tables on the terrace in the shade of the plane trees, which affords views of the orchards! There is art displayed everywhere in the house.

Name: Kirschner Stuben
Description En: This warm and welcoming place exudes a charming liveliness. The terrace overlooking the lake is an absolute delight. Complementing the inviting ambiance is a delectable selection of regional cuisine. An appealing array of fresh, flavoursome dishes awaits, ranging from braised veal cheeks to game and fish from Tegernsee. Most of the ingredients are sourced locally. At lunchtime there is a speciality menu. Maier zum Kirschner Hotel proposes pretty guestrooms imbued with Alpine charm.

Name: Landhaus Hohenlohe
Description En: This long-standing family business, now with Matthias Mack at the helm, is run according to a winning formula. In a very pleasant informal atmosphere, extremely friendly and experienced waitstaff are always on hand. The delicious food is freshly prepared and feautures regional and international influences. You can compose a three- or four-course set menu from the appealing list of options (also vegetarian) or order à la carte. Appetising dishes include porcini ravioli, baby spinach, Brettenfeld Jerusalem artichokes, truffle fonduta. The restaurant also has its own herb and vegetable garden. Overnight accommodation is available in this well-kept country house nestled in a residential area.

Name: Juliette
Description En: Are you looking for a slice of the French way of life in the middle of Potsdam? In the Holländisches Viertel (Dutch Quarter), you will find this beautifully designed restaurant, which is housed in a charming 17C half-timbered house. The dining space comprises three different levels, where you can enjoy ambitious classic cuisine accompanied by just the right wine, as a discreet soundtrack plays in the background. In addition to the menu, you can also choose a few dishes à la carte. If the weather is nice, would you like an aperitif at one of the small tables on the pavement before your meal?

Name: Bistro
Description En: The bistro at the exclusive Gut Lärchenhof golf club on the outskirts of Cologne offers a somewhat simpler alternative to the eponymous fine dining restaurant, but you are just as assured of flavour and freshness – at both lunch and dinner. They serve dishes ranging from Currywurst to Königsberger Klopse (meatballs) and caviar. Needless to say, the terrace overlooking the green is delightful!

Name: Domschenke
Description En: This family-run restaurant is now in its third generation. Whether you sit in the rustic-style dining area with its regulars' table or in the pleasant conservatory, you are assured of friendly service. The menu features home-style, regional and more sophisticated dishes. Order à la carte or opt for one of the daily specials on the blackboard. In summer, make a beeline for the outdoor seating area, which is shaded by old trees.

Name: Heim's Restaurant
Address: Moselstraße 27, Reil an der Mosel, 56861, Germany
Description En: The food served in this 300-year-old restaurant is honest, fresh and full of flavour. Classic and regional cuisine is served throughout the day (kitchen opening hours: 12-8.30pm), taking the form of dishes such as cod à la grenobloise with spinach and mashed potatoes or "Original Wiener Schnitzel" with fried potatoes, salad and cranberries. You will be able to find just the right Moselle wine to accompany your meal. Service comes courtesy of a friendly and proficient team, the atmosphere is pleasant, and in summer, the wonderful terrace with a view of the vineyards and Moselle beckons. The Reiler Hof hotel has lovely guestrooms.

Name: Ganter Restaurant Mohren
Description En: Whether you opt for a cosy-rustic or a chic-modern interior, the food on offer here is fresh and regional with international influences. Try the char with pearl barley, herbs, almonds and madras curry spices.

Name: Gasthaus Cervus
Description En: At this well-run, rustic-style restaurant located in the town centre, Johannes Füller serves up regionally influenced cuisine strewn with international touches. The dishes are lovingly prepared and delicious – the speciality is Rostbraten (roast beef with all the trimmings). You can choose between a set menu and à la carte options. Simpler and shorter lunchtime menu. From some tables you can steal glimpses into the kitchen. In summer, the courtyard is a charming spot.

Name: Landhaus Drei Raben
Description En: The Koep family has been synonymous with excellent cuisine since 1995… and you can expect just that when you come to eat here on this property on the 18C Landgut Jaquetrois. This former agricultural estate is planted with beautiful old trees. The restaurant has a cosy dining area (warming fireplace in winter) and a fabulous terrace with views over the Mahnensee – especially charming at sunset! The food is international, regional and seasonal. Tip: Coffee and cake are served on Sundays.

Name: Schloss Niederweis
Description En: This tasteful restaurant is housed in the converted corn barn of a magnificent Baroque castle dating from 1751. The decor is a fascinating blend of rustic cachet and modern design – the open truss roof is striking and the two historical carriages on the wall are certainly eye-catching! Sample the flavoursome dishes à la carte or as a set menu, washed down by your choice from the terrific wine list that includes rare finds, including by the glass. Charming garden, a banquet hall and a registry office. On a practical note: easy parking.

Name: IU & ON
Description En: This family business in the heart of Nuremberg has been around since 1972! Many regulars keep coming back, having been won over by the aromatic dishes, which include classics like laab and tom yum. Add to that a clean-lined, minimalist-style interior and friendly service. By the way, the restaurant takes its name from the sisters Iu and On who cook here.

Name: Wilde Triebe
Description En: Set in refurbished former railway buildings dating back over 150 years, Wilde Triebe offers a minimalist, imaginative and fashionable mix of art and food. The flavoursome, seasonal, regional fare is served in an upmarket brick, concrete, steel and wood interior on the restaurant’s own tableware. Great garden.

Name: MINNECI
Description En: The historical character of this town house dating back to 1560 makes it the perfect setting for an Italian restaurant. Here, diners can either opt for a four- to six-course set menu or order à la carte – think flavoursome Mediterranean dishes such as ravioli with wild mushrooms, sage and balsamic vinegar. At lunchtime, there is a smaller, more budget-friendly set menu. Friendly service comes courtesy of charming waitstaff. Delightful terrace in front of the building. For those coming by car: there is a public car park next door.

Name: Schloss Restaurant Venus
Description En: Set in the "Versailles of Westphalia", this classic, distinguished restaurant has vaulted ceilings and numerous paintings by owner Franz L Lauter, an avid painter. A seasonal set menu is available in the evening (from 5pm). At lunchtime on Thursday to Saturday, there are set menus. Tip: Either before or after dinner, why not take a walk around the castle and park?

Name: ZweiSinn Meiers | Bistro
Description En: If a really nice bistro in Nuremberg is what you are looking for, then this is the place for you! A pleasant, refined atmosphere, friendly service, and good food await you here. The modern and Mediterranean-inspired à la carte selection is appealing, and there is also a caviar menu. At lunchtime, the reasonably priced daily special is always in demand. Tip: On Wednesday and Thursday evenings, selected dishes from the menu of the fine dining restaurant, which is located in the same building, go into a three-course business menu (sparkling wine included). They also offer fine wines by the glass and top-drawer alcohol-free alternatives.

Name: Historisches Gasthaus Sanct Peter Restaurant Weinkirche
Description En: Having been renovated following the disastrous floods of 2021, this restaurant gives off an impression of classical elegance. A 13C church with a gallery forms the core of the establishment. There are also two other attractive dining spaces (called Alte Lay and Walporzheimer Himmelchen). The delightful terrace to the rear of the building offers a view of the greenery. The menu features dishes with regional, seasonal and international influences. Classics include braised ox cheeks in Ahr valley Burgundy sauce, and turbot in Ahr valley blanc de noir sauce. The selection of Broggsitter wines is impressive, and there is a well-stocked wine shop on site, too. From 2-6pm, you can order from the smaller menu, with options such as the platter of cold meats and cheeses. They also run Hotel Sanct Peter in the town.

Name: Imperial by Alexander Herrmann
Description En: The location that houses this restaurant is interesting in the way it blends the architectural details of the old building, such as high ceilings and large arched windows, into the modern, chic-meets-urban look. In this stylish yet relaxed setting, diners are treated to warm hospitality and can watch Michael Seitz at work in the open kitchen, as he cooks up international dishes with a Franconian twist. For parties of two or more people, the sharing menus "Celebration Mood" and "Glamour Mood" are highly recommended, as well as the "Nuremberg Menu", which presents Franconia's Top Ten dishes in a whole new way. Tip: The "OpenHausBrunch" takes place on certain Sundays, and there are other regular events.

Name: Cornelia Poletto
Description En: A really appealing restaurant in a great location! The upscale, modern and elegant interior is a delightful setting in which to enjoy the fresh Mediterranean cuisine. With clear Italian influences, an interesting three-course set menu is served at lunchtime; in the evening, a larger set menu is proposed, along with a selection of delicious à la carte options. Be sure to try the antipasti! The service is friendly and professional. Tip: In summer, there are also a few tables on the pavement in front of the building. Between the restaurant and the cookery school, Paola's is a bar-cum-deli – ideal for an aperitif or cocktails.

Name: Spielweg
Description En: First mentioned in records in 1705, the original Spielweg building, managed by the Fuchs family, makes for a wonderfully cosy setting. The charming dining rooms are done out in traditional Black Forest style and the service is extremely friendly and attentive. Diners can expect classic regional cuisine that is ambitious and full of flavour, as in the warm smoked char from the Wutach in a cold potato and leek broth. It also draws on Asian influences, cf. their wild boar dim sum with soy sauce – Asian cuisine is one of the young chef's passions. The lunchtime menu proposes somewhat simpler fare, making this place an ideal stop-off for a light meal during a hike. You can stay overnight in well-kept, individually furnished guestrooms.

Name: Turmstube
Description En: In the friendly atmosphere of this elegant space, the delicious and seasonally inspired cuisine with international influences is made with select ingredients, sourced from the region wherever possible. Diners can choose between the set menu ("Genießermenü") or the à la carte options. Tip: Take in the lovely view from the terrace. For those who would like to stay a little longer, Der Birkenhof hotel promises patrons a comfortable stay complete with spa facilities.

Name: Steinheuers Landgasthof Poststuben
Description En: This attractive alternative to the fine dining restaurant also impresses with sophisticated cuisine made with excellent ingredients. The classic menu incorporates regional influences alongside international flavours. This results in a diverse range of dishes, such as pan-fried veal black pudding on hispi cabbage with fried onions and bacon, or tuna carpaccio with a soy and sesame vinaigrette and tuna tartare on a sushi rice base, as well as fine cuts of local rabbit on spring vegetables with gnocchi, or Zwiebelrostbraten (sirloin steak with crispy fried onions and gravy), Brussels sprouts and Schupfnudeln (finger-shaped potato dumplings). The well-stocked wine list is the same as in the fine dining restaurant. Dine in the cosy interior, or head out to the delightful leafy terrace. For overnight stays, there are double rooms available in the main building, as well as a comfortable guesthouse.

Name: Christians Restaurant
Description En: Run by Sandy and Christian Heß, this is an appealing restaurant – and that goes for the atmosphere as well as the cuisine. The interior is sleek, bright and welcoming, with beautiful arched windows affording a view of the Neckar River. And then there's the terrace overlooking the water – a truly idyllic spot in which to dine in fine weather! The cuisine is contemporary with a Mediterranean touch – opt for a set menu or order à la carte. This lovely space can also be used for private functions.

Name: Joseph Naus Stub'n
Description En: This restaurant, named after the first climber to reach the summit of the Zugspitze, is not just an attractive place where service comes courtesy of very friendly staff; the food here is also delicious. At lunchtime, there is a reasonably priced two-course set menu and a small à la carte menu. In the evening, peruse the large menu, from which you can order either à la carte or a set menu. Hotel Zugspitze also has well-kept guestrooms, should you wish to stay overnight.

Name: Ponyhof Stammhaus by Tobias Wussler
Description En: The sort of restaurant you would love to have in your own neighbourhood. This long-standing family-run establishment delights guests with classics like cordon bleu, as well as contemporary creations such as scallops with pumpkin, curry and lemongrass – and, of course, excellent charcoal-grilled steaks. The menu, which features plenty of comforting soul food dishes, is complemented by friendly service and an inviting setting that makes it easy to linger. In summer, the terrace is divine. Unsurprisingly, this charming spot is also a popular choice for weddings.

Name: CARLS Brasserie an der Elbphilharmonie
Description En: As you take in the view of the Elbe River and the Elbphilharmonie concert hall, you can soak up the lively and casual yet elegant brasserie atmosphere and enjoy sophisticated North German cuisine such as fish stew or whole sole. The unique location means that window seats are in demand. And in summer, diners make a beeline for the terrace. The bistro next door serves bowls and tartines. A wine bar is also part of the premises.

Name: Zipang
Description En: Zipang translates to "kingdom of the rising sun" – everything about this restaurant, from the modern minimalist decor to the menu, is a celebration of the Far East. The food is definitely something to get excited about – with meticulous attention to detail, the finest ingredients are prepared using authentic Japanese techniques. At lunchtime, excellent value for money; in the evening, the mood is more upscale, with a six- or eight-course tasting menu featuring dishes such as hamachi with mackerel, yuba, Japanese mayonnaise and summer vegetables, or tuna with shungiku wasabi sauce and shrimp croquette. Great selection of top-shelf sake! Friendly service.

Name: Kamino
Description En: The Zumkeller family have transformed what was once Chämi-Hüsli into this cosy restaurant and tapas bar – the striking fireplace with extended flue after which Kamino is named presides in the middle of the dining area, which has a high ceiling and a round floor plan. The classic and Mediterranean cuisine always has a modern touch and a certain pizazz. Dishes such as roasted sea bass fillet with home-made tagliarini and lobster cream give the tasty tapas a run for their money. The icing on the cake is the charming service provided by owner Stefanie Zumkeller and her team. For an overnight stay, there are three pretty and cosy guestrooms.

Name: NIKKEI NINE
Description En: You should not hesitate to make a reservation at this culinary hotspot in Hamburg. Located in the luxurious Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten, the restaurant has a stylish and elegant ambience, courtesy of an interior done out in dark wood, cream and gold tones. On the menu: Japanese-international fusion cuisine. The service is very friendly and attentive. They also have a cool bar.

Name: Hirschen
Address: Breisgauer Straße 47, Freiburg im Breisgau, 79110, Germany
Description En: One of Freiburg's culinary institutions, Hirschen draws diners to the peaceful neighbourhood of Lehen. An authentic and cosy Baden-style atmosphere awaits you in the dining area of this charming historic inn, which is run with dedication by the Baumgartner family. For years, the kitchen has been renowned for its masterful blend of regional fare and classic French cuisine. Dishes such as Baden lamb's lettuce with roasted goose liver and black truffle, and "winemaker's skrei" with cabbage braised in champagne, glazed grapes, bacon strips, butter croutons and mashed potatoes showcase the finest, freshest ingredients. The carefully curated wine list also highlights wines from Baden and France, including prestigious labels such as Romanée Conti. Service is friendly and attentive. The restaurant is part of the hotel of the same name.

Name: Goldener Karpfen
Description En: In this historical house, seasonal international cuisine with classic regional roots is prepared from select fresh produce. Tip: the classic beef tartare. To be accompanied by a choice of international wines. The interior is elegant and cosy at the same time; in summer you can sit outside. For overnight stays there are comfortable guestrooms ranging from stylishly refined to modern chic.

Name: Hirschen
Description En: A beloved fixture in the valley, this restaurant is part of the long-established hotel of the same name, located right in the heart of the village on the banks of Glotter River. In its rustic yet elegant interiors, diners are waited on by a friendly front-of-house team. For decades, the kitchen has showcased the best of Baden and French cuisine, with a pronounced emphasis on seasonality – be it game, mushrooms or asparagus. Both at lunchtime and in the evenings, the cooking is ambitious. Dishes such as grilled octopus served on a bed of curried lentils and vegetables, or veal loin in a cream sauce with chanterelles are available à la carte or in the set menu. The wine list is dominated by labels from the Baden region.

Name: Zenzakan
Address: Taunusanlage 15, Frankfurt on the Main, 60325, Germany
Description En: Since opening in 2009, this has been a go-to classic in the city's financial hub. Somewhat hidden away, this elegant and stylish restaurant is accessible via a courtyard. The interior, done out in dark tones with dimmed lighting, smacks of the Far East (the terracotta warriors are eye-catching). The atmosphere is lively, and contemporary music provides the acoustic backdrop. The menu includes a wide selection of pan-Asian dishes ranging from sushi and sashimi to classic curries and robata grill specialities. Dishes such as velveted black pepper beef or char siu chicken are especially tempting.

Name: Zum Krug
Description En: This place has a long history that stretches back to 1720, and the Laufer family has now been at the helm for three generations. Behind the gorgeous historical façade, the cosy dining spaces exude traditional charm. Theregional and international cuisine takes its cue from the seasons, and the menu includes dishes such as a Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast) of organic pasture-fed beef with potato dumplings and cranberries. The friendly and professional waitstaff will be happy to recommend fine Rheingau wines from the estate to accompany your meal. Delightful courtyard terrace. Smart guestrooms – some are especially modern.

Name: Rebstock
Description En: Rebstock offers comfortable, country-style dining rooms, attentive service and good regional fare including snail soup, pike dumplings and venison ragout. In summer the idyllic terrace offers views of the surrounding parkland and the Black Forest, while another attraction is the large selection of home-made cakes and pastries.

Name: Lohninger
Address: Schweizer Straße 1, Frankfurt on the Main, 60594, Germany
Description En: Set on the banks of the River Main in Frankfurt, this restaurant tastefully blends the classic flair of the old building in which it is housed – beautiful high stucco ceilings, herringbone floorboards – with modern minimalist design. The cuisine draws on the Lohninger family's Austrian roots as well as Asian and Mediterranean influences, and the menu has been divided into two sections accordingly: "Die Heimat" (homeland) and "Die Welt" (the world). The dishes stand out for their finesse, intense flavours and the quality of the ingredients; chef-patron Mario Lohninger and his kitchen team are careful to avoid gimmickry and place the emphasis on flavour. This holds for both classics and signature dishes such as Carinthian Schlutzkrapfen (high-Alpine cheese ravioli), Imperial and Royal ox cheek goulash, or Spencer Gulf kingfish sashimi with foie gras, pickled vegetables and a buttermilk and horseradish dressing. The front-of-house team is friendly, attentive and pleasingly relaxed and down-to-earth – anything but stuffy.

Name: Bastian's Restaurant
Description En: This country inn with its bright, tastefully decorated interior and beautiful, partly covered terrace specialises in serving culinary classics that evolve with the seasons. There are two set menus (one of which is vegetarian) comprising four to seven courses. The quality of the ingredients, which are mostly locally sourced, is beyond question. Great value for money. The service is very friendly and charming.

Name: Weinstube Sibylla
Description En: A good place to come for unpretentious cuisine. The menu ranges from classics such as Wiener schnitzel or Berlin-style calf's liver to a "Gourmet Tradition" section featuring dishes such as saddle and shoulder of venison in pasta sheets, with tenderstem broccoli and an elderberry jus. There is also a selection of vegetarian dishes and a range of delicious desserts. Lovely old wooden floors, wood-panelled walls and pretty decorations make for a charming atmosphere. The verdant terrace is also inviting. Guestrooms are available in the adjoining Erbprinz hotel.

Name: Kupferpfanne
Description En: Erwin Weidenhiller's restaurant, in a central location opposite the town hall, has been a classic on Fürth's food scene for decades. In the comfortable and elegant interior, they serve classic cuisine with seasonal and international-Mediterranean influences, made with good-quality produce. Tip: the reasonably priced lunch menu.

Name: Hartmaier's Villa
Description En: This modern restaurant is housed in a pretty villa dating back to 1816. The Hartmaier family and their team have been serving up good food here for many years. The menu is wide-ranging, characterised by seasonal, regional and international influences – from Zwiebelrostbraten (steak with onion rings), beans with bacon and roast potatoes to wild-caught Icelandic redfish fillet with pak choi and spinach and ricotta ravioli. At lunchtime, people flock here for the bargain set menu with a choice of starters and mains. The feel of the place is both elegant and more casual, with a lovely leafy terrace in front of the building. Tip: You can buy wines to take home at their Vinothek.

Name: Landgasthaus Schuster
Description En: The Schuster family's country inn is thoroughly charming! This is primarily down to the warm hospitality extended by the lady of the house, and the tasteful interior design. And then there are the chef-patron's seasonally influenced classic dishes such as pike-perch sausage accompanied by creamed sauerkraut with dates, or venison with nuts, black walnut sauce, cranberries and Savoy cabbage. Individual courses from each of the two set menus ("Tradition" and "Genusswerk") can be ordered à la carte. Decent wine selection with good options available by the glass.

Name: Stüble
Description En: Stüble is the tasteful, rustic-style à la carte restaurant of Wellness Lauterbad, a chic spa hotel. In the cosy and comfortable wood-panelled space, the service is friendly and attentive. The regional and seasonal cuisine has international influences. Order à la carte or plump for a three- or four-course set menu. In summer, you can drink in the view of the countryside from the terrace.

Name: Lindenhof
Description En: Like their hotel with its cosy individually designed guestrooms, the Hankhs' restaurant is also very popular. This is down to the excellent seasonal cuisine, which has regional and Mediterranean influences. A great deal of dedication and care is invested in preparing the often complex dishes. You can order à la carte or opt for a set menu (vegetarian version available). Friendly and competent waitstaff. The small terraces in front of and to the rear of the building are delightful.

Name: Das Ballenberger
Description En: A friendly, modern restaurant in the centre of the old town close to the historic Krämerbrücke bridge, Das Ballenberger serves seasonal, international cuisine including scallops with two kinds of asparagus and orange. You’ll also find some mouthwatering home-made cakes and a delicious breakfast from 9 am after a stay in one of the five charming overnight apartments.

Name: Bistro Fatal
Description En: It would be a shame (perhaps even a fatal mistake) not to get to know Alexandre and Sarah Bourgeuil's pleasantly unpretentious bistro, where savoir-vivre is the order of the day. The classic French menu is enticing, featuring staples such as beef tartare, chocolate soufflé and – of course – oysters. The food here is excellent. You can pick dishes to make up your own three-course "Toi & Moi" set menu – vegetarian options are also available. In summer, a terrace is set up on the pavement in front of the building. N.B. Finding a parking space nearby is not easy.

Name: VIDA
Description En: This place has it all: a stylish, upscale decor, enthusiastic, professional and friendly service, and creative international cuisine incorporating both Asian and Mediterranean influences. Diners are offered a choice between the "VIDA" set menu – with meat or vegetarian – and a range of à la carte dishes. The attentive and well-drilled service team is also on hand to offer expert wine recommendations – there is an attractive selection to choose from. Wine pairings to complement the set menu are also available. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif or digestif at the VIDA bar.

Name: Kronenschlösschen
Description En: The setting is lovely, whether under the elegantly painted period ceiling or out on the pretty terrace with its adjoining garden. The cooking is a modern take on classically based cuisine, enhanced with international influences. At the helm is Marcus Langer, most recently head chef at the Atelier Sanssouci in Radebeul. His set menu (with meat/fish or vegetarian choices) can be ordered in a five- to seven-course format – with the option to extend it to 10. Tempting dishes include cauliflower and "Périgord truffle délice with hazelnut vinaigrette and tarragon" or king crab tartlet with wild garlic and morels. The wine list ranks among the best in Germany. The bistro on site is an alternative to the fine dining restaurant. There are cosy, well-appointed guestrooms in the hotel of the same name.

Name: Il Cortile
Description En: You get to this restaurant, which is located in a pretty little courtyard in Erfurt's old town via Johannesstraße. In a cosy atmosphere, diners tuck into Mediterranean-inspired cuisine that draws on flavours from all over the world. The menu features dishes such as "Ricotta, truffle, pea, Serrano", "Salsiccia, capers, sugar snap pea" or "Fjord trout, grape, risotto, truffle".

Name: Weinrestaurant Turmschänke
Description En: In this restaurant in the Nicolaiturm, the lovely historical details, such as paintings and original furniture dating from 1912, foster a rustic yet elegant feel. The waitstaff are pleasingly laid-back and down-to-earth. Meticulously prepared seasonal dishes are served as a set menu or à la carte; mouthwatering options from the barbecue are also available. Complete with helpful descriptions, the wine list comprises some 140 items – most are from the region, but international labels also feature. Special wine evenings are also hosted here.

Name: Gambero Rosso da Domenico
Description En: Domenico Cannizzaro has been on a mission to showcase Italian cuisine in Franconia for well over 20 years, and has run this restaurant at the small marina with his wife, Teresa, since 2012. Here, they live and breathe hospitality, serving two set menus, "Domenico" and "Teresuzza", which each comprise three or four courses – it's also possible to mix and match. Astute wine recommendations come courtesy of the chef-patron himself. Gorgeous terrace overlooking the Main River.

Name: Taverna & Trattoria Palio
Description En: Palio offers fresh Italian fare from the open kitchen in a relaxed trattoria-style atmosphere – you simply have to try one of the pasta dishes! The seasonal set menus are also interesting. There’s also a lovely terrace in the shade of some old chestnut trees.

Name: Restaurant Villa Esche
Description En: Built in 1903, the former coach house of Villa Esche (now the Henry van de Velde Museum) houses this bright, tastefully designed restaurant where diners can enjoy attentive service and top-notch seasonal cuisine. Opt for the four-course menu or order à la carte. At lunchtime, the options are slightly more limited but include moderately priced daily specials. Delightful terrace overlooking the grounds.

Name: Redüttchen
Description En: What was once the gardener's cottage at the 18C La Redoute ballroom and concert hall is a feel-good place that has won over more than its fair share of regulars. The restaurant's appeal lies not only in its extremely charming ambience, but also in Matthias Pietsch's innovative take on modern cuisine and the experienced, courteous and cordial service. The pleasant dining area is laid out over two levels, and the terrace to the rear of the building is also a lovely spot.

Name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
Description En: A big name on the fine dining scene, Tim Raue has created a pleasingly down-to-earth brasserie of the sort you might expect to find in Paris. This place has a modern feel tempered by a slight touch of nostalgia. The excellent food comes in the form of an interesting contemporary concept: diners can choose à la carte or put together their own four-course meal – a vegan version is also possible. The menu features classics such as beef Wellington for two and seasonal dishes.

Name: eins44
Description En: This restaurant tucked away in the third courtyard of the Otto-Reichel-Höfe hits the mark. Inside, the converted distillery exudes a casual, trendy urban loft atmosphere with an industrial feel. At beautiful solid old beechwood tables, diners tuck into ingredient-led seasonal cuisine. The modern, creative dishes are served in the form of a five- or seven-course set menu – either with meat/fish or vegetarian. Dishes such as "spring salad, brawn & peanut" or "Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef), wild garlic & coffee", are rich in flavour and represent excellent value for money. Service is provided by a dedicated, friendly and well-organised team.

Name: maiBeck
Description En: Run by Jan Cornelius Maier and Tobias Becker (hence the contraction "maiBeck"), this inviting restaurant serves modern cuisine made from select ingredients. The decor strikes just the right note: upscale yet unpretentious; the service is friendly. The wine list offers excellent value for money, particularly the bottles. Finally, the location between the cathedral and the Rhine means that the terrace is a place to see and be seen. Tip: Take a stroll through the Old Town before or after you dine. Handy for motorists: The Philharmonie underground car park is just around the corner.

Name: Schwanen
Description En: This family business has been going for three generations. The dishes served in this chic, modern restaurant are made with preference for regional produce and sing with freshness and flavour. For a bistro alternative, Karl Benz Stube has a short menu featuring traditional Swabian fare. There are also suitable spaces for special occasions available and practical guestrooms with contemporary decor. Tip: the "Kultur & Genuss" events.

Name: Wappen-Saal
Description En: This imposing castle estate provides a truly unique setting for dining. Before taking a seat in the stately Wappensaal in the Schlosshotel at Burg Schlitz, take a leisurely stroll along the Goetheweg. Experience the historical ambiance of this restaurant as you savour a four- to six-course menu of ambitious classic cuisine beneath an impressive high ceiling. The charming and experienced staff will be happy to help you choose the perfect accompaniment to your meal from the well-curated wine list.

Name: Hubertushof
City: Ilbesheim bei Landau in der Pfalz
Address: Arzheimer Straße 5, Ilbesheim bei Landau in der Pfalz, 76831, Germany
Description En: Remaining true to the Südliche Weinstraße, Sandra Bernhard and Jochen Sitter moved from Birkweiler to this 300 year-old former coaching house, which they run with great dedication and charm. The chef cooks traditional and modern, but above all, flavoursome fare. Dishes include classics such as pan-friend black pudding and Saumagen (stuffed pig’s stomach). The interior courtyard is gorgeous.

Name: Das Tschecherl
Description En: This small restaurant is an offshoot of Jürgen Wolfsgruber's Sparkling Bistro, which is located nearby. The cuisine has a distinctly Austrian bias, with dishes such as pike-perch fished in the Salzkammergut region, Szeged cabbage and caraway potatoes featuring on the concise menu. On these premises where legendary chef Hans Haas of Tantris fame used to have his cookery school, the decor is now pleasantly sleek and pared back. A competent team takes care of the service; you get interesting glimpses of the action in the open kitchen. The restaurant is open from 12-8pm.

Name: Zehntkeller
Description En: Located in the middle of the village, this traditional establishment serves good regional and seasonal cuisine. The menu features mouth-watering dishes such as braised beef cheek in a Pinot noir sauce. Opt for a four-course set menu or order à la carte. The house proposes its own organic wines. Very friendly and well-drilled service, a cosy interior, and a lovely terrace laid out under the wisteria. The hotel of the same name has stylish, classic guestrooms.

Name: Zur Iphöfer Kammer
Description En: This picture-perfect Gasthaus is located on Marktplatz, in the centre of this quaint wine-growing town. The lovely little terrace is as inviting as the elegantly charming interior. Your dedicated hosts, Heidrun Kaufmann and Markus Lösch, really know how to create a warm and welcoming atmosphere: she provides cordial service with a personal touch; he cooks up ambitious dishes brimming with bold flavours – venison ragout fin with rye bread gnocchi, or sea bass with artichokes and lemon polenta. Excellent wines from Wirsing wine estate.

Name: Danzer's
Description En: The contemporary ambience in a sleek and at the same time homely style makes for an appealing start – not to mention the terrace with a view of the dike. The food is international and regional, such as fillet of sea bass in bacon butter with wok-fried savoy cabbage. Short lunch menu.

Name: Westphalenhof
Description En: This stylish and sophisticated restaurant is somewhat tucked away in a residential area. Here, the Westphal brothers – one is the chef, the other the sommelier – delight diners with delicious food and excellent wine recommendations. The menu features international dishes that take their cue from the seasons, such as confit halibut fillet in nut butter, potato scales, cauliflower cream, dried tomatoes and Sardinian pasta. The walk-in wine cellar accommodates 120 different labels. The restaurant is also open for lunch on Saturdays and Sundays.

Name: Adler Stuben
Description En: The traditional Parkhotel Adler, which has been a family-run business for over 500 years, is home to this historical Black Forest establishment whose origins date back to 1639. It has five really pleasant dining areas, from the charming "Stube" with its old wood panelling and a low ceiling, to the chic "Bergkristall", and of course the terrace. The cuisine comprises Baden and international dishes; vegetarian options are also available. The wine list features a good selection of wines from the region. For an overnight stay, there are cosy, elegant guestrooms.

Name: FLYGGE
Description En: An interesting location! The restaurant run by the partnership of chef-patron Mathias Apelt and Britta Künzl is housed in the canoe club and has a cool, pared-back design with an urban boathouse feel. There is also a wonderful view of the fjord – needless to say, a spot on the terrace is a tempting prospect. The open kitchen serves Nordic-inspired and regionally based soul food – appealing dishes include "pasture-raised beef tartare, cauliflower, jalapeño & mole" or "winter cod, black pudding, pointed cabbage, apple & fermented chips". Tip: You can also book the Chef's Table – here, a five-course set menu is served to parties of up to six diners, who can enjoy a view of the kitchen.

Name: Schwane 1404
Description En: In this centuries-old inn in the beautiful old town, this is a truly charming alternative to the fine dining restaurant. Both the inviting, rustic-style restaurant room and fantastic inner courtyard are appealing places to eat. In the evening, you can order modern-inspired classic dishes à la carte or opt for the "Romantik" set menu. Many of the ingredients are locally sourced; some of the vegetables are from their own garden, and they have their own wines. Hearty meals (‘Brotzeit’) are served at lunchtime.

Name: Am Osterfeuer
Description En: First opened as a bakery 100 years ago, this family-run establishment is now in its fourth generation. Hans-Jörg Dunker and his team have long been synonymous with quality and Westphalian cuisine with an international twist. The restaurant interior is attractive and cheerful, having been given a skilful modern makeover, but care has been taken to leave the traditional character of the building intact. One of the chef's specialities is the wonderful fish and shellfish soup with aioli, bread and Parmesan. A gorgeous terrace for summer. There is also a charming hall available for festivities.

Name: Wieland-Stuben
Description En: This restaurant has become something of an institution in the region. The Wieland-Stuben has been a byword for classic cuisine since 1965. The elegant, tastefully decorated dining area makes for a really appealing setting, as does the gorgeous garden terrace. In their classic French cuisine, Lukas Erfurth and his team use only selected ingredients that impress with their freshness and quality. You can opt for the set menu or dine à la carte. The excellent service comes courtesy of a team headed up by sommelier Ronja. On Sundays, there is a three-course set menu (no à la carte dishes).

Name: Madame Ngo - Une Brasserie Hanoi
Description En: It is definitely worth waiting for one of the coveted tables here! This charmingly informal restaurant is very popular due to its simple but excellent Vietnamese cuisine, which is also inexpensive. There is an enticing aroma from the bubbling pots in the open kitchen – a large bowl of authentic “pho” (noodle soup) is practically a must!

Name: Jacobs Restaurant
Description En: Accommodated in Hotel Louis C. Jacob, which boasts a prime location, this restaurant serves modern cuisine with classic touches in an elegant setting. Diners can order à la carte or opt for one of the set menus (conventional or vegetarian). Among the standout dishes are the lobster foam soup and the braised ox shoulder. The Vierland duck served in four courses is a classic option for two. Well-curated wine list. The seating out on Lindenterrasse, overlooking the Elbe River, is undoubtedly the highlight in summer.

Name: Otto
Description En: This compact restaurant has an appealingly lively atmosphere. The friendly vibe is due in no small part to the fantastic, well-drilled team, who have a personalised touch when it comes to looking after diners. The open kitchen – overlooking which there are also a few seats at the bar – sends out seasonal, modern, pared-down dishes with Nordic influences, all made using locally sourced ingredients. You can choose between the sharing menu and à la carte dishes. Vegetarians are also catered for. There is a rather short but carefully curated wine list with a predilection for natural and orange wines. Small terrace in front of the restaurant. This very popular restaurant has limited seating, so be sure to book in advance!

Name: Roku - Japanese Dining & Wine
Description En: This is the third restaurant to be opened by Yoshizumi Nagaya in Düsseldorf. The atmosphere is trendy, modern and relaxed. The Japanese menu ranges from a variety of appealing starters and a fine selection of sushi and sashimi to tempura, fish and meat dishes – including, for example, A5 Wagyu steak. There is a good, predominantly German wine list and a selection of sake. Tip: Lunch Wed-Fri.

Name: Il Teatro²
Description En: Founded in 1984, this family-run establishment located close to the Staatstheater (hence the name) is now run by the second generation, with Daniele di Sario taking the helm several years ago. He delivers classic Italian and French-style cuisine that is in keeping with the zeitgeist: The spaghetti carbonara, turbot with Champagne sauce or lemon dessert ("Kreation von der Zitrone") are shining examples. In keeping with the name of the restaurant, the menu is divided into different sections: Act 1, Intermezzo, Act 2 and Epilogue. Veteran chef Giovanni likes to get in on the action front of house, joining forces with the enthusiastic and attentive service team. In summer, the terrace seating out on the wide pavement is especially appealing.

Name: Klinker
Description En: It's no surprise that this spot in central Harvestehude draws such a crowd, with its trendy urban design, lively atmosphere and floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the street's activities – plus terrace tables available in summer. The food is predominantly vegetarian. The establishment's commitment to ecology is reflected in the exclusive use of regional ingredients, primarily sourced from Demeter farms. Fermenting and preserving are also part of their practice – with about 3 000 jars of preserves in stock, their dedication speaks for itself! Some jars are also used as decoration in the restaurant. Tip: The sharing option allows you to sample various dishes. Highlights include the salsify "carbonara" with Parmesan and hazelnut, and yellow carrots with saffron and chives.

Name: Chang
Description En: This restaurant serves a wide range of Asian cuisine – sushi, curries and wok dishes are the highlights, and the focus is squarely on the quality of the ingredients. Inside, there is a minimalist decor and open kitchen; outside, a lovely covered terrace. The trip to Grünwald is definitely worthwhile. Marily, which sells ice cream and confectionery in summer, is housed in the same building. Tip: Park free of charge in the multi-storey car park on Marktplatz a few metres away.

Name: Kurpfalz Weinstuben
Description En: A typical Palatinate wine tavern in the middle of Berlin? At Adenauerplatz near Ku'damm, you will find this traditional bar tucked away in a courtyard. In cosy, rustic rooms you can enjoy home-style cooking and regional classics, along with 50 wines served by the glass and 800 on the wine list. Short menu of the day at lunchtime.

Name: Hirschkönig
Description En: Here, rural charm combines with elegant and contemporary interior design to create a welcoming setting – that goes for both the Hirschen hotel and its small fine dining restaurant with its upscale, sleek and stylish dining space. The modern and seasonal set menu, "Feld & Flur" ("Field & Fell"), is composed of six or seven courses imbued with a hint of the Mediterranean, such as wild garlic ravioli with tomato. Wine pairings are available upon request. Head to the delicatessen for house-made specialities such as chutneys, pickles and cured meats.

Name: Phaedra
Description En: Are you in the mood for Mediterranean cuisine with Greek influences? Then try, for example, the fried halibut with a chive beurre blanc and trout caviar or the house-made mezze – to share or as a starter. Good produce is used, including meat from Franz Keller and wild-caught prawns. The place has an appealingly trendy bistro look and a pleasantly relaxed atmosphere. Diners take their seats at regular tables or high tables – the latter offer partial views into the open kitchen. Tip for motorists: public multi-storey car park opposite.

Name: Freilinger Wirt
Description En: This traditional Bavarian inn has been around since 1870 and today it boasts a lovely blend of clean, modern design and warm wood. The patron and chef is a master butcher and his experience working at renowned restaurants can be seen in his good seasonal dishes. The large terrace is popular.

Name: 20° RESTOBAR
Description En: This modern, unpretentious restaurant with a terrace, bar and lovely inner courtyard is located in the centre of town. In a pleasantly lively atmosphere, you can enjoy Spanish-Mediterranean cuisine: in addition to fish, meat, rice and potato dishes, you will of course also find tapas, croquetas and the like. In keeping with the Mediterranean concept, the name refers to the average water temperature around the island of Mallorca.

Name: Oechsle
Description En: Serving flavoursome dishes made from fresh, high-quality ingredients in a pleasant contemporary atmosphere, this restaurant on the corner is a real gem. Its short menu draws on both Mediterranean and classical influences. This place also doubles as a wine bar, so you can look forward to a well-curated wine list. Experienced and charming waitstaff provide great service with a personal touch. In summer, the tables out front, facing the street, are in high demand.

Name: XO Seafoodbar
Description En: As well as haebel, just across the street, Fabio Haebel runs this trendy, laid-back establishment in the heart of St Pauli. Occupying two floors, the restaurant has an agreeably lively atmosphere. Upstairs there are also a few seats at a counter facing the open kitchen. The food is modern and seasonal, with a focus on seafood specialties, including oysters, monkfish schnitzel and grilled prawns, and of course the famous "Pasta Krabbe". Alternatively, you could opt for "Chef's Choice" – a selection of items picked from the menu by the kitchen team. Tip: Treat yourself to a cocktail at the small bar. In summer, head for the terrace and soak up the buzzy atmosphere.

Name: Bistro oma & enkel
Description En: oma & enkel ("grandma & grandchild") is the culinary concept at this bistro in the long-established Posthotel. The name symbolises a bridging of the gap between the generations, from the traditional to the modern. Recipes of yesteryear are brought up to date and classics of Franconian cuisine are given a contemporary twist. In a pleasingly laid-back atmosphere, choose between "Franconian tapas", the "Signature Menu" or the "Duck Menu". Don't miss out on the Franconian bouillabaisse or the apricot dumplings.

Name: Thuns Dorfkrug
Description En: This restaurant offers beautifully laid tables, attentive service and good cuisine offering a mix of regional and international elements. The simple and elegant style of the decor features attractive contemporary pictures and parquet flooring. The guestrooms are in a clean-lined, modern style.

Name: martino.kitchen
Description En: This pleasant, well-run little restaurant in the town centre has a friendly atmosphere and trendy vibe. Led by chef Martino Stirn, after whom the restaurant is named, the team sends out tasty Mediterranean/Italian dishes made in the open kitchen using seasonal ingredients. In addition to the à la carte selection, in the evening there is the option of ordering a surprise menu. Lunch options are more limited. The lady of the house provides charming service. In summer, from the terrace you can hear the carillon of the majestic church, the nearby Marktkirche, ringing at given times.

Name: Scala
Description En: This modern restaurant boasts beautiful views across the lake and a delightful terrace. It also serves seasonal dishes with an emphasis on regional ingredients, and the vegetable and animal produce are used in their entirety. A smaller selection of dishes is served at lunchtime. Friendly service and fine wines.

Name: Ratsstube
Description En: What was once the town hall is now home to a cosy yet on-trend restaurant that combines contemporary design with the warmth of wood and natural tones. The cuisine is ambitious, creative and modern, but at the same time agreeably down-to-earth. The names of the dishes are original, such as "Feuerstarter" ("Firestarter"): corn-fed chicken pot-au-feu from the charcoal grill, or "Geflüster" ("Whispers"): Ahrenholz catfish fillet, char caviar, pea medallions, leek, elderflower beurre blanc. The colourful, visually appealing creations are underpinned by meticulous preparation and are a joy to eat. In addition to the à la carte selection, there are two four-course set menus, one of which is vegetarian. Shaded by lime trees, the terrace is lovely in summer. Comfortable overnight accommodation is also available.

Name: Steinbuck Stube
Description En: In the centre of town is this pretty, lavishly restored 400-year-old house. You can sit in the cosy, tastefully decorated restaurant, in the modern wine bar or on the terrace that adjoins the two. There, you will be served seasonal and Mediterranean-influenced classic dishes, accompanied exclusively by regional wines. There are also guestrooms for a pleasant overnight stay.

Name: Park-Restaurant Vogelherd
Description En: Quality restaurant in a former manor house famous for its good seasonal cuisine. You can also dine on the attractive terrace alongside a small pond.

Name: Brunnenstuben
Description En: Don’t be put off by the somewhat unprepossessing exterior at Brunnenstuben because the food is excellent! Petra and Thorsten Beyer – she running the kitchen, he managing the friendly and professional front-of-house team – serve flavoursome Swabian fare including an excellent Zwiebelrostbraten (roast beef with onions).

Name: Johanniter-Kreuz
Description En: This former farmhouse, which is over 350 years old, has been turned into the lovely Johanniter-Kreuz Romantik Hotel, complete with a tasteful, rustic-style restaurant in what was once the stable. Old beams and a central fireplace lend the space a cosy atmosphere. The food is rooted in classical culinary tradition, with regional influences and close ties to the seasons. Vegetarians are also catered for, and there is a decent wine selection.

Name: Gastraum
Description En: This modern extension of the attractive Villa Hügel (1914) has a sleek and elegant feel. The ceiling-to-floor windows afford an impressive view of Trier, and the terrace is a particularly sought-after spot in this regard! Savour fresh, contemporary dishes made from good-quality ingredients and washed down with regional wines. The young team in charge of serving you are charming and professional. Cosy guestrooms and a lovely relaxation suite await overnight guests.

Name: Fässle le Restaurant
Description En: For years this has been a favourite in the city, drawing plenty of loyal regulars and newcomers alike. In his cosy restaurant in the Degerloch neighbourhood, Patrick Giboin presents his take on classic French cuisine both as a set menu and à la carte. Vegetarians are also well catered for, and children's menus are available, too. At lunchtime during the week, the prices are somewhat lower – the Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) is especially popular. Tables on the terrace are coveted in summer.

Name: Ambiente
Description En: Few would suspect that such a stylish restaurant could be found on this rather unremarkable industrial estate. In summer, a lovely terrace adds to the appeal. The friendly proprietress provides highly attentive service while the chef-patron transforms top-quality ingredients into freshly prepared classic dishes such as venison saddle with nut crust, savoy cabbage, gnocchi and juniper jus. Three set menus are available (one of them vegetarian), and dishes may also be ordered à la carte.

Name: Dorfstube
Description En: It's no wonder people that love to eat here! In addition to its fine dining restaurant, Hotel Hirsch has its Dorfstube, which is a great option for fans of Swabian cuisine. In the cosy old dining space, completely done out in wood, you can tuck into specialities such as tripe, maultaschen and Zwiebelrostbraten (roast beef with onions). Vegetarian options are also on the menu. The delicious dishes are all made using regional produce. Friendly service. We highly recommend staying overnight. The guestrooms are really lovely and inviting.

Name: BECKER'S
Description En: Matching the architecturally striking design hotel of the same name, this upscale fine dining restaurant impresses with its chic, minimalist style. The interior boasts leather shell chairs, elegant hardwood floors and grey panelling on the walls – a lovely setting in which to enjoy a modern menu made with selected ingredients, to the sound of contemporary background music – choose four- to six courses. Incidentally, chef-patron Wolfgang Becker is not only a cook – as the son of a winegrowing family (now in its fifth generation), he has also trained as a winemaker. He shares his passion for fine wines with his wife Christine Becker, herself a winemaker and sommelier, who oversees the vineyard. Naturally, wines from their own estate are among the options to accompany the excellent food.

Name: Uwe & Uli - Zuhause bei uns
Description En: A listed building standing directly on the market square, the 17C Liefrink House has an appealing exterior. Behind the pretty half-timbered façade is a charming, modern restaurant (formerly “essWebers - Küche am Markt” but now with a new name) which serves seasonal, international cuisine. The chef's set menu is complemented by a number of à-la-carte options.

Name: Seehalde
Description En: Run by the Gruler brothers, this restaurant boasts a stunning lakeside location – tables on the terrace are much coveted in summer! The fresh and ambitious cuisine is also a major draw. The menu takes its cue from the region and the seasons with a classic bent. Fish from Lake Constance is also served and is even the focus of a three- or four-course set menu for two people. There is also a set menu based on regional classics. Alternatively, take your pick from the appealing à la carte selection. The well-curated wine list includes some gems, too. Well-drilled front-of house team. Tip: Take some homemade bouillabaisse in a jar with you to enjoy at home. There are well-kept guestrooms as well - most of them look out to the lake.

Name: Zur Tanne
Description En: The setting could not be more charming: a gorgeous centuries-old Black Forest house with a cosy, rustic-looking interior. As for the food, top-notch seasonal ingredients from the region and the seasons go into flavoursome dishes. Attentive service. The well-kept guestrooms don't have TV, but in this idyllic village setting, you'd rather enjoy the peace and quiet anyway!

Name: Zur Linde
Description En: The Trautwein brothers run this former coaching inn with great dedication. Some 300 years old, it features a charming blend of historical and modern decor. The menu includes Swabian classics such as Gaisburger Marsch (traditional beef stew), Maultaschen and Zwiebelrostbraten (beef and onions in gravy), alongside seasonal dishes such as pink-roasted lamb rump with beans done two ways and polenta with herbs, as well as vegetarian options. A lovely leafy terrace lies to the rear of the building. A rustic vaulted cellar can be booked for private functions. Tip: The shop sells soups, sauces, Maultaschen and spaetzle to take away.

Name: Bootshaus
Description En: The beachside location is simply idyllic – you can't get much closer to the Baltic Sea! In this restaurant at the Weissenhaus Private Nature Luxury Resort, diners are shown to their tables in a modern interior with a glazed façade that affords fantastic views. But it is of course the terrace that is the top attraction! The food is a fresh blend of Mediterranean fare – somewhat simpler at lunchtime, more sophisticated in the evening, from classic dishes to elegant culinary compositions. Service runs from 12:00 to 17:00, and in the evening (by reservation) from 18:00 to 21:30.

Name: Meister Lampe
Description En: It's a real pleasure to eat here, and there's a good reason for that: chef-patron Daniel Stübler clearly puts his heart and soul into running his cosy little restaurant. He cooks up excellent regional and international dishes, and also does the serving himself – not only is he highly accomplished at what he does, he is also an extremely cordial host and single-handedly creates a fantastic atmosphere! The carefully curated wine list is also remarkable, featuring wines from Baden-Württemberg, Baden and the Palatinate only.

Name: Zum Hirsch
Description En: Familiar faces in the region, Markus and Britta Nagy are known as ambitious restaurateurs. Here, in their charming half-timbered inn dating back to 1688, they serve regional and Mediterranean-inspired fare. In addition to an à la carte menu, there is a three- to five-course set menu in the evening and the reasonably priced three-course "Eat & Talk" set menu at lunchtime (Tue-Fri). On Friday and Saturday, for dinner, diners choose between two set menus (no à la carte). In winter, the room with a fireplace is cosy; in summer, the lovely terrace beckons. Well-kept overnight accommodation available.

Name: Villa Hammerschmiede
Description En: Housed in a charming villa dating back to 1893, this is a thoroughly inviting destination. Whether seated in one of the comfortable dining areas or the light and airy pavilion, you can look forward to ambitious, classic and regional cuisine, presented in the appealing "Villa Lunch" set menu or in the evening the three- to five-course "Feinschmecker-Menü". There is also an à la carte selection featuring dishes such as farm-raised duck with red cabbage and creamed chestnuts, or Dover sole for two. The terrace is especially lovely in summer, and comfortable accommodation is available as well.

Name: goldener Adler
Description En: Everyone would love to have a cosy and buzzing restaurant like this in their neighbourhood! The contemporary decor strikes a rustic note; the traditional regional cuisine is based on fresh produce. The menu ranges from classics such as cordon bleu with potato salad to internationally inspired dishes such as pan-fried prawns with shellfish noodles. Vegetarian options are also available. The beautiful large terrace (you can park here in winter) is a stand-out feature in this city-centre location.

Name: Krietsch
Description En: This centuries-old establishment has a rich and eventful past, having functioned at various times as an arms factory, an orphanage, a prison and finally the restaurant Fuggerei. Today, as Krietsch, it serves seasonal, regional cuisine, but it also draws on international influences. As well as flavoursome dishes à la carte, such as Black Angus Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast) with bread dumplings and Brussels sprouts with bacon, a six-course set menu is available on Thu-Sat evenings (with 48hr notice). At lunchtime, a daily set menu is served. The interior boasts a soaring period vaulted ceiling, and there is a gorgeous terrace outside. Tip: Take the opportunity to visit the minster right behind the restaurant.

Name: Der Engel
Description En: The perfect example of a traditional Baden inn! This family-run establishment has been welcoming guests since 1764, offering a consistently enjoyable experience. Behind its old half-timbered walls, there are charming dining areas – some more traditional, others more modern. In a warm and welcoming atmosphere, diners tuck into delicious regional fare. Options include classic dishes, daily specials and set menus. Tip: There is a fantastic selection of digestifs. Overnight accommodation available.

Name: Gourmetfabrik
Description En: This restaurant boasts a gorgeous location at Lake Schwerin. Inside, the atmosphere is pleasingly laid back; the decor is modern, and you can see into the open kitchen. Out on the terrace you can take in the view of the small harbour. The reasonably priced daily set menu, served at lunchtime, is a hit. In the evening, you can choose from a good variety of dishes, including steaks listed on the specials board. Only the finest regional and seasonal ingredients are used. Tip: They also hold cookery classes.

Name: Die Alte Brauerei
Description En: This establishment started out in 1877 as Becker-Brauerei and the interior decor incorporates a combination of historical, rustic and modern elements. In today's iteration of the restaurant, Florian Dauphin, son of the friendly owners, Eric and Isabelle Dauphin, heads up the kitchen team. Lorena-Jil, his charming wife, manages the service with professionalism, care and attention. You will be treated to seasonally influenced French dishes – choose à la carte or go for one of the set menus: the four-course "Découverte" or six-course "Signature". During the week, they propose a reasonably priced lunch deal. The restaurant is accessed via the courtyard. The terrace is lovely. It is also possible to stay overnight in one of the six guestrooms, each individually designed by artist Margret Lafontaine.

Name: Kings and Queens
Description En: This small restaurant has plenty of regulars, who are drawn by the modern and elegant decor, the friendly and professional service and the seasonal international cuisine. A choice of three menus, one of which is vegetarian, is proposed. You can also swap out courses or order à la carte. The wine list is sure to please, with an especially well-curated selection of labels from the region.

Name: Weinstube am Brühl
Description En: These former stables have been converted into a delightful restaurant, in which terracotta tiles, warm colours and an old brick ceiling lend a real country feel. The international cuisine on offer follows the seasons closely. The six-course "Weinstuben-Menü" (with vegan/vegetarian alternatives) comes with optional wine pairings. À la carte dining is also possible. Attentive service comes courtesy of a friendly and adept front-of-house team. Tip: Summer barbecue evenings (Jun-Aug) – booking recommended. Charming and elegant guestrooms are available in the Hotel Am Brühl.

Name: Schlossanger Alp
Description En: Set against the backdrop of the Allgäu Alps, this hotel has tasteful, comfortable guestrooms and a lovely, inviting restaurant in which cosy Alpine vibes meet elegant table settings. Affording stunning views, the terrace is a wonderful spot for a meal in summer! The menu is varied: at lunchtime (from 1pm) there is a three-course set menu and à la carte dishes, including "small bites to share"; in the evening the selection includes their "Signature Menu", as well as dishes ranging from braised vegetable ravioli to lobster, and venison loin to Gröstl (pan-fried potatoes). The extensive wine list encompasses a fine selection.

Name: Hoppe's
Description En: The atmosphere is welcoming and lively, and the food is great – it's no wonder that people come back again and again. The menu features dishes from Alsace and Baden, with mouthwatering options such as "coq au vin à la chef", beef sirloin served with roasted onions and spaetzle, or Baden-style pike dumplings. They also do Flammkuchen. There is outdoor seating to the front of the building.

Name: Weingut
Description En: After a stroll through the city, how about dinner at a chic restaurant with a trendy modern decor? There are plenty of options to choose from here at Weingut, including house specialities, steaks, plus a selection of dishes that changes every week (see the "Wochenkarte"). Alternatively, you could simply opt for tapas or a glass of wine – you can also buy bottles to take home. The service is very friendly and attentive. Decorative wine racks and high tables contribute to the pleasant wine bar atmosphere of the place. There are two reservation times: 17:30 - 20:00 and from 20:15.

Name: Fährhütte 14
Description En: This restaurant, an offshoot of Überfahrt, enjoys an idyllic lakeside location. The modern decor has a touch of rustic maritime flair while the service is friendly and accomplished. International and seasonal dishes. You will also have the opportunity to rent a deckchair on the beach! N.B. the restaurant is not accessible by car – getting there involves a 300m walk.

Name: La Bouche et El Pato
Description En: This bistro with a pleasant, cosy atmosphere is located in the middle of the city – the cathedral is just a stone's throw away. La Bouche is on the ground floor and El Pato is on the first floor, but diners enjoy the same international and Mediterranean dishes on both levels. One speciality is beef bourguignon with French Charolais beef. In addition to à la carte dishes, there are two set menus, one of which has dishes for sharing, tapas-style. Cordial service. The terrace in the pedestrian zone is also appealing.

Name: Kugelmühle
Description En: Max Matreux has been at the helm of this sleekly designed restaurant in a side wing of a factory since 2001. He champions a responsible approach, as is apparent in his classic cuisine, which features seasonal and regional ingredients. In addition to the three- to five-course set menu, there is an appealing à la carte selection. Friendly and professional service adds to the pleasant atmosphere.

Name: Heldmann & Herzhaft
Description En: Originally the home of an industrialist, this smart 19C villa is the perfect backdrop for the delicious cuisine of chef-patron Ulrich Heldmann. Diners choose from a varied seasonal menu and à la carte dishes based on fresh produce – and the "Menu Surprise" Wed-Thu. The setting is truly lovely, with its high ceilings, elegant hardwood floors and refined table settings; in summer, tables on the terrace are of course particularly coveted. And then there is the experienced, attentive and pleasingly laid-back service provided by a team under the management of hostess Petra Heldmann. The restaurant is also open for lunch Wed-Fri.

Name: Gastwirtschaft Ferdinand Reuter
Description En: This traditional family-run establishment serves good-quality regional cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons. Classic fare and more sophisticated dishes both feature on the menu. The atmosphere is friendly and cosy – in the more modern section, diners take their seats at long wooden tables. Hotel Reuter, which houses this restaurant, has comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Adler
Description En: There is a snug, rustic feel to this old inn, where service is warm under the direction of the proprietress – a charming lady from Styria and a superb hostess. In the kitchen, a father-and-son team prepares flavoursome dishes using good-quality ingredients. The menu is divided into two sections: classic Swabian dishes such as Kutteln in Lemberger (tripe cooked in red wine) or house-made Maultaschen, and sophisticated dishes like pan-fried Breton monkfish on parsley root purée in lemon beurre blanc with tomato and spinach, and wild garlic risotto. An old jukebox provides the background music. Tip: The restaurant produces its own range of schnapps.

Name: Kraftwerk
Description En: This restaurant housed in a converted power station is more than a stylish location – it also serves extremely good food. The cuisine combines classic, Mediterranean and Austrian influences, including appetising dishes such as lobster with truffle sauce, beef fillet Rossini; the "Austrian classics" section on the menu features the likes of "Bertl's Kalbsfleischpflanzerl mit Kartoffel-Rahmgurkensalat" (veal patties with potato salad in a creamy cucumber sauce). In addition to à la carte dishes, there are two set menus: "Kraftwerk Classics" and "Kraftwerk Finest". The international wine list is comprehensive. In summer, tables are set up on the terrace. Friendly, attentive and professional service.

Name: Ondersch Genusswirtschaft
Description En: Going by the name "Ondersch" (a dialect word meaning different), this establishment located in the multipurpose "LOFT" building offers a street-food restaurant with a bar and the Genusswirtschaft gourmet restaurant. On the upper floor, a lively, urban atmosphere provides the setting for tasty modern cuisine made from seasonal and regional produce.

Name: Alpenkönig - Esslust
