Description En: Diners take their seats in a lovely, upscale dining space comprising areas that range in style from traditional charm to modern chic. A cordial and professional front-of-house team serves fresh regional cuisine that draws on the seasons and Mediterranean influences. You can go à la carte or choose dishes for the three or four courses of your own set menu. There is also an appealing wine list. The restaurant is located in the attractive Alpenkönig hotel, which has inviting guestrooms and modern wellness facilities, set in the gorgeous Allgäu landscape.

Name: Würzhaus
Description En: This really is an appealing restaurant. At lunchtime, things are toned down a little, with reasonably priced options (à la carte or a small set menu). In the evening, there is an ambitious set menu that comes in four to six flavourful courses. Head chef Diana Burkel is committed to using locally sourced ingredients. The wine list is dominated by organic, biodynamic and natural wines. The service is friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere is welcoming.

Name: Villa Medici
Description En: This spruce villa enjoys a delightful location in a quiet residential area on the outskirts of the city. Diners here are pampered with friendly service, Mediterranean flavours and Italian wines in a chic and inviting atmosphere. In addition to à la carte options, there are daily specials and a tasting menu. A charming terrace is laid out to the side. Plus, there are five attractive guestrooms.

Name: von Rhemen
Description En: The restaurant at the stylish Schloss Wilkinghege hotel features an elegant and lofty dining room with an ornate stucco ceiling and bags of historical charm. The cuisine is classic and very seasonal – order à la carte or opt for one of the set menus. The selection varies slightly depending on the day of the week. Service is friendly and adept. Given the grand setting, guests are often tempted to book a room for the night.

Name: LENZ
Description En: Lenz Leslie Himmelheber pours his heart and soul into his cheerful, modern restaurant and his style of hosting has a distinctive personal touch. In season, the self-proclaimed "duckman" carves his signature Vierlande duck at your table. The menu also includes regional, seasonal and cosmopolitan cuisine with dishes such as salmon tartare with ponzu beurre noisette, pear and avocado, or "Wiener schnitzel deluxe" with cucumber salad, truffle chips and truffle mayonnaise. A separate lunch menu featuring simpler and more affordable dishes is another highlight. The food is complemented by an appealing wine list, service is attentive, and the bright conservatory can be opened up in summer!

Name: Fischereihafen Restaurant
Description En: This is and remains an institution – something of a home from home for Hamburg's fish lovers, young and old! A constant stream of international customers comes and goes from lunchtime to evening. In an elegant setting boasting traditional Hanseatic decor and a view of the harbour, quality fish from the fish market is served at the height of freshness. Classic dishes include turbot or lobster in different variations, but the menu also includes Asian and Mediterranean-influenced options.

Name: Henriks
Description En: This stylish restaurant is loved for its good food and attractive setting. The interior is chic; outside, there is a lovely terrace shaded by mature trees. Led by patron Claas-Henrik Anklam, the kitchen team combines Asian and Mediterranean influences with seasonal, regionally inspired cooking, including grilled dishes, lobster and caviar. The wide-ranging à la carte selection is complemented by a more budget-friendly lunch menu – ideal when time is short (takeaway is also possible). Beyond the impressive wine list, HENRIKS Bar beckons with long drinks, cocktails and more.

Name: Bahnhöfle
Description En: Run by Thierry and Elisabeth Falconnier, this charming restaurant is a real institution in the Freiburg area. Set in a little house by Gundelfingen's railway station, the place has a cheerful, easygoing feel. Inside, watercolours by the owners' daughter adorn the walls; outside, the cosy terrace is lovely in summer. True to his roots, the chef-patron serves up French cuisine – pleasingly pared down, brimming with flavour and made from excellent ingredients. Fish is the speciality here: think salmon carpaccio, monkfish with porcini or grilled sea bass. Meat lovers are also well catered for, with highlights such as Ibérico pork chop or braised beef cheeks.

Name: Farmerhaus
Description En: African produce enriches the cuisine, which is international in character. Wood carvings and trophies from the country where the dishes originated are interesting to look at.

Name: Die Reichsstadt
Description En: This is the restaurant of the chic hotel of the same name, which provides the historical backdrop for your meal. The tasteful dining area is done out with high-end furnishings and a modern eye. Staff are friendly and professional as they set about serving you fine Baden classics, modernised French dishes, which you can choose à la carte or combine into a set menu – a vegetarian version is also available. The "Taste Menu" comprising six or seven small courses is also an excellent recommendation. In summer, the garden is magical!

Name: Zum Rössl
Description En: This long-standing family-run establishment is housed in a former coaching inn dating back to 1642. In the charming, traditionally styled restaurant, you can choose between regional classics and seasonal dishes, some with a Mediterranean twist. Menu highlights include boiled beef brisket with sweet-and-sour fruits, horseradish sauce and potatoes, or French bouillabaisse with toasted bread and rouille sauce. A surprise menu can also be pre-ordered. The lunch options are particularly appealing. Tip: In good weather, make a beeline for the idyllic terrace!

Name: Kinfelts Kitchen & Wine
Description En: Located near the Elbphilharmonie concert hall, this restaurant embodies the quintessential HafenCity style. The interior is simple yet chic; the large windows allow natural light to stream into the space and afford compelling views of the Elbe canal. Kirill Kinfelt, who made his reputation at Trüffelschwein, serves up classically rooted contemporary cuisine made from top-notch ingredients, eg king prawn with buttermilk, chilli and Thai basil, or monkfish with fregola sarda, radish and herbs. An outstanding selection of international wines and expert recommendations. For dinner reservations, choose between two seatings.

Name: EssensArt
Description En: This restaurant in a residential area has made a name for itself with its seasonal and internationally influenced cuisine. Since 2010, the cordial hosts have been committed to their guests' happiness. Delicious dishes are available in the form of two set menus – one of which is vegetarian – or à la carte. Friendly atmosphere; a nice covered terrace outside.

Name: Alter Wirt
Description En: This inn has a long-standing tradition of hospitality. A relaxed atmosphere reigns in the delightful interior, which combines modern elements with rustic charm. Outside, the lovely terrace is shaded by chestnut trees. With an emphasis on organic and locally sourced ingredients, the menu features regional fare and takes its cue from the seasons. Daily specials are also available. For overnight stays, there are well-appointed guestrooms furnished with natural materials and designed with sustainability in mind.

Name: Brasserie
Description En: If you don’t fancy the gourmet cuisine on offer at Meierei, you can enjoy fresh, international fare or just a slice of home-made cake in the less formal atmosphere of the Brasserie.

Name: Cox
Description En: With its charmingly laid-back feel, this place is everything a bistro should be and, unsurprisingly, draws a diverse crowd. Diners appreciate both the thoughtfully curated, internationally inspired menu and the amiable, attentive staff, who help create the welcoming atmosphere.

Name: Witwenball
Description En: What makes this deluxe bistro in Hamburg's bustling Schanzenviertel so beloved? A perfect blend of cuisine, service and atmosphere. Once a dance hall, this place now exudes a laid-back yet lively energy, and feels at once trendy and chic with its decorative wine racks – the white marble counter in the middle of the space is a striking feature. The delicious contemporary food incorporates regional, seasonal, and international influences. Order à la carte or compile your own four-course "Your Choice" set menu, with a fish, a meat or vegetarian option for the main course. Wiener schnitzel is also always available on Sundays. The impressive wine list comprises over 500 items, and the staff provide expert guidance. Alternatively, you could have a cocktail. Lovely pavement terrace.

Name: Zum Goldenen Engel
Description En: This traditional 16C inn right next to the church has been rebuilt in a way that is absolutely true to the original. You will feel completely at home in the lovingly decorated restaurant, thanks not only to the atmosphere and the competent, charming front-of-house team, but also of course to the high-quality food. Many ingredients come from the region. Plus they have cosy guestrooms.

Name: Villa Busch
Description En: This beautiful, lavishly refurbished villa in an elevated location not only boasts a lovely terrace for summer, but the interior of the restaurant is also tasteful with its stuccoed ceilings, wooden floorboards and modern designer chairs. The chef-patron's kitchen team creates dishes with Mediterranean and Asian influences, including many fish specialities. Plus, you are waited on by a warm and charming front-of-house team.

Name: Brook
Description En: International, German and classical influences are at play here, e.g. loin of lamb with string beans and Parmesan potatoes or venison with Brussels sprouts and chestnuts. In the evening, the beautifully illuminated Speicherstadt opposite is a sight to behold!

Name: Schneider Stube
Description En: Hotel Tuchmacher, ensconced in a pretty Renaissance town house with this delightfully cosy restaurant, is an institution here in Görlitz. The classic regional menu includes dishes such as Wiener schnitzel, stewed rabbit leg on Leipziger Allerlei vegetables, and stewed brook trout roll on pickled vegetables. Almost all of the wines are also available by the glass. In summer, the courtyard with its terrace is absolutely idyllic! "Bleicherstube" and "Zunftsaal" are their attractive salons. The location in the heart of the old town is charming – it is next to the church (Pfarrkirche St Peter and Paul) and not far from the Lausatian Neiße River that borders Germany, Poland and the Czech Republic.

Name: Frankfurter Botschaft
Address: Westhafenplatz 6, Frankfurt on the Main, 60327, Germany
Description En: A really cool location – the spot directly on the Westhafen makes the terrace a real highlight! The interior is just as attractive with its chic decor and wraparound glazing that ensures fine views of the water from every angle. Internationally inspired cuisine is served as a set menu – with meat/fish or vegan – or à la carte. Furthermore, valet parking is also available – it's preferable to put in your request when you make your reservation. Another point of interest is 23 Nord, the event space on the 23rd floor of the adjacent Westhafentower.

Name: Zöllner's Weinstube
Description En: Surrounded by splendid gardens, this 18C half-timbered sandstone building is as charming on the outside as it is on the inside. Sitting beneath a striking vaulted ceiling, diners can enjoy regional as well as Mediterranean-inspired cuisine made from first-rate produce. There is also an excellent selection of Franconian wines. In summer, the terrace is a must!

Name: SonneStuben
Description En: The regional and seasonal cuisine served here wins diners over with the flavours it exudes and its technical prowess. Examples include fillet of regional salmon trout, pak choi, saffron sauce, and braised ragout of local venison, creamed kohlrabi, fried mushrooms. In "Sonne Sharing Style" (for four or more people), the chefs put together a selection of dishes for diners to share. The pretty, cosy dining area affords views of the old town's historical half-timbered façades; having your meal out on the terrace that overlooks Marktplatz is a pleasant option. They are also open for lunch. Tip: It is worthwhile taking a stroll through the town. You can spend the night at Die Sonne Frankenberg hotel.

Name: Mühlenhof
Description En: It is little wonder that Anette and Stefan Rottler's hotel is so popular: Their restaurant serves classic Baden dishes made with top-quality ingredients – from snail soup to pork fillet in cream of mushroom sauce to Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy). The smaller dishes and reasonably priced set menu of the day are also much in demand. The wine list is dedicated to local labels. Friendly and attentive service. Food is served in various dining rooms, some with a cosy, regional feel, others with a fresh and modern look. Delightful covered terrace.

Name: Medici
Address: Weißadlergasse 2, Frankfurt on the Main, 60311, Germany
Description En: Two brothers are your hosts in this city centre restaurant. International dishes with a Mediterranean influence are served in a modern atmosphere.

Name: Bistro Villa Merton
Address: Am Leonhardsbrunn 12, Frankfurt on the Main, 60487, Germany
Description En: Located just outside Frankfurt, north of the Palmengarten, Bistro Villa Merton is a lovely alternative to the fine dining restaurant. While the latter welcomes diners in the evening, the bistro is only open at lunchtime. In the spruce villa built in neo-Baroque style, you can take a seat in an inviting decor done out with an elegant touch to enjoy high-quality regional and international cuisine infused with seasonal influences. An appealing lunchtime set menu is on offer, as well as several à la carte options. The appetising dishes include breast and leg of guinea fowl and classics such as Wiener schnitzel made with veal. Excellent wine recommendations are to be had from the friendly and knowledgeable front-of-house team. Tip: There is a fantastic selection of champagnes. The terrace is also a pleasant place to sit. Good to know: Regular events are also held here.

Name: Brasserie Stadthaus
Description En: This attractive brasserie with its striking high coffered ceiling and pretty interior courtyard promises a genuine French dining experience. Try the tourte de queue de boeuf (oxtail pie) or the seafood platter followed by the tarte au citron. All the wines are French.

Name: The Duchy
Description En: On the first floor of the luxurious Breidenbacher Hof, overlooking Heinrich-Heine-Allee, this is an elegant brasserie. The cuisine is a broad mix, from sashimi and ceviche to beef tartare or ravioli, not to mention the steaks. They set great store by the origin of their ingredients, working with regional producers – and they keep their own chickens and cows. Decent wine selection.

Name: Butcher's american steakhouse
Description En: At Butcher's american steakhouse you can enjoy fine Nebraska beef that the chef presents to the table personally. The cosy restaurant is dominated by dark wood and warm colours.

Name: Adler Wirtschaft
Description En: Established in 1993, Franz Keller's family-run Adler Wirtschaft is an institution in the region. Inside this charming little half-timbered house, the atmosphere is cosy and down-to-earth – traditional tavern culture is still alive and well here. Even from the entrance, diners can catch a glimpse of the Molteni stove, on which the flavoursome dishes are prepared. The concept: you choose dishes to make up your own fixed-price menu – opt for "Das kleine Abendessen" ("The Small Dinner") or "Das große Abendessen" ("The Large Dinner"). The steak selection is tempting as well. Good to know: They use pork from Bentheim Black Pied pigs and beef from Charolais and Limousin pasture-raised cattle, sourced from their own farm in the Taunus region (Falkenhof). In summer, there is a lovely terrace with shade sails behind the building. N.B. Bill for the whole table only.

Name: Saittavini
Description En: Combining a bistro, wine bar and delicatessen, this friendly restaurant serves Italian food (including a lovely small antipasto counter). They also sell over a 1 000 different wines in the wine shop and a range of Italian specialities in the delicatessen.

Name: Restaurant Baiken by Schröer
Description En: Set amid the vines, and with a magnificent view of the vineyards and Eltville, the location is truly magical. In summer, the terrace is of course very popular. This restaurant run by Dirk Schröer and Amila Begic-Schröer is part of the Kloster Eberbach wine estate on the Rauenthaler Baiken. The chef adheres to a strictly classical and fuss-free style of cooking, showcasing outstanding, impeccably fresh ingredients, as in the saddle of venison in a bread crust with wild mushrooms, apricot and pointed cabbage. You can order à la carte or choose from different set menus, for example, the enticing and reasonably priced three-course "Afterwork Menu" (including wine and water) on Mon, Thu and Fri. The wine list is dominated by the Hessische Staatsweingüter wine estates. The decor is tastefully understated and attentive service comes courtesy of a front-of-house team who are friendly, professional and always on hand – pleasant atmosphere guaranteed.

Name: Mon Amie Maxi
Address: Bockenheimer Landstraße 31, Frankfurt on the Main, 60325, Germany
Description En: Housed in a villa dating from 1925, this restaurant is chic, almost opulent – the wonderfully lively atmosphere is complemented by friendly, attentive and adept service. To the side is Raw Bar, and there is an open kitchen. The menu features typical Parisian brasserie dishes, ranging from the classic seafood platter and French onion soup to kidneys or entrecôte with a peppercorn sauce. Good, exclusive wine selection.

Name: Gasthaus Landbrecht
Description En: Set in the tranquil hamlet of Haindlfing, this family-run country inn has been in operation for more than 100 years and is now helmed by fifth-generation chef-patron Maximilian Landbrecht. Dedicated to working with select regional ingredients, often sourced from organic producers, he presents flavoursome, meticulously prepared dishes that celebrate local produce with occasional Mediterranean accents. Notable examples include Ampertal beef broth with toasted farmhouse bread and brown onion, and pan-seared Freising brook trout with herb butter, a vegetable medley and sautéed potatoes. Both the Gaststube and the more elegant Esszimmer (dining room), which features a lovely tiled stove, provide a cosy setting; in summer, the terrace beckons. A bright ballroom and the rustic Wirts Chalet can be booked for private functions. Smart modern apartments available for overnight stays.

Name: Eiflers Zeiten
Description En: The pleasant, rustic-style alternative to Bembergs Häuschen has a distinctly cosy feel. The menu features mouthwatering regional classics such as roast Eifel beef with roast potatoes, as well as internationally influenced dishes such as cod with a lemon crunch topping and Chinese cabbage. There are also daily changing specials. The two chandeliers fashioned from bottles are sure to draw the eye! The view through the windowed façade onto the pond is also lovely.

Name: Landhaus am See
Description En: The lakeside setting, nestled in lush greenery, is altogether exceptional – particularly if you dine on the terrace with views across the magnificent garden to the water. Inside, the decor is equally lovely, featuring tasteful and welcoming country-house-style decor. The kitchen emphasises seasonal and regional sourcing, with dishes that are meticulously prepared and full of flavour. Choose from the enticing à la carte selection or compose your own set menu. For overnight stays, there are charming, individually appointed guestrooms.

Name: WEINreich
Description En: A modern take on the traditional wine tavern in a tranquil little village. The historical setting has been given a makeover including attractive decorative touches: alongside the numerous wine bottles on display, the ceiling is adorned with a depiction of the wine route marked with its famous wine villages. In summer, the courtyard terrace is a wonderful spot. The dedicated team led by Jeanette and Henning Weinheimer provides very friendly, professional service. Their high-quality regional and seasonal cuisine is full of flavour and character – and pairs well with local wine. Diners can order à la carte or choose between two set menus – one with three courses, the other with four. Meat-eaters should ask about their "Steak Weeks"; Sunday roast is available if pre-ordered. House-baked bread can also be purchased to take away. For overnight stays, there are lovely guestrooms.

Name: Schmidt's
Description En: This restaurant is housed in the Hellerauer Werkstätten für Handwerkskunst (a workshop founded in 1909 by Karl Schmidt). Served in a modern bistro atmosphere, the classically based food has seasonal and regional influences, and is made with carefully selected ingredients, which are prepared for maximum flavour and minimum fuss. Having difficulty deciding? Then go for the surprise menu ("Schmidt's Karte rauf und runter"). The affordable lunch deal goes down a treat, and the terrace is also lovely.

Name: Köllner's Landhaus
Description En: Set in grounds covering 11 000m² this charming half-timbered house dating from 1589 is a picture-book property with a country house-style interior that certainly does it justice. Then there is the excellent regional and international cuisine. You might also choose to spend the night in one of the comfortable and modern guestrooms.

Name: St. Urban
Description En: Along with the fine dining restaurant Schwarzer Hahn, St. Urban is part of the appealing culinary microcosm of the lovely Deidesheimer Hof hotel, which is located right on the historical market square. The cosy interior exudes the traditional charm of a Palatinate inn. Good regional and seasonal cuisine is served, à la carte or as a set menu. The menu also includes the classic "Palatinate Favourite – Saumagen (stuffed pig's stomach), Bratwurst and liver dumplings with sauerkraut and mashed potatoes".

Name: Zucker
Description En: The name sort of gives it away if you have any German: This attractive modern brasserie is housed in a former sugar factory, now a listed building. Exposed red brick walls and high ceilings give the setting an appealing industrial feel. In summer, the terrace is shaded by awnings. Flavoursome seasonally inspired dishes are served à la carte, with an additional set menu available. The waitstaff are pleasantly down-to-earth, very friendly and well organised.

Name: Reussenstein
Description En: Everything here is "100% Swabian". All the ingredients come from Württemberg, and the menu is entirely dedicated to regional fare. If you are ordering à la carte, you pick your main dish by its key ingredient (eg beef, game or freshwater fish) and it comes served on a special ash wood tiered platter that was custom-made for the restaurant. The glass partition means there are interesting glimpses into the kitchen, plus the service is very cordial. The vaulted cellar houses a further restaurant, Wild, where a seasonal set menu featuring game is served on Friday evenings. At dinnertime Tue-Thu, this menu is available exclusively for small groups. Their novel "Spätzle Drive-in" is open throughout the day. This long-standing family business also has cosy modern guestrooms.

Name: Krone
Description En: This long-standing family business is run with real dedication. No compromises are made when it comes to the quality of the produce, and the dishes taste great! No wonder the restaurant is widely known and popular – this also means it is better to make a reservation. Tip: the very reasonably priced lunch menu.

Name: der allerKrug
Description En: Here at der allerKrug with its friendly hosts Sven Hütten and Petra Tiecke-Hütten, you can look forward to carefully and skilfully prepared dishes. The dishes are based on country cuisine with international influences, plus there’s an attractive terrace to the rear of the restaurant.

Name: Leopold
Description En: This lavishly converted stable of the Von Winning winery (part of the Bassermann-Jordan empire) is an impressively modern and extremely popular restaurant that serves excellent food. The menu includes a selection of international and Palatinate dishes. Lovely terrace. It can also be booked as a fantastic location for events. The restaurant was named after Leopold von Winning, founder of the winery.

Name: Kucher's Weinwirtschaft
Description En: The mismatched antique tables and chairs, the pretty decoration and the almost familial atmosphere lend this place a charming feel. The Swabian-style sour kidneys with sautéed potatoes have been on the menu here forever – a classic with its own loyal following. In addition, the menu includes contemporary dishes such as braised Ellscheid lemon chicken with Mediterranean vegetables. Most of the meat used by Florian Kucher and his team to create their seasonal regional fare comes from the Eifel area. Be sure to peruse the wine list – wine is a passion of senior chef Martin Kucher and he will be happy to advise you.

Name: Restaurant 1718
Description En: At 1718, elegant period architectural elements blend beautifully with modern design. Part of Ketschauer Hof hotel, the restaurant sits across from the fine dining restaurant L.A. Jordan – separating them is a lovely terrace in the peaceful, verdant courtyard. On the menu, French and international cuisine are the order of the day, accompanied by a superb selection of wines from the Palatinate and beyond. Tip: The establishment runs a wine shop around the corner.

Name: Bergfriedel
Description En: This establishment has been run by the same family with great dedication for years! The welcoming team serves delicious, fresh food that diners can enjoy as they take in the views over the Bühlertal. They follow a philosophy that is close to nature - and their own chickens in the garden fit in nicely. The wide-ranging menu includes traditional cuisine from Baden, vegetarian/vegan dishes and gourmet specialities. Add to that an extensive wine list. The chic restaurant extension is done out in a modern take on regional style. Pleasant overnight accommodation is available – the rooms and suites ("Natur-Zimmer" and "Natur-Suiten") are done out in locally sourced materials and are contemporary in their design.

Name: Schapers
Description En: A family-run place where you will be treated to friendly and cordial service. As for the food, you can look forward to ambitious classic cuisine brimming with regional influences. Choose from the à la carte offering or the set menus drawn from it, which include a vegetarian set menu. The terrace is lovely. Should you wish to stay overnight, there are comfortable and convenient guestrooms available, distributed over two buildings.

Name: Berchtesgadener Esszimmer
Description En: This long-established inn run by Maximilian and Roxana Kühbeck with great dedication has bags of character. As the charming couple work alone, service can occasionally take a little longer, but this only enhances the pleasingly warm atmosphere. Their seasonal dishes are made with carefully selected ingredients from the immediate area – herbs, for instance, are foraged, or harvested from their own organic garden. There are two set menus, one of which is vegetarian, plus an à la carte selection. In addition to the cosy little dining space with its vaulted ceiling, there are two very popular "Kitchen Tables" for those who wish to see the chefs at work.

Name: Behl's Restaurant
Description En: The dedication of the Behl family is palpable whether you're staying in their Genusshotel with its cheerful and cosy guestrooms or dining in the restaurant, complete with charming shaded courtyard terrace. You can look forward to a welcoming atmosphere and delicious dishes made with locally sourced produce such as Blankenbach brook trout or Spessart pasture-raised beef. They also host regular Brennabende ("spirit evenings") in the distillery, including a set menu with spirit pairings and a demonstration.

Name: Stubersheimer Hof
Description En: The tasteful decor of this lovingly restored old farmhouse exudes rural charm. In the inviting wood-floored traditional dining room, Gabi Laib and her team provide friendly and attentive service, while junior proprietor Martina takes charge in the kitchen. She prepares regional and internationally influenced dishes such as monkfish with lemon foam and saffron risotto, or braised cheeks of Swabian-Hall free-range pork, as well as traditional Zwiebelrostbraten (sirloin steak with crispy fried onions and gravy) with spaetzle. In summer, there's no better place to dine than in the charming courtyard. This family-run business also has lovely guestrooms for those wishing to stay overnight, as well as spaces that can be booked for private functions.

Name: Forellenhof
Description En: The diversity of the Bareiss culinary empire knows no bounds! The historic and idyllically located Forellenhof has been transformed into a charming restaurant open to all-comers from 11:30 am to 5: 30 pm, Fridays from 11:30 am. to 10 pm. The emphasis here is on freshwater fish – from their own fish farm – but they also serve snacks. Tip: you can buy fresh fish in the Forellenlädle (9am-noon).

Name: GRACE
Description En: "The place to be" in Berlin! A really appealing and stylish restaurant that oozes glamour and counts Hollywood stars among its patrons. Dishes with Asian-Californian and European flavours are served. A must: after the meal, a cocktail in the rooftop bar lounge! The restaurant is located in the tasteful, high-quality designed "Hotel Zoo" in a great location directly on Kurfürstendamm.

Name: INDIA CLUB
Description En: Authentic Indian cuisine is to be found in Berlin! At India Club, the self-styled "rustic cuisine" with its roots in North India includes delicious curries and original tandoori dishes, as well as numerous vegetarian and vegan options. In addition to the appealing à la carte menu, the three-course surprise menu is highly recommended, as it gives a good overview of this style of cuisine. Many ingredients are sourced from the restaurant's own organic farm (Gut Vorder Bollhagen) on the Baltic Sea. With its mahogany furniture, dark wood panelling, bright colours and traditional patterns, the elegant interior has an almost festive atmosphere and exudes Indian flair. The restaurant is located not far from the Brandenburg Gate, at the rear of the exclusive Hotel Adlon.

Name: Rolin
Description En: Elegant ambience, friendly service, tasty and ambitious international, classic and seasonal cuisine – on the menu e. g. fillet of North Sea cod with a horseradish, honey and rosemary crust. Incidentally, "Rolin" is the name of a ship's captain. Hotel Cap Polonio has well-kept rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Beesten
Description En: Since 1906, over four generations, the Beesten family has put its heart and soul into running this traditional inn in the heart of Rheine. The owner himself is at the helm in the kitchen, preparing classic French and German cuisine peppered with seasonal influences. The interior is elegant and tasteful, while the service is charming. Take a seat on the terrace under the lovely old chestnut trees.

Name: Koch und Kellner
Description En: A cornerstone of the Nuremberg fine dining scene. The set menu, written up on a large board, comprises nine courses, but for those with a smaller appetite, it can also be shortened. The dishes are crafted from carefully selected ingredients and are quite aptly described as "modernised classics". Besides the chef, owner and waiter Frank Mackert is always on hand with his inimitable Franconian charm. Thanks to his extensive wine expertise, he can confidently guide you through the 500-label list. Clear lines, a warm colour palette and parquet flooring make for a lovely setting. By reservation only: Mon-Sat lunchtime (11.30am-2.30pm).

Name: Alte Mühle
Description En: This friendly, well-run restaurant with its appealingly pared-back style adjoins the historical building of a grain mill, which has been converted into guest accommodation. Service is provided by attentive and professional staff, as you tuck into Mediterranean, regional and seasonal cuisine. In addition to à la carte dishes, a set menu is also available.

Name: Stumpenhof
Description En: It's impossible not to feel comfortable when you're in such good hands! The service in this long-standing family business is exceptionally friendly, and the owner herself always has a smile and a friendly word for her guests. The menu has something for everyone, from affordable lunch set menus and daily specials to traditional regional dishes and light bites. Lovely terrace.

Name: Lumperhof
Description En: This family-run inn is a lovely spot in the countryside and has a charming terrace shaded by a majestic old lime tree. The menu is varied and full of delicious options. Made with regional and seasonal produce, the dishes draw on Mediterranean, Middle Eastern and Asian influences. Options such as the cream of sweetcorn soup with deep-fried mussels and purple curry, or the Allgäu cheese spaetzle with melted onions and a green salad are sure to whet the appetite. In the evening, you can dine à la carte or opt for a set menu comprising three or five courses. Cash payments only.

Name: Culinarium
Description En: This chic, pared-back restaurant with a lovely terrace area is located in the Weingut Matthias Dostert, a winery that also offers cosy guestrooms. Chef Walter Curman draws on his considerable craftsmanship to meticulously create flavoursome dishes. The classics on the menu hint at his Austrian origins – try the appetising Kaspressknödel (pressed cheese dumplings) or Alt Wiener Kaiserschmarrn (Viennese pancake)!

Name: Die Halde
Description En: At an elevation of 1 147m, this elegant restaurant effortlessly bridges the gap between the old and the new! In cosy traditional dining rooms, friendly and professional waitstaff serve dishes such as medium-rare topside of veal with coleslaw, pickled onions, chive cream and mustard gherkins, or pan-fried cod fillet with gremolata, asparagus, pea purée and gnocchi. The menu also features Zwiebelrostbraten (sirloin steak with crispy fried onions and gravy), schnitzel and other classics. The kitchen prioritises regional ingredients, and the water comes straight from the property's own mountain spring. The lovely guestrooms are done out in a modern, regional style.

Name: freistil.
Description En: In addition to an appealing modern decor featuring sleek design and warm wooden fittings, diners can look forward to a selection of regional and seasonal dishes (including vegetarian and vegan options) that can be put together to create a set menu or ordered à la carte. For overnight stays, the boutique hotel has attractive, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Sülbecker Krug
Description En: Calling all steak lovers! This restaurant is known for its exceptional cuts of meat, which are cooked in an oven heated to 800°C. The menu features rib-eye, flank steak and tenderloin – and each piece is served on a wooden board, with superb sauces. Alternatively, there is a three-course set menu ("Menü Heimat") or four-course "Sülbecker Steak Menu"; as for the à la carte selection, the classic "Sülbecker Krüstchen" is particularly popular. Freshly fried North Sea sole meunière is another good option. They also have a wine bar. Various special offers are to be had throughout the year – don't hesitate to enquire!

Name: Gasthaus Sternen Post
Description En: Since 2006, Bernd Lutz and his wife Rosemarie have been welcoming guests to their charming inn dating back to 1875. The chef-patron and his team serve up flavoursome classic seasonal dishes (eg cured salmon with pearl barley, beetroot and horseradish, or pan-fried veal sweetbreads with leaf spinach and spaetzle (a Swabian pasta speciality) made using a wealth of locally sourced produce. The appealing wine list features a well-curated selection of local vintages. Charming interior; gorgeous terrace. The service, led by the proprietress, is exceptionally friendly and attentive. For those wishing to stay overnight, cosy guestrooms and an attractive holiday apartment are available.

Name: Torkel
Description En: The Stoppel family serve not only cuisine underpinned by Mediterranean and classic influences, but also plenty of regional dishes. If you are having trouble choosing, a failsafe option is the short "Fine Dining Menü". It's also well worth perusing the wine list. Sit back and enjoy your meal in the inviting dining space or out on the pretty terrace. The hotel of the same name has lovely cosy guestrooms.

Name: Sternenschanz
Description En: A fun dining experience! The Linck family - now in its fourth generation - put their heart and soul into running this delightful restaurant. Diners can look forward to friendly service and the chance to eat really well without breaking the bank. The menu focuses on Swabian fare and home-style cooking, with dishes such as Flädlesuppe (pancake soup) and creamy veal goulash. No wonder there are so many regulars! In summer, the gorgeous garden terrace beckons.

Name: Hermannshöhle
Description En: Set in a former ferry house dating back to 1517, this establishment has been run by Wigbert Weck since 2007 and has a loyal following of regulars. The dishes created by the chef-patron are skillfully prepared from fresh ingredients with no unnecessary embellishments, and they are delicious! Tip: the surprise menu (only for the whole table). Complete with a glass-fronted wine refrigerator full of regional wines, the interior has the feel of a modern wine bar. Outside, the lovely terrace overlooks the Nahe River, which is just across the road. Two holiday flats can be booked for overnight stays.

Name: Postschänke
Description En: With its cosy and lively atmosphere, Postschänke is a fantastic alternative to Zur Post, the fine-dining restaurant. Here, the delicious seasonal cuisine made with select, fresh ingredients goes down a treat. They serve a daily set menu with options, as well as daily specials. The service is exceedingly friendly and attentive.

Name: Spinne
Address: Eichkehle 58, Neustadt an der Weinstraße, 67433, Germany
Description En: This restaurant situated on the forest's edge sticks to a simple winning formula, with a focus on regional and seasonal cuisine prepared using the finest ingredients. Perhaps you'd like to try the surprise menu? Take a seat out on the lovely terrace. Welcoming and modern guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: Hackbarth's Restaurant
Description En: In the trendy, chic interior behind the red front door, a welcoming team and attentive service await you. The modern cuisine combines regional and international elements, Mediterranean and Far Eastern influences and seasonal produce. In addition to the à la carte selection, there is a five-course surprise menu. The tapas menu served on Tue and Thu is worth checking out. Nicely curated wine list. Lovely terrace. Tip: It is advisable to make a reservation for the weekend (Fri and Sat).

Name: DAS BERNHARDS
Description En: The Bernhard family's centrally located restaurant is cosy in its rustic charm, attracting many regular guests who appreciate both the cordial, attentive service and the excellent food. The menu features regional and seasonal dishes alongside Swiss classics such as "Züri Gschnätzlets – veal strips, creamy mushroom sauce, cognac, authentic Swiss rösti", reflecting the family's Graubünden roots. The daily specials are especially popular at lunch. The terrace is lovely in summer.

Name: Zirbelstube
Description En: The journey to this friendly family-run establishment on the outskirts of Nuremberg is well worthwhile. Set in a smart sandstone building (1860), Zirbelstube boasts an attractive main dining space and a separate room with a vaulted ceiling. They serve good regional and seasonal cuisine with classical and international influences in the form of two set menus featuring dishes you can mix and match, such as pan-fried octopus with fennel and beans, labneh and olive tapenade, or Franconian Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast), red cabbage and cranberry salad, dried fruit and bread dumplings. Delightful terrace. Attractive guestrooms.

Name: Novalis
Description En: Diners can opt to eat inside, in the stylish, elegant restaurant, or outside with a view of the historical castle grounds. The seasonal food is positively packed with flavours and aromas, and made with top-notch produce – regional wherever possible – such as game that they have hunted themselves or smoked fish from Leinetal. There is also a vegetarian set menu. The service is cordial and professional. Tip: The wine list comprises a broad selection of French red wines, alongside gin, korn schnapps, vodka and whiskey from the restaurant's own Hardenberg Distillery. "Novalis" comes from an ancestor of the owners – it is the pseudonym of writer Georg Philipp Friedrich Freiherr von Hardenberg. Hardenberg BurgHotel promises an overnight stay in tasteful accommodation.

Name: Gaststube Zum Klosterbräu
Address: Kirchplatz 1, Neuburg an der Donau, 86633, Germany
Description En: This is how you imagine a historical Bavarian restaurant: wooden beams on the ceiling, floorboards, tiled stove – rustic, inviting and wonderfully cosy (or "zünftig" as they say in these parts). There is also a wonderful terrace. The cuisine is classic, regional and seasonal – served à la carte or in three set menus, one of which is vegetarian. There is a good selection of wines to choose from. Tip: well-priced lunch menu with two or three courses (Tues. to Fri., except public holidays). You can also visit the Baroque Münster Heilig Kreuz in Bergen.

Name: Burg Nideggen - Kaiserblick
Description En: This eatery is a good alternative to the Brockel Schlimbach restaurant at Nideggen's centuries-old castle, Burg Nideggen. They serve market-based cuisine in the form of regional dishes, prepared from fresh seasonal ingredients mainly sourced from suppliers and producers in the region. The interior decor is modern and the front-of-house team is very friendly and obliging. Weather permitting, you can dine on the pretty terrace in the castle courtyard.

Name: Stüffel
Description En: The riverside location right by the Isekai is every bit as appealing as the contemporary seasonal cuisine with Mediterranean and regional influences, made with choice ingredients. The menu includes, for example, Husum pasture-raised beef tartare, or poached cod with balsamic lentils, as well as classics such as beef fillet and lobster ravioli. The wine list is well chosen – the chef will be happy to guide you. You can eat in the stylish modern bistro or outside on the waterfront. There is also a wine bar in the building.

Name: Herzog von Burgund
Description En: First you admire the attractive exterior of this stylish townhouse. Then, inside, the impressive, heritage-protected staircase. The two dining spaces (Erftzimmer and Gartenzimmer) form a classically elegant setting – the paintings by Düsseldorf artist Markus Tollmann draw the eye. The menu has a seasonal focus, and Wiener schnitzel is a house speciality. Friendly and experienced waitstaff. Delightful outdoor seating: The terrace is a verdant oasis in the heart of the city!

Name: Wirtshaus zur Sonne
Description En: This restaurant has been in the same family for over 300 years. Diners can sit inside in the wonderful, wood-panelled dining room or outside on the pretty garden terrace to enjoy the flavoursome fare. This includes tafelspitz (boiled topside of beef) galantine with radish carpaccio or pan-fried skrei cod with tomatoes and herbs.

Name: Husar
Description En: Charming dining rooms await behind the painted façade of this inn, which has stood for over 400 years. Here, diners are treated to attentive service as they tuck into classic cuisine. The dishes are packed with flavour and made with good-quality ingredients; attention is paid to seasonality, and a regional produce is given preferential treatment. Started in 1986, the Merget family business continues today, having resumed in 2004 after a brief hiatus.

Name: GRILL
Description En: In this restaurant housed in Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten by Hamburg's Inner Alster lake, Caucasian walnut wood, warm colours such as olive green and pigeon blue, along with a log fire create an elegant yet cosy setting that harmoniously blends traditional and modern elements. On the menu: seafood specialities such as oysters and lobster, along with classics such as steak tartare and special cuts of meat cooked in the Southbend infrared broiler.

Name: Gasthaus Adler
Description En: Savour classic Baden fare with French and international influences in these cosy, quintessentially "Black Forest" dining rooms. In winter, for example, the game and goose dishes are popular. In summer, there is outside seating in the Adler Gärtle. The service is friendly and there are comfortable guestrooms, some simpler than others.

Name: H'manns
Description En: The Hegmanns run this genuinely charming restaurant that is a hit with diners. Only the best produce makes its way into the dishes, which are meticulously prepared to bring out the full flavour of the ingredients. On Fri-Sun, two four- to eight-course seasonal set menus, one of which is vegetarian, are served. On Mon, tapas menu only – to be washed down with something from the promising wine selection. Extremely friendly waitstaff. Tip: The chef's table is very close to the kitchen but sheltered from the thick of the action.

Name: Das Esszimmer
Address: Hintergasse 38, Neustadt an der Weinstraße, 67433, Germany
Description En: A lovely restaurant in the Old Town: the welcoming, sleek and modern setting is bound to appeal, and the atmosphere is pleasantly intimate, the service is attentive and well trained. You can watch Italian/Mediterranean dishes being prepared in the open kitchen. Look out for the "speciality days". On Thursdays: tasting menu only. The terrace in front of the house is also a pleasant place to sit.

Name: Spitzweg
Description En: This place has been serving up consistently good food for years – there's a reason why it attracts so many regulars. On the menu: seasonal, regional and international dishes. The sleek, modern decor boasting a bold red colour scheme and paintings on the walls is stylish. Friendly and professional service. The lively terrace set up on the pavement is a lovely place to sit. There is also an annexe for private events.

Name: Ostaria da Gino
Description En: This delightful family-run restaurant's enduring popularity among regulars is a testament to the unwavering dedication and passion that have been poured into its operations for the past 40 years. Authentic Italian cuisine is served in a laid-back setting with bags of charm! Staff will be happy to guide you through the options written up on the board and recommend the right wine. Tip: the moderately priced lunch deal. Delicatessen goods can be purchased to take home.

Name: Der Kaiserhof
Description En: Run by the same family for four generations, Kaiserhof has a surprisingly chic and fresh interior behind its deceptively traditional façade. The tastefully designed dining space is accessed via the open kitchen – diners can also watch the chefs at work. The concept here is a seasonally orientated "Culinary Journey" in six courses – for which you should allow plenty of time. Vegetarian dishes such as aubergine with pointed cabbage and Parmesan are just as enticing as the duck with Savoy cabbage and blackcurrant. Friendly and attentive front-of-house team. The chefs are involved in serving and talk you through the dishes. In summer, head for the terrace in the small courtyard. There are well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Jagstmühle
Description En: With its cosy yet elegant interior and charming terrace, the restaurant blends seamlessly into the romantic setting of this estate on the banks of the Jagst. Light wood panelling, a tiled stove and pretty fabrics all create an inviting sense of warmth and comfort. Cordial and attentive service also contributes to the lovely atmosphere. The cooking follows the seasons and incorporates international influences. Diners can choose from an appealing à la carte menu. Good to know: The restaurant also opens for lunch at weekends. Tip: Before or after your meal, take a stroll through the beautiful grounds. Cosy guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Lamm
Description En: A tasteful, modern interior incorporating a sleek design, premium materials and warm tones goes hand in hand with the hospitality of a traditional inn. The menu whets the appetite with an interesting array of regional and international dishes, such as roast Angus beef served with two kinds of onions, warm potato salad and maultaschen>/i> (Swabian dumplings) sautéed in butter or Barbary duck breast accompanied by stir-fried Asian vegetables and Himalayan basmati rice. The five different set menus, which include a vegan one, are also excellent. A very popular establishment – book early if you are looking to come at the weekend!

Name: Rive Fish & Faible
Description En: Sitting right on the port, this bistro is run by the same team as Tschebull. It serves good quality, flavoursome seafood and grilled meats alongside classic dishes such as Hamburger Pannfisch and Wiener Schnitzel. In summer the wonderful terrace is a must! Hot food served throughout the day.

Name: Rüssel's Hasenpfeffer
Description En: This excellent alternative to Rüssel'schen fine dining restaurant is very popular with guests! Here in the left-hand side of this attractive country house, the buzzy atmosphere is pleasingly laid-back; the tasty food is made using good-quality ingredients. Classic cuisine with regional influences can be enjoyed as a set menu or à la carte – game and braised meat are among the favourites.

Name: heyligenstaedt
Description En: The high ceilings, steel girders, large mullioned windows and sections of exposed brick wall show a conscious effort to retain some of the industrial charm of this old factory building: these features have been merged into the chic, modern design. The tasty cuisine has international and seasonal roots; smaller menu at lunchtime. Friendly service, and the adjoining boutique hotel has trendy guestrooms and rooftop sauna area.

Name: Jennerwein
Address: Münchner Straße 127, Gmund am Tegernsee, 83703, Germany
Description En: A truly delightful establishment with a charmingly rustic inn atmosphere – it's genuinely cosy here. The menu includes freshly prepared seasonal Bavarian cuisine such as braised shoulder of lamb with root vegetables, or beef tenderloin on a bed of fried mushrooms and potatoes, as well as parmesan risotto with king prawns. More limited options at lunchtime.

Name: Schillingshof
Description En: Schillingshof has been around since 1648. The family business takes pride in providing first-rate hospitality. Behind the spruce half-timbered façade, you will find an elegant interior where diners enjoy attentive and cordial service and, last but not least, classic cuisine. Made using carefully selected ingredients, the dishes are pared down to the essentials. There are various set menus and tempting à la carte options such as confit char on a bed of mussel risotto with lime foam, or veal fillet "saltimbocca" with rosemary gnocchi, vegetables and sauce divine. The wine list is also fantastic – sometimes, a Mediterranean antipasti platter and a good bottle of wine are all you need. Lovely guestrooms.

Name: Posthörnle
Description En: This casual, minimalist-style little restaurant is housed in one of the oldest taverns in the town. It serves fresh, seasonal cuisine with dishes ranging from venison rissoles with black mustard to pan-fried zander with oranges and chicory.

Name: STRAUCHS FALCO
Description En: This smart and stylish restaurant is next to the Maritime Museum. Situated in the Elbarkaden in the middle of HafenCity, it also boasts an appealing terrace. The kitchen offers a broad international selection ranging from grilled dishes and Mediterranean fare, such as fish and shellfish soup, to German classics like Labskaus (corned beef and potato mash) and Wiener schnitzel, as well as pasta dishes. Tip: Come with friends and choose dishes to share so that you can sample a wider variety. Also recommended: Bar & Deli.

Name: Wirtshaus zum Herrmannsdorfer Schweinsbräu
Description En: "Dishes that can't be pigeonholed" – such is the name of the game for chef Olimpia Cario. In her surprise set menu, she gives free rein to her creativity, cooking up unusual combinations such as chicken, trout, egg, cucumber, corn and redcurrants. She uses seasonal produce and high-quality ingredients, often grown on her own farm. The interior itself has an eye-catching design, with a large, high-ceilinged space reminiscent of a modern rustic barn on account of the beam construction climbing up into the roof.

Name: Zur Krone
Description En: The Isele family has been cultivating the art of hospitality in this traditional building since 1854. The interior boasts a pleasant atmosphere in which to enjoy classic German cuisine that is seasonal, carefully prepared and based on a range of regional ingredients. The home-made terrines and desserts are definitely worth trying – the diet will have to wait! The wine list also has a very regional slant. In addition, there are comfortable, tastefully decorated guestrooms in which you will be tempted to stay for more than one night!

Name: L'arte in cucina
Description En: This attractive restaurant opposite the Basilika St. Margareta is a rare example of an authentic Italian ristorante, where the cuisine of Tuscany is served with love and culinary flair. Specialities from the chef's Tuscan homeland such as gnudi (a kind of gnocchi) or "Il Coniglio" (rabbit). The pasta is house-made.

Name: Hopmanns Olive
Description En: With great dedication, the Hopmanns have been running this friendly, sleek, modern restaurant for over 20 years – Ingo heads up the kitchen; Petra is in charge front of house. Based on classical foundations, the cuisine is seasonal and draws on Mediterranean inspirations. One of the classics is, for example, gently braised lamb shank. In summer, you can also take advantage of the gorgeous terrace. Tip: The adjoining historical engine shed is an ideal location to book for events.

Name: Basho-An
Description En: Located near the pedestrian zone, this restaurant is a popular spot for authentic Japanese cuisine. If you want to avoid disappointment, be sure to make your reservations in good time! The decor is characteristically minimalist; there are also a few seats at the sushi counter. Tip: the reasonably priced lunchtime set menu. The options for dinner are wider ranging. At both lunchtime and in the evening, vegetarian dishes are also available. The wine list also includes sake, of course, and some regional wines.

Name: Zum Goldenen Anker
Description En: Not only does this 18C hotel offer a comfortable stay (opt for one of the newer guestrooms), it is also a popular modern take on a rural restaurant. Diners are waited on by a friendly front-of-house team in an attractive modern setting with a rustic touch. The food is flavoursome, fresh and seasonal. The main courses are also available in smaller portions. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace to the rear of the building.

Name: Torschänke
Description En: Right next to the Obertor (the historical city gate), Torschänke is a really inviting restaurant. The atmosphere inside is cosy and pleasingly down to earth, and outside there is a lovely, leafy terrace. Dishes with French and Mediterranean influences are prepared using top-notch fresh produce and served by a friendly, attentive and proficient front-of-house team.

Name: La Cuisine Mario Kalweit
Description En: A nicely restored building from the late 19th century houses this stylish, modern, elegant restaurant serving creative cuisine. Pleasant terrace.

Name: Zu den drei Linden - Lindenblüte
Description En: Tanja and Thomas Siemes run their family business with great dedication, and the food here is exceptional. He cooks up international cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons and incorporates Mediterranean and regional influences; she provides charming service. You can opt for the set menu or order dishes à la carte, such as the mouthwatering crispy fried loup de mer with spinach and Carmague rice. The atmosphere is friendly and the decor has an elegant Mediterranean feel.

Name: Kölbl
Description En: Plenty of regulars come here to enjoy the regional and international cuisine served à la carte or in the form of a four-course set menu – a vegetarian version is also available. Diners can sit in one of the cosy dining rooms or on the courtyard terrace to enjoy the seasonal dishes. The guestrooms are ideal for overnight stays.

Name: Sette Feinbistro
Description En: Somewhat tucked away in the pedestrian precinct, this gem has been run with great dedication by the Tegge family for many years. The name "Feinbistro" encompasses both a delicatessen and a restaurant serving Mediterranean and regional cuisine. Breakfast is also available. Don't forget to purchase delicacies such as jam, cheese and wine etc from the shop to enjoy at home.

Name: MAXIME de Guy Graessel
Description En: An appealing modern restaurant with an intimate atmosphere. Chef-patron Guy Graessel, who hails from Alsace, specialises in classic fare from Alsace and Baden. Diner choose between the five-course surprise menu (for two or more people) and à la carte dishes. For al fresco dining, there are tables in the charming verdant garden courtyard. Drinks are also served on the terrace in the pedestrian precinct Tip: Located in the entrance area, Café Hesselbacher has house-made cakes, tarts and pastries for sale at the weekend, over the counter or pre-ordered. For motorists, there is a car park – Parkhaus Löwenhof – not far from the restaurant.

Name: Zum Goldenen Pflug
Description En: In one of the oldest inns in the region, tradition is celebrated, but not at the expense of progress. There are a number of charming dining areas in which to enjoy dishes such as Rindertafelspitz aus dem Kupferpfandl (boiled beef fillet from the copper pot), apple horseradish, chive sauce, creamed spinach and sautéed potatoes and, for dessert, Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake) with plum compote and whipped cream. Order à la carte or opt for the "Signature Menu" for two or more diners.

Name: ESSperiment
Description En: This restaurant serves up modern cuisine that combines influences from different countries and changes with the seasons. Dine à la carte or opt for a set menu comprising four or six courses. On Sunday evenings, a surprise menu is another appealing option. The clean-lined modern interior design and friendly service make for an inviting atmosphere. The terrace is particularly lovely in summer.

Name: Orania.Berlin
Description En: The restaurant belonging to the lovely hotel that shares its name has a stylish, warm and relaxed ambience. The lobby and bar (with its interesting cocktail menu) are directly adjacent. Modern, creative dishes are sent out of the large open kitchen that draws the eye. Attentive and accomplished service. Try the four-course "Xberg Duck" set menu (min. two people).

Name: alexxanders
Description En: Located in a residential area, this restaurant boasts a stylish interior and a courtyard terrace with a beautifully landscaped little garden. The flavoursome dishes draw inspiration from around the globe and incorporate Mediterranean and seasonal influences. Why not enjoy an aperitif at the bar before your meal? The wine list is also worth a look. Guestrooms with modern interior design are available in the hotel of the same name.

Name: Altdeutsches Restaurant
Description En: Florian Kellerbauer's kitchen philosophy centres on quality ingredients, with a strong commitment to regional and seasonal sourcing. Diners can opt for a set menu – either with meat or vegetarian – comprising four, five or six courses. You can also order à la carte. The service is friendly, attentive and professional. The restaurant occupies a prime spot in the historical centre – Kirche St Georg just opposite is well worth a visit. For overnight stays, there is Hotel Deutsches Haus, a patrician house dating from 1440, or in the Ehemalige Sparkasse, both just 50m away.

Name: Warias Am Markt
Description En: Diners can expect regional and seasonal cuisine that makes use of excellent produce – the daily specials are always a good option. The menu features timeless favourites such as beef carpaccio with pesto and Belper Knolle cheese, or pan-seared fish-of-the-day with potato and cucumber salad. The single five- or nine-course surprise menu served on Friday and Saturday evenings available only by reservation. The restaurant has a convivial atmosphere, and the outdoor terrace is a delightful spot. Conveniently, the establishment has well-kept, light and airy guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Lockstein 1
Description En: This really is a special place: you enter the charming kitchen through the 500-year-old farmhouse, which is run by an established mother-and-daughter team. They inject love and skill into their cooking, which takes the form of a vegetarian set menu comprising fresh dishes made using regional produce. The two pretty holiday flats are also popular.

Name: Rebstock-Stube
Description En: A cosy atmosphere reigns in this lovely inn run by the Frey family. The decor is inviting, with dark wood panelling and neatly laid tables at which the classic cuisine of chef Axel Frey is served. Dishes such as "pike dumplings, leaf spinach, lobster sauce" or "boiled veal 'pink', Maultasche (German raviolo), braised vegetables, herb velouté" make an impression with their flavour and quality. You can choose à la carte or opt for a set menu. The wine list is also definitely worth a look! The service is friendly and attentive. The terrace is wonderful for those summer days. Tip: Visit the local history museum next door.

Name: Landhaus Gräfenthal
Description En: Steeped in tradition, this establishment has a solid reputation in the area. Peter Lauterbach represents the fourth generation to run this family restaurant in an idyllic location. The food is a contemporary take on regional, seasonal cuisine and influenced by Mediterranean culinary tradition. Inside, pale wood, a tiled stove and pleasing decorative touches make for an inviting setting; outside there is a beautiful garden terrace. With warm and attentive service, this place has everything it takes to ensure a comfortable dining experience.

Name: Crackers
Description En: You’ll find this trendy eatery one floor below Cookies Cream. Ring the bell and the staff will lead you through the kitchen into a large and lively restaurant with a high ceiling and dim lights. The menu offers a range of ambitious meat and fish dishes.

Name: Schlosskeller
Description En: When it comes to the setting, the lovingly decorated vaulted cellar is really cosy, and the terrace by the castle pond is fantastic! The seasonal cuisine is in a regional vein, ranging from classic Wiener schnitzel to roasted fillet of sea bass with a rosehip foam. They are also open at lunchtime, which is excellent news.

Name: Die Klosterschänke
Description En: Idyllically set a few kilometres from the city centre, this warm and welcoming family-run restaurant boasts a magnificent terrace affording splendid views of the Rhine plain. The chef cooks up regional and seasonal cuisine along with a selection of Italian dishes. The mouthwatering options include a classic cordon bleu with Black Forest ham and Alpine cheese, and saltimbocca alla romana from the chef's homeland.

Name: Le Comptoir
Description En: Located in the Nauwieser Viertel, this restaurant is housed in an old sandstone and brick building, incidentally the birthplace of director Max Ophüls. An attractive modern interior and a friendly atmosphere await you here. The seats at the counter ("le comptoir" in French – hence the name of this establishment) are very popular. In the evenings, a modern seasonal set menu comprising four or five courses is served.

Name: Brauereigasthof Aying
Description En: The restaurant is part of the picture-perfect Brauereigasthof Hotel Aying is a family-run establishment steeped in tradition and now run by the seventh generation. Diners are treated to warm hospitality in an upscale yet cosy setting. The terrace to the rear of the building is delightful in summer. The menu features exquisite regional and seasonal dishes, crafted from carefully selected produce of the highest quality – the restaurant has its own herd of Pinzgau beef cattle, as well as a hunter, who provides the game. In addition to the selection of fine wines, there are of course Ayinger beer specialities. Good event facilities. Comfortable and tastefully decorated guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Brasserie Lamazère
Description En: Ready for a dose of French savoir-vivre in Berlin? You almost feel like you are in France here in the heart of Charlottenburg at Brasserie Lamazère thanks to its charming, down-to-earth and lively atmosphere. The regularly changing seasonal dishes are chalked up on the blackboard. You can put together your menu (starter, main, dessert) from a fine selection. They will be happy to recommend a good French wine pairing to accompany your food – the appealing and reasonably priced wine list is proprietor Régis Lamazère's passion.

Name: Landgasthaus Zum Kreuz
Description En: The appealing alliance of regional and modern influences is omnipresent at the Neumaier family's establishment – whether in the cosy restaurant, the food or the lovely comfortable guestrooms in the Speicher guesthouse next door. Chef-owner Peter Neumaier's sons Lars and Tim are now also involved in the kitchen. The menu features classic and seasonal dishes – be sure to check out the "mini Versucherle" (mini appetisers). You can eat à la carte or choose a set menu – vegetarian options are also available. Owner Michaela Neumaier heads up the team providing friendly service. In summer, the wonderful terrace is the best place to soak up the gorgeous rural location!

Name: Berghofstüble
Description En: This restaurant enjoys a stunning location up above the town. The interior has a pleasing design and there is an attractive conservatory with a pretty terrace outside offering impressive views. The cuisine is based on good, fresh produce with appetising dishes such as Skrei cod on leaf spinach in beurre blanc.

Name: GUI
Description En: It's a good idea to book, because this lively bistro in the middle of town has more than its fair share of regulars! The Mediterranean-inspired cuisine also has regional influences. The quality of the ingredients is first rate, from the fresh pasta with porcini to the cod and the tender venison fillet. The modern interior decor is pleasant – the floor-to-ceiling shelf with decorative wine bottles draws the eye, as does the open kitchen with one striking red wall. In summer, the terrace in the pedestrian area is very inviting. Incidentally, ĝui means "enjoy" in the international language of Esperanto.

Name: Schwarzmatt
Description En: Served à la carte or as a set menu, classic cuisine made with seasonal produce is the order of the day here. The upscale interior is very comfortable, with harmonious, lovingly arranged decorative objects – it certainly does full justice to the luxurious setting of the traditional holiday hotel of the same name in which this restaurant is housed. For overnight stays, there are elegant country-house-style guestrooms – this is after all the sister hotel of Baiersbronn's Hotel Bareiss. Make a beeline for the gorgeous garden terrace in summer. A must in the afternoon: cakes made to Hermine Bareiss's old recipes!

Name: Abt- und Schäferstube
Description En: The location – the beautiful grounds of a centuries-old monastery estate surrounded by nature – is the very epitome of peace and quiet. Oozing historical, rustic charm, the restaurant serves classic, seasonal cuisine with a distinct modern influence. You can order à la carte or opt for the set menu (up to six courses). The service is competent and friendly. The terrace with a view of the Odenwald forest is particularly pleasant, and the well-stocked vaulted wine cellar dating back to 1524 is also worth seeing. For an overnight stay, the Der Schafhof hotel has well-kept guestrooms. Be sure to take a look at the collection of carriages.

Name: WEINrestaurant Ayler Kupp
Description En: While you tuck into the fresh seasonal dishes, which the chefs here cook up with produce from the region, you can take in the vineyards and the lovely garden. There are two set menus, each made up of three to five courses; you can also choose individual dishes à la carte. The wine list includes Riesling from the neighbouring wine estate. They also offer accommodation in inviting, well-kept guestrooms in the hotel.

Name: Gasthaus Assenmacher
Description En: It's clear that Christian and Christa Storch put their heart and soul into running this place. The chef-patron wins over diners with his modern take on classic cuisine. Eschewing any gimmickry, he lays the focus squarely on quality produce and flavour. The lady of the house manages the friendly and attentive waitstaff. Pleasant little terrace to the rear of the building. Decent accommodation options at the hotel.

Name: Die Ratsstuben
Description En: One draw of this restaurant is its beautiful location in the centre of the pretty old town on the Alb River, another is its chic, modern interior. The cuisine is based on high-quality ingredients and ranges from classics such as house-made maultaschen to international specialities such as barbecued octopus and burgers, and not forgetting the various tartare options. The waitstaff are friendly and well trained. In summer, the terrace overlooking the square is a delightful spot where you will be serenaded by the carillon music from the town hall tower.

Name: Trichards
Description En: This chic and modern restaurant-cum-wine bar is located in Munich's Lehel neighbourhood. The owner comes from France, which is reflected in the cooking style. Tip: The "Bouillabaisse-style noble fish and gamba with rouille" is a year-round speciality. The seasonal dishes can be accompanied by your choice from the comprehensive wine list. Ideal for those who like to eat al fresco – the terrace and garden are covered and as such protected from the elements.

Name: SCHORN by Lukas Schild
Description En: With Lukas Schild as chef-patron, this restaurant in the Bilk neighbourhood boasts a big name in the Düsseldorf fine dining scene. Select ingredients go into ambitious seasonal cooking – the dishes draw on the classics. The set menu comes in a four- to seven-course version, or you can take your pick from the à la carte selection. The team is friendly and knowledgeable – the chef comes to your table and talks you through the dishes. The appealing wine list comprises mostly German and French labels. The restaurant has a charming, intimate feel, with decorative features including an old stove, a wine barrel serving as a digestif table and modern paintings. The terrace is lovely in summer.

Name: Müllers auf der Rü
Description En: Nelson Müller's fine dining restaurant, Schote, may have moved to Bergisch Gladbach, but this cherished Essen-based establishment at Rüttenscheider Stern U-Bahn station has stayed put. This is a market hall-style brasserie integrated into a shopping arcade. Sitting at high tables, diners tuck into delicious dishes ranging from currywurst to turbot, prepared in the centrally positioned open kitchen. Friendly service. Tip for motorists: public multi-storey car park around the corner.

Name: Zum Simonbräu
Description En: A down-to-earth pub, just the way we like them! Part of the Bitburger Brewery, this place has an attractive decor of solid wooden tables (no tablecloths here!), walls decorated with pictures, and modern details that foster a pleasantly lively atmosphere. The charming team serves home-style regional dishes, as well as more sophisticated options. Cordon bleu with Eifelschwein pork and "Ōra King salmon – tartare & fried" whet the appetite. The inexpensive dish of the day is popular with the lunchtime crowd. You can also spend the night in one of the spruce guestrooms.

Name: Der Dantler
Description En: A tip to start with: reserve well in advance! Given the great value for money and the relaxed atmosphere, it's no surprise that they tend to get booked up. They call themselves the "Bavarian Deli". In the interior done out in a slick Alpine/country-style style, the service is personable and relaxed. At lunchtime you can order pasta, a pastrami sandwich, ramen or the fish dish of the day à la carte, or the three-course "business lunch". In the evening, creative modern cuisine is served in the form of a set menu – a vegetarian or pescetarian version is also available (request this when you book). There is also a wine bar next door.

Name: Das Esszimmer
Description En: A small, neat house on the outskirts of the city centre houses this pretty restaurant with its modern and minimalist design. The cuisine is also modern; one of the menus is vegetarian. The choice of accompanying beverages includes not only wines but also an alcohol-free alternative. Pleasantly relaxed, friendly and professional service.

Name: Mine
Description En: Very close to Ku'damm, this chic and laid-back establishment is run by a family that already has restaurants in St Petersburg and Moscow. The premises actually used to be home to Berlin's smallest bar. A charming pavement terrace beckons in front of the restaurant. Their Italian cuisine (including classics such as vitello tonnato or pasta) also draws on international and seasonal influences. Opt for the "Greatest Hits" set menu (two or more people) for a tempting selection of dishes. Nicely curated wine list. The wine cellar can also be booked for private dinners or chef's table events.

Name: Carte blanche
Address: Egenolffstraße 39, Frankfurt on the Main, 60316, Germany
Description En: As the name "Carte Blanche" suggests, there is no fixed menu here; instead a surprise six-course menu is served – and a four-course version is also available Wed-Thu. Wine pairings for the individual courses are available upon request. The cuisine is modern and seasonal – the summery tomato salad with mackerel ceviche or the charcoal-grilled sturgeon are tempting options. The emphasis is on artisanal craftsmanship; even the bread is made in-house. The restaurant boasts a lovely location in an attractive historical building on a corner plot with high ceilings decorated with moulding, and unique interior details that contribute to a charming atmosphere.

Name: Valentin
Description En: Tucked away in a small side street of the island's historic centre, this restaurant is housed in a lovely vaulted cellar. In an attractive, modern setting, you can enjoy seasonally inspired cuisine made from high-quality ingredients, presented as an appealing, concise à la carte selection. Service is provided by a friendly team. The intimate courtyard terrace is a pleasant spot, and the wine bar is also a great draw. The nearby sister boutique hotel, Das Ludwig, is home to Das Ludwig x ae restaurant, which serves a modern, French-inspired set menu.

Name: sushi Lounge
Description En: The latest culinary hotspot at FAVORITE Parkhotel is a restaurant within a restaurant! Sushi lounge is located inside the hotel's Weinbar. Only sushi and sashimi are on the menu in this compact space, and everything is made with the finest produce – something for which FAVORITE Restaurant also has a reputation. Must-try nigiri: otoro for melt-in-your-mouth richness, scallops for pristine freshness or unagi for bold umami.

Name: Lang is her
Description En: "Lang is her" is the appetising culinary concept brought to Hotel an der Wasserburg by a dedicated team led by the Rohde family (the owners). The modern, international cuisine with seasonal influences is served as a three- to seven-course set menu or à la carte. Both in the chic interior, which has a friendly vibe, and, in summer, out on the lovely terrace with its walnut tree, staff provide attentive service and will be happy to recommend the perfect accompaniment from the well-stocked German/international wine list. Wasserburg Bistro & Bar, also part of the property, has a separate menu. Tip: The medieval castle, Burg Neuhaus, is within walking distance.

Name: 5 SEN:SES by Mario Aliberti
Description En: At this fine addition to Karlsruhe's culinary scene, chef-patron Mario Aliberti fuses Italian cuisine with Asian influences. An appealing range of dishes is available: Lunchtime features reasonably priced set menus, plus a small selection from the evening menu. At dinnertime, there is a fine dining menu, an Italian menu and a sharing menu, as well as an extensive à la carte selection. Octopus cooked in black beer with ponzu beurre blanc and black garlic is a house classic. It is worth perusing the well-stocked wine list, too. The inviting modern interior exudes a distinctly loungey feel. In summer, head for the quiet terrace laid out right in front of the restaurant.

Name: Félix
Description En: The trip out of Hamburg city centre to the well-to-do Hochkamp neighbourhood is well worth it, as the many locals who regularly dine here will confirm. Fitting seamlessly into the villa-studded neighbourhood, this elegant little bistro boasts an upscale modern interior. The service is warm and professional. From some tables, diners can see through the glass partition into the kitchen. Félix Bechtolf – after whom the establishment is named – and his team craft classic French dishes including plenty of fish and seafood. The quality of the ingredients and meticulous preparation never fail to impress. Order à la carte or opt for the three-course set menu, which changes every week. The well-curated wine list features premium French labels. Open for lunch on Saturdays. Tip: In fine weather, take a stroll along the Elbchaussee.

Name: DAS MAXI - GENUSSREICH
Description En: Das Maxi has proven to be a successful addition to Das Freiberg hotel and is an appealing dining option – and not only for hotel guests. The kitchen specialises in contemporary, mostly Mediterranean dishes with seasonal influences. In addition to the set menu, which changes daily, there is also a small à la carte selection. Food is served in tastefully designed dining areas, and there is additional garden seating available for the summer months. The wine list, featuring international labels, is second to none. The gorgeous guestrooms have magnificent views of the mountains.

Name: alto
Description En: This restaurant in the Atlantic Grand Hotel has a tastefully sleek interior, with dark wood panelling, large modern fixtures, as well as designer upholstered chairs in red and brown. The conservatory extension is also a lovely spot, as is the courtyard garden in fine weather – an Alpine-style hut is erected here every winter.
