The menu features classic dishes with a modern twist, plus classics such as schnitzel. Incidentally, the crockery is custom-made in Bremen. The location in the old town is ideal, with all the main attractions – the Weser River, Schnoor, Rathaus, Kunsthalle – just a short walk away.

Name: Altes Rathaus by What the Food
Description En: A truly delightful example of casual, down-to-earth dining that brings pleasure and joy! This restaurant is housed in a picturesque half-timbered house in the pedestrian area. The interior is modern and minimalist, and outside there is a charming terrace overlooking the forecourt. Chef-patron Patrick Schubert cooks up dishes that are creative and full of flavour – opt for his ambitious signature set menu ("Da kommsch rum") or choose from the somewhat simpler à la carte selection. Options are more limited at lunchtime. Friendly and competent service comes courtesy of maître d' Anne Henrichs. Good to know: they have a food truck that can be booked for special occasions.

Name: Müllers auf Norderney
Description En: Affording unobstructed views of the sea, 1884's exclusive location alone is a major draw. The charming little boutique hotel is a spa-style building complex composed of Villa Mathilde and the adjoining Villa Olga. It is also home to a chic restaurant with modern and minimalist interior design and a fabulous terrace. In the kitchen, Nelson Müller's team prepares flavoursome and pleasingly uncomplicated dishes from fresh, good-quality ingredients. Soul food would be an apt label for this cuisine.

Name: Daniels
Description En: Located in the centre of Kusel's old town, right on the market square, this renovated townhouse is certainly charming. Out front, there are a few trees and a fountain – the terrace seating here is delightful in summer. The place has a modern feel and a laid-back, friendly atmosphere. Wooden ceiling beams and exposed old sandstone masonry hark back to a bygone era. Ulrike and Daniel Bößhar deliver attentive service and ambitious cuisine in the form of a set menu inspired by modern culinary trends and ranging from three to seven courses. From the carefully crafted amuse-bouches to hearty dishes such as celeriac soup enriched with autumn truffle and Ibérico pork cheek, their detailed, flavour-led approach is unmistakable.

Name: Jäger & Lustig
Description En: What a cosy and quaint-feeling place, serving what the owners term "Heimatküche": think hearty, fresh, flavoursome cuisine. Classic German dishes are the stars of the show – game and goose are specialities of the house. They are at pains to use regional ingredients and remain aligned with the seasons. Service courtesy of friendly and competent staff. Make the most of the beer garden in summer.

Name: Lou im Cavalierhaus
Description En: The estate is worth a visit in its own right. The palace and 620ha Branitz Park landscaped by Prince Hermann von Pückler in the 19C are conducive to a stroll. Lou (a nickname given to Prince Pückler) is an elegant restaurant housed in the smart Kavaliersbau (squire's lodge). Here, chef-patron Tim Sillack serves up modern seasonal cuisine with an artful juxtaposition of regional and international influences. The individual courses of the menu can also be ordered à la carte. "Pückler Eis" (Neapolitan ice cream) has a permanent place on the menu and is something of a signature dessert. There are also three tastefully furnished guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Les Deux Dienstbach
Description En: Les Deux Dienstbach refers to the two sisters who founded this restaurant at the renowned Weingut Künstler and whose French roots influence the cuisine. Nathalie Dienstbach has since returned to her native Normandy, leaving seasoned owner Jennifer Himmel (née Dienstbach) in charge of overseeing both the restaurant floor and the kitchen. She is joined by chef Christian Aguilar, who creates a three- to seven-course set menu using select ingredients. The food is accompanied by wines from France and Weingut Künstler. The setting is also appealing with its colour palette of muted tones, and smart, modern interior design features make for a tasteful interior in the heart of this historical building. On Sunday lunchtimes, you can dine à la carte.

Name: Schwitzer's PUR
Description En: There have been some developments at Schwitzer's. In the newly refurbished rooms of the former fine dining restaurant with floor-to-ceiling windows affording views of the park grounds, diners are invited to embark on a culinary adventure that takes its cue from the seasons. Depending on the time of year, varying styles of cuisine are proposed – à la carte or as a three-course surprise set menu. Schwitzer's Hotel am Park has upscale guestrooms.

Name: Zwo20
Description En: The name of this restaurant refers to the year 2020, in which Andrea von Csiszer (head chef) and Sophie Herzog (the cordial and highly adept maître d') set up shop. Diners are drawn here not only by the somewhat unusual setting in a historical chapel with striking features such as vaults and ceiling paintings, but also the trendy and laid-back atmosphere, as well as the intriguing culinary concept: Asian sharing cuisine with a European twist. You can put together an assortment of several small, cleverly devised dishes to share, such as "Peking pork 24hr sous vide" with fried onion, soya and honey, or cauliflower wings with red cabbage, sweet chilli, fennel and potato. The location in the centre of the old town, caught between the Danube and the Inn, near the Dreiflüsseeck (three-river confluence), is also delightful. Tip: Römerplatz multi-storey car park just a few minutes' walk away.

Name: Fangfrisch
Description En: A friendly, laid-back restaurant located on the edge of the city centre, only five minutes from the Holstentor. Trendy industrial-style design, very friendly and relaxed young service team and, last but not least, tasty modern cuisine. The emphasis is on regional ingredients – for example, organically farmed catfish from Brandenburg. Hot meals are served all day, but there are also sandwiches and fish rolls to go.

Name: JAPATAPA TOSHIBAR
Description En: Japatapa Toshibar is tucked away in a side street near Münchner Freiheit in the Schwabing district. Having formerly run the restaurant Toshi for a long time, owners Toshio and Tamiko Kobatake are no strangers to Munich's gastronomy scene. The small space, in which you sit at the counter or a small table, is done out in a minimalist style. Kobatake's cuisine is authentically Japanese: you should definitely try the tasty sushi, but dishes such as onsen egg with caviar and dashi broth or black cod grilled with saikyo miso are also tempting. The proprietress provides discreet and friendly service, and there is a good selection of wines as well as an impressive number of sakes.

Name: Macionga
Description En: This attractive, sleek restaurant located close to Ku'damm (Kurfürstendamm) is named after its owner – sommelier and winemaker André Macionga. In keeping with his passion for wine, the wine list is very nicely curated, and the restaurant also has its own wine shop. Chef Christopher Wecker builds on stints in various Tim Raue kitchens, successfully incorporating his own ideas. He rustles up modern dishes with a seasonal bent, such as "scallop, coconut, sweet and sour pumpkin, buttered dashi broth" or "chicken fricassee CW, truffle, black walnut, Madeira jus," not to mention his unique take on a Poire belle Hélène, the classic pear dessert. The portion size means you can try several different dishes – a concept that is entirely in keeping with modern trends and goes down very well with diners.

Name: Feinschliff
Description En: This restaurant in the town centre has a trendy, chic interior and a window through which you can see the chefs at work in the centrally positioned kitchen. The large floor-to-ceiling windows look out onto Kirchplatz and Pfarrkirche St Peter. In the evening, the modern menu with subtle Asian influences comprises four regularly changing courses, for example, "tuna, veal, capers" or "venison, parsley root, mushrooms". Service starts for everyone at 6.30pm (no walk-ins). Decent, reasonably priced wine pairings. At lunchtime, only a dish of the day is served. Tip: There is a public car park 150m away (Schießberg 1).

Name: Margaux
Address: Kornmarkt 7, Limburg an der Lahn, 65549, Germany
Description En: Behind the beautiful historical half-timbered façade of this listed 14C building in the heart of the Old Town, there lies a tasteful, modern interior. In this setting, Fabian Sollbach serves up a modern take on French cuisine, in which select ingredients take centre stage. The ambitious dishes include elegant fjord trout with Maine lobster and pearl barley. The attractively priced lunch menu is also very popular. There are a handful of places to be had on the small gallery level and, in summer, tables are set up on an inviting terrace on the Kornmarkt. Tip: The cathedral is just a stone's throw away – it is well worth having a stroll through the charming Old Town.

Name: WurzelWerk
Description En: This restaurant lives up to its name: Wurzel, meaning "root", signifies a dedication to the local terroir, Werk, meaning "craft", highlights a commitment to artisanal cooking techniques – chef-patron Benjamin Bendzko puts both into practice in his market-fresh cuisine. Exceptional and almost exclusively regional ingredients are used to create flavoursome and pleasingly down-to-earth dishes. Two buildings, built in 1875 as a farmstead, now house a guesthouse (with a café at weekends) and this restaurant, whose rustic charm and pretty decor make for a cosy atmosphere. In summer, the garden terrace is the place to be.

Name: Berta
Description En: Berta would be very proud of her grandson, chef Assaf Granit, who has named this appealing restaurant after her. The energy of the chefs in the open kitchen, nestled behind the counter, is infectious, as they fill the colourful dining space with a vibrant and convivial atmosphere. A lively scenario, for which the menu is a perfect match: it is a veritable celebration of family recipes from Jerusalem infused with the modern spirit of Berlin. The "Frenavon" bread with tahini and tomatoes served beforehand is downright addictive. It is practically impossible to resist the charm of this restaurant!

Name: Porte Neuf
Description En: Among Detmold's restaurants, this spot on the outskirts of the Old Town is a fantastic find. Chef-patron Daniel C Fischer presents ambitious dishes that meld French and Far Eastern elements with a modern twist. The set menu comes in a four- or six-course format, and can be extended to nine courses with advance notice. The wonderful food is complemented by dedicated, friendly service and expert wine recommendations. The chefs bring their dishes to your table personally. The intimate restaurant's chic, modern design creates a warm and inviting atmosphere. There is also a lovely terrace for an aperitif, digestif or coffee.

Name: Restaurant 1831
Description En: Even the route to the magnificent moated castle, a 17C architectural gem, is an experience – you get to this stunning estate through a wooded area, then a bridge over the moat leads into the beautiful inner courtyard. The restaurant allies the character of this site steeped in history with modern comfort and winter garden-style. The view through the large glazed front is fabulous, not to mention the terrace! They serve a 4-, 5- or 6-course set menu of modern inspiration – on reservation also vegetarian. You can choose the matching wine or non-alcoholic pairing.

Name: Villa's Wine & Dine
Address: Moselstraße 5, Reil an der Mosel, 56861, Germany
Description En: The fine dining restaurant of Villa Melsheimer serves imaginative and creative modern dishes made from excellent fresh ingredients. One of the three set menus is vegetarian. You can also go à la carte. In summer, the truly beautiful terrace overlooking the Moselle is a huge draw! In the event the weather does not cooperate, you can also enjoy the view from the bright conservatory. The boutique hotel has comfortable guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Vinophil
Description En: The name says it all: wine plays a starring role here. This chic yet relaxed restaurant also boasts its own wine shop. Hosted by an enthusiastic duo – one a chef, the other a sommelier – diners can expect sound wine recommendations to accompany the flavoursome, modern-inspired cuisine. The menu features dishes such as crayfish cocktail with wild herb salad, mango, papaya and dill, or Ibérico pork chop with baked polenta, peppers and smoked almonds. Don't miss their streamlined lunch specials or the wine club evenings. The cocktail list also offers plenty of interesting options. The friendly and adept service further adds to the welcoming atmosphere.

Name: Benders
Description En: This chic and modern restaurant has found the perfect home within the pretty half-timbered building of the long-established Birkenfelder Hof. It is an ideal setting for "casual dining". The atmosphere is also suitably relaxed, the waitstaff are experienced and friendly, and the delicious seasonal modern cuisine, which draws on French, Mediterranean and regional influences, incorporates the occasional Asian touch. The successful synthesis of different culinary styles is evident in dishes such as "Breton monkfish, dashi beurre blanc, pak choi, Sardinian pasta, tomato and pine nut vinaigrette". Classics such as roast beef, burgers (Tue-Wed only) and Wiener schnitzel (Thu only) are also tempting. It is pleasant to dine al fresco on the beautifully landscaped terrace. Well-maintained guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Konrad's
Address: Platz der Vereinten Nationen 4, Bonn, 53113, Germany
Description En: This restaurant on the 17th floor of the Marriott Hotel has the "wow" factor of a great view over Bonn through its floor-to-ceiling windows. In the open kitchens they cook up modern dishes with Mediterranean influences. Pre- or after-dinner drinks are served in the bar right next door. Parking is available in the underground garage, and the lift leads directly to the restaurant.

Name: Eatrenalin
Description En: A unique, almost futuristic spin on the fine dining experience! Using the online ticketing system in advance, you pick one of the two eight-course set menus – "Red Dimensions" with fish and meat, or the vegetarian "Green Dimensions" – and choose your drinks. Those who want add-ons can order either menu in the variants "Exclusive Dinner", "Champagne Dinner" or "Sommelier Dinner". During the 2hr "Eatrenalin Experience", on ultra-modern "floating chairs", you are guided through rooms with differently themed worlds, where tailored appetisers and dishes are served. Renowned chef Peter Hagen-Wiest is the culinary director behind this extraordinary concept that constantly incorporates ideas from star colleagues. The result is modern, creative dishes inspired by international influences and made with top-quality ingredients for perfectly balanced flavour. A case in point is "Umami – Asia's fifth dimension": black cod, Japanese consommé, spring onion, radish, and duck gyoza, chives, shiitake. The evening is clearly structured and seamlessly organised, ending with refined drinks in the bar.

Name: KRasserie im verve⁵
Description En: A former textile factory has been transformed into a modern brasserie and event space, creating an attractive new destination. The exposed concrete and ventilation pipes give the space an industrial feel; minimalist design and decorative art create a modern and stylish look. The floor-to-ceiling windows can be opened up in the warmer months – there's a small terrace out front. Fresh and flavoursome dishes drawing on regional and international influences are served à la carte or as a set menu named "Herzstück". The rooftop bar is great in summer (Thu-Sat).

Name: Melkhus
Description En: The former cowshed of the beautifully renovated historical Immenhof estate houses this charming alternative to the Rodesand restaurant. The cuisine, made with top-quality, fresh produce, is traditional, regional and seasonal. Holstein-style sour meat is one of the classics on the menu. The 48hr-braised beef cheek and baked pike dumplings are also sure to whet the appetite. Vegetarian options are available too. The food is complemented by friendly service and a cosy, rustic atmosphere – the open fireplace is a nice touch. In summer, make a beeline for the terrace, which overlooks the lake. Good news: The restaurant is open seven days a week for lunch and dinner! Coffee and cake are served in the afternoon. Pick up some home-made jam, souvenirs etc at the farm shop.

Name: In Vino Veritas
Address: Steinacher Straße 9, Haslach im Kinzigtal, 77716, Germany
Description En: Inga and Ralf Müller have made a name for themselves with this friendly restaurant. This is due in no small part to the international and regional cuisine, which is made with very good, often local ingredients. The service is attentive and charming. In summer, you can dine on simpler fare in the charming courtyard with its vine arbour. There are chic, modern guestrooms and apartments for overnight stays.

Name: Rodesand
Description En: In an idyllic lakeside location by the Kellersee, this estate was made famous by the German cult film series Immenhof. Nowadays, within the pretty white walls of the manor house, diners tuck into ambitious fish and vegetarian/vegan dishes, such as "beetroot, buckwheat, calamansi, dill" or "Lofoten skrei, monk's beard, verjus, capers, chorizo". Choose between the set menu and individual dishes à la carte. The grilled fish options are sure to whet the appetite. The interior design is delightful: With seven tables, the main room has an elegant, modern feel. There are also two private dining spaces for smaller parties, and Jantzens Bar (with a cigar lounge), where sushi is served. Delightful terrace overlooking the greenery. Tip: Afternoon tea on Sat and Sun. Hotel, riding facilities and farm shop on site.

Name: Ontra
Description En: This restaurant with a tastefully designed modern interior is located in TechSquare, the new centre for digitalisation south of the city centre. A friendly and professional team serves up seasonal cuisine that also includes vegetarian dishes. The shorter lunchtime menu proposes some cheaper options. The neighbouring Ontra's Gourmetstube serves a fixed set menu made up of seven courses in the evening.

Name: Kuhlemann
Address: Freyung 39, Neustadt an der Waldnaab, 92660, Germany
Description En: In his restaurant in the family-run Grader hotel, Adrian Kuhlemann cooks up creative modern cuisine rooted in regional, seasonal produce. His personal culinary style is showcased in interesting dishes – names such as "Salmon Trout Kimchi" or "Egg and Spinach" offer little hint of the inventiveness behind the succinct descriptions. From 7pm – and by prior reservation only – a six-course set menu is served. The well-curated wine list features appealing labels from Germany, France and Italy. Alternatively, guests can opt for harmonious wine pairings served by the glass. The attractive setting blends rustic and modern features; the friendly service team is efficient and attentive. If you prefer to dine à la carte, head to Fischerstüberl for dishes such as spelt risotto with mushrooms or veal meatballs with potato salad (from 6pm).

Name: PIER 6
Description En: This stylish restaurant in the Havenwelten quarter delights diners with modern dishes made with locally sourced seasonal ingredients. Mouthwatering options on menu include Heligoland lobster bisque and skrei fillet with a tomato and thyme crust. Wallet-friendly lunch specials such as beef roulades or goulash also have their fans. The tables near the windows and on the terrace are especially coveted – the view of the New Harbour is beautiful. Given the popularity of this place, it's definitely best to book in advance.

Name: riva
Description En: Housed in Kaisergarten Hotel – the sister establishment of Ketschauer Hof, also located in central Deidesheim – this restaurant has a sleek interior done out in light natural tones. In this setting, pleasingly laid-back, friendly and professional waitstaff serve up delicious international and Mediterranean cuisine. The menu also features barbecued meats prepared on the Big Green Egg, along with options for fans of pizza. The selection of wines from the hotel group's own vineyards is excellent. RIVA Bar-Lounge is the perfect spot for a cocktail. The terrace overlooking the garden is delightful in summer.

Name: Landhaus Rössle
Description En: Expect ambitious cuisine is in a classic/French vein with regional and seasonal influences – dishes include the likes of seared scallops on orange fennel, and the classic Zwiebelrostbraten (beef and onions in gravy). You can dine à la carte or opt for the set menu – available in an omnivore or vegetarian version. Attentive and charming service is the forte of the lady of the house. The interior is modern and elegant, and in winter tables by the fireplace are very much in demand. In summer, the garden terrace is a boon. There are attractive rooms for overnight guests.

Name: Gasthaus Lege
Description En: This spruce restaurant blends seamlessly into the tranquil village atmosphere of the Thönse district. A feel-good dining experience is guaranteed at this warm and welcoming restaurant run with great dedication by Claudia and Hinrich Schulze. And that's to say nothing of the terrific cuisine, which comes in the form of two set menus: "Gaumenfreude" and (vegetarian) "Gartenliebe" – available in three- to seven-course variants. Classic dishes such as "Kalbstafelspitz (veal rump cap), porcini sauce, colourful Swiss chard, nut butter dumplings" bowl diners over with their excellent ingredients and meticulous craftsmanship. Under the tutelage of Claudia Schulz, the waitstaff provide friendly, proficient and professional service, including astute recommendations when it comes to drinks.

Name: Kantiners
Description En: Hotel Waldkrug is a traditional family business in a green and leafy location, and its restaurant is tastefully designed with modern touches. The menu includes good modern bistro dishes in a French vein – think beef carpaccio, Caesar salad or grilled steaks – but also traditional regional dishes, such as beef consommé with marrow dumplings, or schnitzel. In addition, they have pretty terraces at the front and to the rear of the building. The cosy Barstube in the front area is another really lovely option.

Name: Das Alte Haus
Description En: Enrico Dunkel and his small restaurant have been a well-established part of the city's culinary landscape for years. His cooking style is ambitious, creative and draws on international influences. The set menu can comprise five, six or seven courses. Choose your accompaniment from the extensive selection of fine German wines. There is also a pairing menu. The interior is modern yet cosy. In summer, the pretty terrace beckons.

Name: Adler
Description En: Here, traditional Swabian cuisine meets global influences, blending local and international flavours. Enjoy cordial service in the comfort of either the main dining room steeped in history or the charming inner courtyard. The kitchen serves up seasonally influenced dishes. One of the most tempting dishes is the house classic: Swabian Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) with maultaschen, spaetzle and salad. Chic guestrooms are available for overnight stays. On Tuesday evenings, the restaurant is only open to hotel patrons.

Name: Al Pappagallo
Description En: An elegant restaurant with a lovely, light-filled winter garden and a delightful outdoor space – the latter is all the more appealing for being discreetly located within a beautiful inner courtyard. The kitchen serves classic Italian dishes, crafted from high-quality produce – the pasta is a particular highlight! The enthusiastic front-of-house team is friendly and attentive. You will also see the chef himself making his way around the restaurant and chatting with diners.

Name: Strandhaus
Description En: A beach house (Strandhaus) right in the heart of Bonn – who would have thought? The delightful maritime decor and laid-back atmosphere transport you to a seaside retreat. Not forgetting the cosy secluded terrace. This is the perfect setting for a Mediterranean-influenced cuisine, with fish at the heart of it all. Using only the finest ingredients, the chef creates flavoursome dishes with a unique twist, available both à la carte and as a tasting menu. As well as fish, there are meat options and a dedicated vegetarian set menu.

Name: Lammershof Stuben
Description En: To start with, the location on a 45ha estate is terrific. The cosy space with a tiled stove that draws the eye exudes rustic charm and a certain chic. Specialities include various dishes featuring meat from bison they have reared on their own farm. Note: On Mondays only bison burgers, or veggie burgers, are served. Tip: the marvellous terrace with a view of the countryside! There is also the ‘WILD X BERG’ restaurant, where you can enjoy a three or four-course menu on Saturdays from 6 p.m. The small Lammershof hotel, the main building of which dates from 1709, has cosy guestrooms.

Name: Jagdhaus Waldfrieden
Description En: Choose whether to enjoy your meal in the cosy dining room with its open fireplace, in the airy conservatory or on the lovely terrace shaded by trees… This restaurant is a charming location in which to sample good regional food: the menu includes dishes such as Glückstädter Matjes (PDO preserved herring) or fillet of wild boar, cooked rare in a juniper berry jus. Tip: The lunch set menu is an excellent deal. Should you wish to stay overnight, the pretty guestrooms are very inviting and all individually decorated.

Name: Rocus
Description En: Housed in an attractively converted railway building dating from 1904, this restaurant proposes ambitious cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons – available à la carte or as a set menu. Dine al fresco in the courtyard or on the terrace facing the railway line. A table in the wine cellar, surrounded by Spanish red wines, comes highly recommended.

Name: Rössle
Description En: This family-run business is now in its fourth generation. Behind a smart half-timbered façade, diners can choose from seasonal cuisine with some international influences and classics with a connection to the region. There are guestrooms done out in a modern Black Forest style. If you fancy a little excursion, the monastery complex and brewery are both within easy walking distance.

Name: Engelwirts-Stube
Description En: This lovely restaurant with its delightful terrace overlooking the garden serves regional and seasonal cuisine with the odd nod to international culinary traditions. A friendly and well-drilled front-of-house team help to create an inviting atmosphere. Tip: If you want to be close to the action, book the Chef's Table in the kitchen ( minimum 6 people). And if you wish to spend a little longer here, Hotel Engel Obertal offers comfortable, stylish guestrooms and fantastic facilities to help make your stay a relaxing one.

Name: Tomatissimo
Description En: This popular restaurant with a friendly atmosphere lies slightly outside the city, in a small village. In summer you can make the most of the wonderful terrace by the village fountain, in the shade of the chestnut trees. Bernhard Grubmüller and his kitchen team serve up a conventional and a vegetarian set menu, as well as à la carte dishes, including charcoal-grilled dry-aged beef from their own maturing cabinet. The surprise menu comprising new small courses gives a good overview of the cuisine. Tip: Bernhards Küchentisch for smaller groups (on prior reservation).

Name: Bocca di Bacco
Description En: On the outside, a smart historical façade, on the inside an attractively modern and elegant restaurant complete with bar and lounge. Visible through its glass panes, the kitchen turns out Italian cooking. Needless to say, the pasta is home-made. To be paired with one of their great Tuscan wines.

Name: Johann Grill
Description En: Overlooking Berchtesgaden, surrounded by stunning natural beauty and with a magnificent mountain backdrop, the location is to die for! At the restaurant of the luxurious Kempinski Hotel Berchtesgaden, you can enjoy delicious seasonal cuisine made with fresh, local ingredients. For dessert, we highly recommend the Eckerbichl-Haustorte. The sleek, modern interior design is a draw in itself. Incidentally, the restaurant is named after the first person to climb the east face of the Watzmann and Germany's first official mountain guide. Weather permitting, be sure to make the most of the spacious terrace. Tip: A short path around the hotel affords panoramic views of the mountains – especially magical at sunset.

Name: Hof Grothues-Potthoff - Hasenklee
Description En: A charming modern restaurant serving ambitious seasonal cuisine that is strongly influenced by the region and often incorporates home-grown fruit and vegetables. The set menu has four, six or eight courses; its vegetarian counterpart comes in a four- or five-course format. The service is friendly and the wine recommendations helpful. In the attractive courtyard, there is also a bakery, a farm shop and a farm café, as well as a hotel. Alternatively, Hasenpfeffer is open in the evenings for traditional dishes with modern influences.

Name: James Farmhouse
Description En: Fresh and tasty cuisine is served here, and the menu is strongly influenced by the restaurant's own farm. For example, they raise their own Husum red pied pigs, chickens and German Angus cattle – exceptionally tender rump steaks guaranteed. The decor is a blend of industrial chic and charming retro style. Very friendly service. There is a smaller menu at lunchtime. Alongside the restaurants Das Grace and Minato, this is another dining option at the Hotel Das James, which enjoys a charming location on the harbour.

Name: Landgasthof Adler
Description En: This centuries-old inn has long been known in the region for serving good food. Since February 2022, chef Michael Vogel has been perpetuating this tradition as the chef-patron with great dedication – he had already worked here years earlier and took over the reins after a stint under top chef Andreas Caminada. The restaurant serves seasonally inspired dishes, available as a surprise menu or à la carte. The inviting decor seamlessly blends tradition and modern design. Tip: The charming guestrooms complement the restaurant perfectly and reflect the establishment's distinctive character.

Name: mondi
Description En: Owner Pelle Kossmann and his young team are committed to implementing their own culinary ideas here. The set menu changes every fortnight and is made with select seasonal ingredients sourced from regional producers; some of the livestock and vegetables are raised or grown exclusively for this restaurant. The chefs also adhere to the principle of nose-to-tail eating. The decor is sleek and modern, with a partially visible kitchen and friendly, laid-back service. Fixed charge for table water.

Name: Ratsstube
Description En: Antje and Ronny Pester's charming restaurant is in the centre of the village, in the side building of the town hall. In a lovely cosy interior, they serve up ambitious modern cuisine that follows the seasons. Plump for either the à la carte menu to be found in the "Gourmet Bistro" section or the four- to six-course set menu dubbed "Menü Restaurant" – a vegetarian version of which can be pre-ordered. The service is attentive and obliging, and the owner's wine recommendations are spot on. There is a lovely terrace to the rear of the building.

Name: Bistro
Description En: Bistro is housed in Parkhotel Quellenhof, the flagship of Aachen's hotel scene – the marble lobby and the fireplace and tearoom with its exquisite wood panelling are well worth seeing. Classic cuisine with Mediterranean influences is served in a stylish, minimalist-style dining space. The appealing evening menu features dishes such as Black Angus beef tartare with brioche, lobster foam soup with lobster ravioli and tarragon, and Wiener schnitzel with potato and cucumber salad, as well as vegetarian options. There is a smaller selection of dishes available at lunchtime and a snack menu in the afternoon. The terrace overlooking the park is a delightful spot.

Name: Beetle
Description En: Environmental awareness has always been key in every aspect of this restaurant certified as organic – from the tasteful interior design to the staff uniform and not least the food. Following a change of concept, the menu now features meat and fish alongside the tried-and-tested vegetarian and vegan dishes. Mouthwatering options include radicchio risotto with pan-fried oyster mushrooms and mushroom foam, or brook trout meunière with brown butter, almonds, lemon, creamed spinach and potato mousseline. The front-of-house team is exceptionally friendly and attentive. Most of the wines – which are from Germany, Austria and Italy/South Tyrol – are organic or biodynamic. Lovely covered terrace.

Name: Schorse im Leineschloss
Description En: This pleasingly down-to-earth restaurant is the second in the cube-like extension of the Leineschloss, along with Votum. The flavoursome food is made with select ingredients and draws on French influences. Delicious examples include the fish soup or the Charolais beef bourguignon. It's lovely to dine on the terrace with views onto the weir (Leinewehr) or the square, Platz der Göttinger Sieben.

Name: YOSO Asian Comfort Food
Description En: Peter Fridén, who also heads up the kitchen at PURS in Andernach, calls his concept "Asian Comfort Food". Serving up sushi and sashimi, as well as dishes such as shoyu ramen, bao chasu and chicken yakitori, he is dedicated to showcasing Far Eastern flavours. Perfectly suited for sharing, these dishes can also be ordered online to take away. The dining space has a chic urban feel, featuring sleek modern design with a Far Eastern touch. The restaurant is located in the historical centre of Andernach right by the boutique hotel Am Ochsentor. Italian trattoria Ai Pero is next door.

Name: Renoir
Description En: This restaurant has been building on a solid reputation for over 30 years, serving classic cuisine and a sophisticated yet pleasantly down-to-earth atmosphere. Delicious dishes are served as a seasonal menu comprising three to five courses or à la carte. Astute wine recommendations come courtesy of the maître d', who happens to be a trained sommelier. Tip: The small gallery in the building is definitely worth a visit.

Name: Restaurant zum Bären
Description En: The Buggle family has been running this traditional restaurant in the idyllic Lahn Valley since 1827 and chef Joachim Buggle represents the eighth generation to take the helm. He has brought in an impressive concept revolving around culinary classics, serving flavour-intensive, unpretentious dishes. Appetising examples include braised venison shoulder with house-made spaetzle, wild cranberries and glazed pointed cabbage, or grilled calamaretti with lemon risoni, green asparagus and a crustacean foam. Food is served from noon to 9pm Thu-Sun. There is a three-course lunch menu Thu-Sat. On certain dates, they propose a four-course surprise menu. With its beautiful country-style interior, the restaurant has a pleasant, cosy atmosphere; the Weinstube exudes a slightly more rustic feel. And they have another ace up their sleeve in the form of a wonderful terrace in the shade of the lime trees! The front-of-house team provides charming and cordial service… and Landhotel zum Bären is an excellent overnight option.

Name: AS am See
Description En: "AS" refers to both the lakeside location (am See: Scharmützelsee) and the initials of chef-patron Andreas Staack. In this inviting, friendly place – a cross between a wine bar and a bistro – the affable owner devises a five-course menu out of his modern dishes, such as "gnocchi, morel cream, sot-l'y-laisse" and "sea bass, fennel, mussel cream". The quality of the ingredients is top notch, and the bill is good value for money. On Sundays, the set menu is available at lunchtime. The restaurant is nestled in a side street in a quiet, leafy residential area a stone's throw from the spa gardens. It also has a lovely terrace. Tip: Take a walk around the picturesque lake before your meal.

Name: Heiligenstein
Description En: Come here to enjoy classic seasonal cuisine in an inviting, modern atmosphere. High-quality, fresh ingredients are prepared in an agreeably straightforward way that brings out their flavour. Choose between an à la carte menu and a three- or four-course set menu. Then there's the excellent wine list featuring over 400 selections. In summer, tables are laid out on a wonderful terrace. The hotel boasts a peaceful location and lovely cosy guestrooms – and the abundance of greenery and surrounding forest mean it is also a good starting point for hikes.

Name: moriki
Description En: Situated very close to the Festspielhaus (opera and concert house), the restaurant of Roomers hotel serves pan-Asian cuisine and a wide range of sushi. The menu reads, for example, "sake teriyaki – Scottish salmon, teriyaki glaze, sweet cucumber, rice". In a setting that is upscale and very much on trend, a young and enthusiastic front-of-house team provides competent service while maintaining a laid-back atmosphere.

Name: Bar Mural
Description En: This hip bar is loud, lively and trendy – and therein lies its charm! In addition to the regularly changing à la carte selection of high-quality small bites and delicious dishes – also suitable for sharing – there is a wallet-friendly four-course set menu ("Chef's Choice"). For drink recommendations, just ask the proficient and laid-back waitstaff. The moderately priced wine list includes a decent selection of wines by the glass. For al fresco dining, tables are laid out on the terrace in the courtyard behind the restaurant and on the pavement in front of the building.

Name: Kaminstube
Description En: The stylish and elegant dining area boasts the fireplace after which this restaurant is named. Classic and traditional cuisine with international influences is served – small portions are also possible. The terrace with a view of the Ellbachtal is popular in summer.

Name: Asam Schlössl
Description En: In his charming restaurant, nestled in the historical Asam Schlössl of 1687 just outside the city centre, Irish-born Shane McMahon expertly weaves his personal touch into delicious Bavarian cuisine. The menu features hearty classics such as roast pork with cracklings and dark beer jus, as well as modern dishes such as barbecued octopus with spicy ox muzzle salad, and steaks done on the Big Green Egg or the "Schlössl Sharing Brettl" (an assortment of snacks for sharing). Both the atmospheric rustic interior and the secluded Schlösslgarten are inviting . Friendly and attentive service.

Name: Gasthaus Sonne
Description En: In this historic inn with a lovely half-timbered façade and a cosy rural-style feel inside, the young owner serves up dishes such as braised knuckle of pasture-raised lamb with Madeira, or pike-perch fillet with chanterelles. The terrace lies under a big old chestnut tree. There are also guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: CARTE BLANCHE
Description En: Housed within SO/ Berlin Das Stue hotel, on the edge of the Großer Tiergarten and right next to the Spanish Embassy, this restaurant is not to be missed. The modern, elegant and cosy design fosters a relaxed atmosphere that puts diners in mind of an upscale living room. The French-influenced cuisine includes classics such as beef tartare, grilled entrecôte or moules marinières. You can also sip on an aperitif or digestif in Stue Bar, which is right next to the restaurant. In fine weather, the quiet, leafy courtyard terrace is a lovely spot – exclusive access for hotel patrons to the Zoo Berlin is a real highlight of staying here! Tip: An attractively priced set menu is served at lunchtime.

Name: am kai | restaurant. seafood. drinks. elbblick
Description En: This pleasant restaurant right on the waterfront is trendy, hip and relaxed, and offers a super view of the container port – especially from the terrace in summer! The kitchen serves modern seafood dishes such as "prawn tempura, kimchi, nuoc cham, passion fruit" and "monkfish BBQ, grilled corn, plum, tarragon". Meat eaters, too, are bound to find something to their liking; there are also vegetarian/vegan options. In addition to a varied à la carte selection, the restaurant offers a seasonal menu and a sharing menu (for two or more people).

Name: Brasserie Ehrlich
Description En: A French-style brasserie par excellence. Stephan Fröhlich and his wife Nadine run their small restaurant with a personal touch – he is the head chef and she is the sommelier. In this cosy setting, diners can look forward to friendly service and good seasonal cuisine in the form of two set menus. Given the popularity of the place, it is advisable to book in advance. In summer the gorgeous terrace beckons. Tip: Delicatessen goods can be purchased to take home. Overnight accommodation available.

Name: 893 Ryotei
Description En: The mirrored, graffiti-covered façade gives no hint of the restaurant that lies behind it. But despite appearances, this restaurant is a hit, drawing in diners in their droves. The trendy interior is done out in black and furnished with small tables. Guests bask in a lively atmosphere that centres around the open kitchen. Here, The Duc Ngo serves up a wide range of Japanese cuisine, infused with other Asian, South American and European influences, incorporating a wealth of spices. The menu includes traditional favourites such as sushi, sashimi, tempura and tataki, as well as more creative options like "sashimi taquitos", "tai yuzu truffle" and "unagi royal".

Name: Tischlein Deck Dich by Lilly
Description En: Having worked at Lilly in Neupotz, Stefan Echle (service) and Matthis Nowak (kitchen) have found their new vocation – in the vaulted cellar of the separately run Villa Königsgarten hotel (formerly Weingut Diehl). A few steps lead down from the courtyard to the restaurant. As you make your way to the dining area, you can take a peek into the glass-paned kitchen, while the modern, seasonal set menu, which offers a choice of options for each course, is being prepared. The three-course surprise menu on Wednesdays and Thursdays is also worth a look. Named after a fairy tale by the Brothers Grimm (The Lying Goat), the restaurant has a modern, elegant interior with historical details. Great service comes courtesy of a friendly and well-trained front-of-house team. The idyllic location in a village surrounded by vineyards, at the foothills of the Palatinate Forest, offers endless possibilities for excursions.

Name: Schupps
Description En: Regina and Markus Schupp, after whom this restaurant is named, are both professionally trained chefs. Here they rustle up seasonal dishes inspired by the cuisines of France and Germany. Delicious examples include scallops au gratin with green asparagus, Jerusalem artichoke and almond, or venison ragout with cranberries, Brussels sprout leaves and sour cream. Those who wish to savour a more extensive meal can put together their own set menu comprising three to five courses for a fixed price. At lunchtime, the inexpensive daily specials are ideal for a quick meal. This friendly little restaurant also has a terrace for sunny days. Tip: free parking available along the street.

Name: ICHI
Description En: If you are looking to experience Japanese cuisine in Kiel, this city-centre restaurant with a modern and minimalist design is just the place. Laid out over two levels and boasting floor-to-ceiling windows, it extends diners a very warm welcome. Authentic Japanese dishes including sushi and sashimi are conjured up in the partially visible kitchen. Order à la carte or opt for a set menu – vegan options are also available. The restaurant is conveniently located close to the pedestrian area and the harbour with its cruise terminals. Tip: Park your car in the Schlossgarage, which is just a 3min walk away.

Name: Stilbruch
Description En: This pretty restaurant proposes a surprise menu in a choice of three formats: the four-course "Einblick" ("Insight"), the five-course "Dialog" ("Dialogue") and the six-course "Manifest" ("Manifesto"). The seasonal cuisine is modern, making use of regional and international ingredients. The resulting dishes include combinations such as "veal, asparagus, couscous, ajvar, BBQ" and "Spanish carabinero prawn, beetroot, mustard, vermouth". A vegan version of the menu is also available. You can opt for wine pairings or house-made alcohol-free alternatives. The friendly, accommodating service with its warm personal touch contributes greatly to the charming atmosphere. The terrace becomes a particularly cosy retreat during the summer months.

Name: NaNum
Description En: As soon as you enter the restaurant, you can see into the open kitchen, where chef Jinok Kim puts a modern spin on the culinary traditions of her Korean homeland. Using regional ingredients, some from the restaurant's own garden in Brandenburg, she shows a particular interest in fermented foods. The ingredient-led dishes are beautifully precise. Natural wines accompany the five-course set menu (vegetarian or with meat) served on Wednesdays and Thursdays, and the seven-course set menu (vegetarian or with fish) available on Fridays and Saturdays. The space is pleasantly pared back and the service is very friendly. Jinok Kim is also a ceramicist and makes the crockery on which the dishes are served – the studio is also located in the building. The restaurant is located not far from Checkpoint Charlie, on a small square (with a lovely terrace) opposite the Jewish Museum.

Name: STUBN in der Frasdorfer Hütte
Description En: This exclusive mountain-top location, surrounded by woods and meadows, really is the stuff of dreams. What was once a hiking lodge is now a cosy restaurant serving modern Alpine cuisine that can only be reached on foot (50 minutes from the Lederstube car park) or by booking a shuttle bus. Diners seated at the front can see the chefs at work in the open kitchen, grilling top-quality produce over an open fire. A shining example is the super-fresh Chiemsee pike-perch with bold roasted aromas, accompanied by an intensely flavoursome Jerusalem artichoke puree and crunchy rapini – a delightfully accessible combination. You can choose à la carte from a short list of options or have a surprise menu put together for you. The evening menu is also available at lunchtime, if requested in advance. The wine list is very well curated and the waitstaff are highly adept. The terrace is wonderful in summer! Simple guestrooms can be booked for overnight stays.

Name: HIO
Description En: "HIO" is the nickname of the small village that is home to this restaurant, which serves a vegetable-led six-course set menu. Much of the produce comes from the restaurant's own garden, which is right by the building, or from local farmers. The interior boasts a stylish blend of modern design and rustic touches, with the open kitchen being a focal point – here you are very much in the thick of things. With capacity for just 16 diners, the place has something akin to a family atmosphere and the service is cordial and pleasingly laid-back. Dishes using regional and seasonal ingredients, such as "brook trout – buttermilk" or "lamb – wild garlic" are prepared in full view. The graffiti on the wall – which translates to "The field cooks" – fits the theme perfectly. A brilliant idea: Upon arrival, guests are taken outside to enjoy hors-d'oeuvres by the charcoal grill and hear about the sustainable philosophy in place here. In addition to HIO, HILZHOF also houses another restaurant, MEIER, plus a handful of guestrooms.

Name: Lemabri
Description En: Despite its somewhat unusual location in an industrial estate, this restaurant run by Sarah Henke and Christian Eckhardt has diners coming in droves. Building on successful stints in Andernach ( at YOSO and PURS respectively), the duo set up shop here with a casual and varied concept. In a spacious setting with chic modern interior design, the kitchen team serves up a wide-ranging selection of plates that are perfect for sharing. The extensive menu includes Asian and regional dishes, as well as pasta and fantastic pizzas from the large Morello Forni pizza oven. Children are also welcome – they will love the children's menu and play area. Reduced offer at lunchtime, pizza also available Tue–Fri.

Name: Die Speiserei im Maier
Description En: The restaurant at Hotel Maier (a family-run establishment since its founding as a café and guesthouse in 1936) serves cuisine that showcases fresh seasonal regional produce; it is also, for the most part, organic and sourced as locally as possible. Order à la carte or opt for a three- to five-course set menu. In the inviting space, the original traditional character has been preserved, but given an elegant update courtesy of discreet modern accents. There is also a spacious courtyard terrace for those who enjoy dining al fresco. Friendly and professional service.

Name: Caro's
Description En: Having relocated within Tübingen, Caro's now boasts a prime location right by the Neckar River. The interior decor is sleek and modern, and the contemporary cuisine includes vegetarian and vegan options, with dishes ranging from yellowfin tuna tatare to stuffed kohlrabi and roast poussin. Opt for the set menu or go à la carte. There is also a bar. Tip: Delicious food items can be purchased to take home.

Name: Springbrunnen SKLENAR
Description En: After almost 30 years in Mallorca, Czech-born Martin Sklenar and his wife Lucie swapped the Balearic island for the vineyards of Oberkirch. In their restaurant, they propose an interesting blend of regional (Baden), Mallorcan and Bohemian-inspired cuisine. This is served in a cosy interior with a slightly rustic feel, or out on the wonderful terrace known as the Weinberggarten. There is also a vegetarian/vegan set menu. The ingredient-led dishes can be accompanied by your choice of wine from a predominantly regional selection.

Name: [w]einklang
Description En: A cosy atmosphere reigns in this chic little restaurant in the northwest of Nuremberg, with wine racks adding a nice decorative touch. In this setting, chef-owner Tomas Spanu serves a four- or five-course set menu, of which a vegetarian version is also an option, and an à la carte menu. The chef – who, as it happens, is of Sardinian-French heritage – cooks in a pleasingly streamlined and ingredient-led style. The friendly and attentive service is the icing on the cake. You'll definitely want to keep coming back for more! NIAN BISTRO is also part of the establishment.

Name: Limbourg
Description En: A wonderful addition to the Belgian Quarter's fine dining scene. The atmosphere is pleasingly laid-back and the vibe tasteful, whether you dine in the ground-floor space or at BelEtage. Chef-patron Alen Radic showcases his cosmopolitan cuisine, which draws on French influences and is made with fresh, good-quality ingredients – served as a five- or nine-course set menu of which there are two versions: "classique" and "veggie". During the week, there is also a five-course lunch, which includes dishes from the evening menu. The sheltered courtyard terrace is particularly inviting in summer.

Name: Lovis
Description En: An impressive architectural feat – a former prison has been transformed into an attractive restaurant. High ceilings and exposed brick walls, sleek interior design and a great lighting concept make for a special atmosphere. Diners take their seats in the former lock yard, now covered and fitted with large windows – the "Aquarium" room is truly original. The modern vegetable-oriented cuisine is available as a set menu or à la carte – regular, vegetarian or also vegan upon request. A selection of wines from around the globe. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif in the lovely bar, which also boasts a terrace. You can enjoy a night in Wilmina, the adjacent hotel.

Name: Die Bürgermeisterei 1728
Description En: A location steeped in history in which to enjoy a meal! The lovingly restored building, which gives directly onto the market square, was once the mayor's residence and dates back to 1728. The elegant fusion of modern style and historical details lends the place atmosphere. The evening menu is ambitious, fresh and full of flavour, with appetising options such as beef bourgignon, dried fig crumble and potato-parsnip mash. The small selection of seasonal dishes is also proposed in the form of set menus, one of which is vegetarian. In summer, make the most of the secluded terrace.

Name: Fachwerk
Description En: Semi Hassine and Patrizia Weidemann-Hassine run this restaurant in the old town, where exposed timber beams lend the space a charming rustic feel. The lovely terrace commands a view of the old half-timbered façades all around. On the menu: Westphalian cuisine with Mediterranean and subtle Eastern influences. Tip: the attractive changing seasonal set menu. Hot food is served from 4pm; on Saturdays from noon, all day.

Name: BEES Restaurant
Address: Am Rottland 6, Rüdesheim am Rhein, 65385, Germany
Description En: This attractive restaurant serving appealing seasonal cuisine is housed in the premises of a former Asbach Uralt brandy distillery. The set menu includes a minimum of four courses, but you can also order à la carte. Sit back to savour your meal and enjoy friendly service in this chic setting with a partially visible kitchen. Tables are set up to create a pleasant terrace in summer. Tip for motorists: there is also a public car park near the train station and the Rhine.

Name: Eulenstein
Description En: Taking its cue from the seasons and made with select ingredients, the food here is meticulously prepared, flavoursome and fresh – it is clear that chef Steve Eulenstein has worked at some top-flight establishments in his time. He proposes two set menus as well as classics such as rump steak. The dining space is attractive and minimalist in style, and the service is friendly and professional. The location in a residential area just a few minutes' drive from the BAB 3 motorway is also convenient.

Name: Pierburg - Erika Bergheim
Description En: Located in the rural outskirts of Essen, Pierburg has been welcoming diners since 1901. With many years of experience in the top league of gastronomy under her belt, Erika Bergheim is now at the helm, cooking up internationally and seasonally inspired dishes. You can choose from the à la carte selection, named "Pierburg Karte", or opt for the "Selection E.B." set menu – the individual courses can be ordered à la carte, too. There is also an extensive, well-curated wine list. Friendly service and a tasteful contemporary setting, with certain tables affording a glimpse into the kitchen. Gorgeous terrace.

Name: Weinbistro "George"
Description En: This bistro, too, is definitely worth a visit. The second dining option in the Weinhaus Uhle hotel is at once a wine shop and an appealing restaurant and is open all day long. Seated at wooden tables in an attractive space, you enjoy à la carte dishes or a three- or four-course menu. For chef Marcel Kube and his team, regional ingredients are key. Classics include "Die Fischsuppe" (fish soup) and "Der Uhlsche Klops" (meatballs). There is also a good wine selection. In summer, tables are set up on the street out front.

Name: vierzehn 85
Description En: The former tithe farm from 1485 - still with a beautiful half-timbered facade - offers homely, modern guest rooms and a very nice, tasteful and casual restaurant on two floors with smaller and larger rooms and charming niches. The kitchen serves really good contemporary dishes from many regional and always seasonal products. Wines from the own vineyard. In summer, the terrace is inviting.

Name: Wibbelings Hof
Description En: Sandra and Jörn Haumann have turned the family-owned estate, which dates back to 1899, into a charming restaurant. While he takes care of the service, she prepares an ambitious set menu that takes its cue from the seasons; some of the ingredients are home-grown. Food is served in a lovely high-ceilinged room, whose modern interior design incorporates decorative features such as a wine rack, a workbench and large pictures. This space also makes an ideal venue for events and weddings. Tip: the farm shop (open on Wed and Thu afternoons).

Name: PULS
Description En: Stylish boutique hotel Legend, right in the heart of Cologne's Old Town, is home to the restaurant-bar PULS. The atmosphere here is lively, modern and urban. You can dine at the bar, at high tables or at standard tables – or, during the summer, out on the lovely terrace. Chef Johannes Langenstück and his team serve bar food alongside dishes in sharing or individual portions. Alternatively, you can hand over the reins and go for the "Chef's Choice" surprise menu. A good selection of wines and an interesting range of cocktails, including signature creations, round off the meal.

Name: Minato
Description En: This is just one of the options in the diverse range of restaurants within the Das James hotel, which is housed in a former naval building at the marina. Here you can look forward to truly authentic Japanese cuisine in the form of two set menus: the "James Sushi Menu" and the "Omakase" surprise menu. The chic design with a subtle Far Eastern touch and the friendly, competent service create a harmonious atmosphere. Minato is an appealing alternative to the restaurant's Das Grace and James Farmhouse and, as such, has many regular guests.

Name: Westerndorfer Stube
Description En: Housed in Landgasthof Karner, this cosy eatery makes for a lovely down-to-earth alternative to the adjacent fine dining restaurant. The outstanding chef, Hannes Fussel, proves that he is also a master of home-style cooking, turning seemingly simple dishes into a delight for the palate! Think lamb lights, Wiener schnitzel or the classic Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) – diners are bowled over by the depth of flavour and presentation. Regional ingredients take centre stage, and the decor complements this perfectly: rustic charm and subtle modern elements make for a harmonious whole.

Name: Oukan
Description En: It's worth seeking out this restaurant, the entrance of which is a bit hidden. A long, mirrored corridor leads you to an interior characterised by distinctive architecture and a clean-lined, minimalist, Far Eastern design. The food is no less interesting: The Japanese-inspired cuisine is completely vegan, with fermented food playing a major role – hence having built their own Fermentation Lab. The creative seven-course set menu can be extended by an additional course. The dishes seem pleasingly pared back, although a lot of effort has gone into them. An individual signature is evident, for example, in the delicate maitake with robust roasted aromas and a subtle note of thyme, accompanied by a sensational sauce made from mushrooms, sake, port wine, vanilla and coffee, which inspires with fantastic depth. The intriguing tea pairings are an absolute must! Top-notch teas are celebrated here and presented in depth. It is also possible to go for a mixture of tea and other drinks pairings.

Name: plaisir by Hamid Heidarzadeh
Description En: The minimalist, elegant look immediately catches the eye, with its gorgeous terrazzo flooring, clean-lined, pared-back design in black and white, and high ceilings with stunning original mouldings. Chef Hamid Heidarzadeh achieves interesting results by building modern elements on classic foundations, also incorporating subtle Asian and Mediterranean influences. Two set menus are available in a three- or five-course format – one vegetarian ("Pflanzenfresser/-innen"), one with meat ("Fleischfresser/-innen"). The names belie finely tuned and precisely crafted dishes with full-bodied taste profiles, such as the combination of tender sea bass, braised pork belly and an interesting take on pointed cabbage – served as a salad and vegetable – as well as flavourful bak kut the. The laid-back yet discreet service is pleasant, and the chefs also muck in front of house. Tip: A reasonably priced lunch dish is available Wed-Fri. There is a lovely little terrace in the courtyard.

Name: Café GUPI
Description En: Set up in what was formerly the gardener's house on a historical country estate, this is the trendy restaurant-bar concept of the Düster and Schneider restaurateur and winemaking families. Christoph Düster's cuisine is made up of what could be described as "modernised classics". The premium quality of the ingredients is evident in dishes such as "pizokel (buckwheat dumplings), Périgord truffle, spinach, hazelnut" or "guinea fowl, sherry, parsley root, Andengold potato". The atmosphere is pleasingly laid-back and casual, not least thanks to the easy-going, attentive and ever-present service under the direction of wine expert Christoph Schneider, who recommends wines from a selection of over 500 labels to accompany the four-course set menu. In case you were wondering, the name of the restaurant is derived from the regional "GUPI" wines ("GUtedel" and "PInot"). In summer, the terrace shaded by the large trees of the lovely Läublin Park is highly inviting. Tip: Booking advisable.

Name: Ursprung
Description En: This smart restaurant is set in the family-run Hotel Aquarium, which is located in the heart of the beautiful city centre. With Jan Boddenberg, the third generation is now at the helm. As head chef, he curates a modern set menu and delivers classic, regional dishes, attaching importance to good produce and seasonality. Friendly service.

Name: Goldmund
Address: Schöne Aussicht 2, Frankfurt on the Main, 60311, Germany
Description En: The restaurant in the Literaturhaus, set on the banks of the Main, has an extremely stylish and upscale interior. Eye-catching features include the spacious bar area and the striking portraits of international artists. The cuisine is rooted in classical traditions and guided by the seasons – order dishes à la carte or opt for one of the two set menus (one is vegetarian), which comprise four to six courses. The adjoining Kaminzimmer ("fireplace room") is also very pleasant. Tip: There are plenty of parking spaces behind the restaurant. This is also a good venue for hosting events.

Name: Weinstube Baldreit
Description En: This lovely wine tavern may be somewhat hidden away in its pleasantly quiet location, but it is well worth seeking out – especially in summer, when the charming secluded courtyard terrace comes into its own. Along with a relaxed atmosphere with rustic charm and friendly service, diners can look forward to an array of different flammkuchen, speciality mussel dishes and regional classics. The seasonal specials of the day are written up on a wooden board or presented verbally. The restaurant has plenty of regulars and is always busy, so it's advisable to make a reservation!

Name: Sorriso
Address: Oppenheimer Landstr. 49, Frankfurt on the Main, 60596, Germany
Description En: In a smart building occupying a corner plot in the Sachsenhausen district, this tastefully designed restaurant serves modern Mediterranean-inspired cuisine made with top-notch ingredients. There are two set menus, one of which is 100% vegan. The owner has some great wine recommendations up his sleeve. Pleasant terrace for summer.

Name: Küppersmühle Restaurant
Description En: A fantastic location with an old industrial atmosphere, view of the inner harbour, and terrace right by the water. This urban-style interior is the backdrop for ambitious modern cuisine with and international influences – the menu includes, for example, tataki of Faroe salmon with buttermilk and coriander broth. At lunchtime, there is a slightly different menu, with a selection from the evening menu. In the KÜ shop, you can buy many delicious items to enjoy at home. Tip: The Küppersmühle Museum right next door is worth a visit.

Name: Inspektorenhaus
Description En: In the city centre, opposite the brick-built Gothic town hall, is the Inspektorenhaus, from which the inspector used to keep an eye on the market and the activity it harboured. Nowadays it is a restaurant with a cosy ambience and distinct charm, thanks to old wooden beams and pretty decorations. In summer, you can sit outside in the courtyard garden. Two seasonal set menus are served, one with fish, one with meat. Friendly service.

The Stadtgarten Pavilion (1936) has been given a new lease of life with a trendy-chic feel, plus a good dose of glamour! The ingredient-led cuisine blends modern and classic techniques. Food is served throughout the day: The "Business Lunch" is available until 3pm, daily specials until 5pm. In the evening, there is a broader range of options. Diners can opt for a set menu featuring à la carte dishes for both lunch and dinner. Those in the mood for classics such as Wiener schnitzel or beef goulash, or who prefer a pizza, will not be disappointed. The terrace overlooking the small park is lovely. Very good, wide-ranging wine list. For a classic bar experience, check out Pino's Bar, which also has an outdoor lounge.

Name: Dae Mon
Description En: This chic and rather stylish restaurant is an interesting option. The food is dubbed "open-minded cuisine": modern dishes that combine the techniques and flavours of Japanese and Korean cuisine in a variety of ways – for example, street food influences make their presence felt. There is also a creative vegetarian version of the set menu. Tip: As an alternative to wine, they propose a beautifully curated cold Asian tea pairing – a real treat for all those who like to go alcohol-free.

Name: Diekmann
Description En: In the mood for the charm of a typical bistro setting? At the front, amid decorative wine racks from an old colonial goods shop, the casual dining area has high tables positioned around a free-standing oyster bar. Alternatively, nab one of the small tables in the charming minimalist-style space at the back of the premises. The welcoming and attentive service also adds to the feel-good factor. In the evening, ambitious French and German dishes are served à la carte or as a tasting menu – cleverly integrated original twists give them a distinctively creative edge. Lunchtime options are more limited but reasonably priced – water, bread and espresso are included. The impressive oyster menu is available at both mealtimes.

Name: Broeding
Description En: This lively restaurant is an institution in Neuhausen. In an outwardly unassuming-looking building on a residential street, diners tuck into delicious, pared-back dishes made with excellent ingredients (mostly organic or Demeter-certified) sourced in the Alpine and pre-Alpine regions. From Mon-Thu, diners can opt for a three- to five-course version of the set menu; Fri-Sat, there is just the one five-course variant – or if you arrive at 6pm, you can go for the three-course early evening set menu. The pleasingly laid-back atmosphere is in no small part down to the friendly, attentive and unpretentious service, which comes complete with expert guidance when it comes to the terrific wine list, which focuses on Austrian wine-growing regions. In summer, the secluded inner courtyard terrace beckons. Tip: From 3pm onwards, Austrian wines can be purchased from the well-stocked wine shop to enjoy at home.

Name: Höfli
Description En: The charming Höfli blends seamlessly into the picturesque old town setting. The enchanting cobblestone courtyard invites you to dine under the summer sky, surrounded by historical walls and half-timbered buildings. The interior is just as pleasant with its sleek, contemporary feel. While maître d' Alexandra Killy ensures a warm welcome, her husband, Marco, prepares delicious and neatly crafted dishes. His classical training shines through in dishes such as foie gras tiramisu with mascarpone, quince, coffee and brioche, or John Dory with fregola sarda and a pointed pepper broth.

Name: Drexlers
Description En: Since 2007, this bright, modern restaurant right next to Colombipark has been something of an institution in Freiburg. Service is friendly and adept and the atmosphere warm and welcoming. Showcasing regional produce, the ambitious seasonally inspired cuisine draws on French and Italian influences. The four- to six-course set menu comes in a "classic" or vegetarian version. On Mondays and Thursdays you can also order individual courses à la carte. Great selection of reasonably priced wines – courtesy of their own wine shop. Tip for motorists: Rotteck underground car park is within walking distance.

Name: Franziska
Address: Hainer Weg 72, Frankfurt on the Main, 60599, Germany
Description En: It takes 40 seconds in the lift up to the top of the Henninger Turm. As well as its magnificent views over the Frankfurt skyline, this restaurant proposes "Progressive German Vintage Cuisine". The name is a tribute to the great-aunt of the Mook Group founder. Cocktails in the Barrel Bar. Terrace one floor down. Online bookings only.

Name: Krone
Description En: You will feel at home here for a number of reasons. Not only can you enjoy the modern, classic and seasonal cuisine showcasing local produce, but there is also the friendly, attentive service that comes courtesy of the owner and her team, who also know their way around the wine list. The elegantly pared-down interior is equally inviting, not to mention the beautiful garden with shaded seating that draws diners in summer. Well-kept guestrooms are available should you wish to stay the night.

Name: Waldhorn
Description En: This restaurant in Stuttgart's Rohr neighbourhood serves an intriguing take on classic French cuisine that draws on Spanish and Swabian influences. This concept wasn't simply plucked out of thin air: the two chefs – José María González Sampedro, who hails from Mallorca, and Caroline Autenrieth from Swabia – met while working in a restaurant in Marseille. The six courses on their surprise menu include deliciously aromatic lamb and braised shallot with a filling of blood sausage ragout with Mediterranean spices. At lunchtime, a three-course menu is offered. In the attractive seating area, old wood panelling and modern furnishings add to the charm.

Name: Genießer Stube - Daniel Raub
Description En: Daniel Raub represents the third generation at the helm of this family-run business. At Genießer Stube, one of the restaurants of Romantik Hotel Landhaus Biewald, he serves up classic French-based cuisine with a seasonal focus, eschewing any frills and putting his ingredients centre stage. In the evening there is the set menu ("Genießer Menü") that comes in four or six courses - supplemented with little extras. You can also opt for fine wine pairings. The wine list is also worth a look. In winter, food is served in the cosy dining room with its old wooden beamed ceiling. In summer, you can also dine in the conservatory or on the terrace. Professional service is provided by a charming front-of-house team. The second restaurant, Zur Tränke, is housed in the newly constructed modern hotel building. In addition to comfortable accommodation, overnight guests can look forward to a fantastic breakfast. Tip: Museum Friedland is just round the corner.

Name: KIKU Restaurant by Jan Fribus
Description En: Kiku means "chrysanthemum" – the Japanese national flower – and, indeed, the cuisine here is strongly marked by Japanese elements, along with seasonal influences and the odd subtle classic French touch. Comprising eight courses, the set menu features dishes such as dim sum with prawns and bisque, and hibachi venison with pumpkin and hoisin. The restaurant is located in a tastefully restored historical building in a small street lined with half-timbered façades, not far from the city centre. Inside, the atmosphere is laid back and elegant, and there is a secluded terrace in the courtyard. The service is friendly and informal – the charming chefs also come to your table to talk you through their dishes. A short yet carefully curated wine list complements the food perfectly, and most wines are available by the glass. Tip: Just upstairs from the restaurant, Anno 1560 offers cosy and stylish apartments.

Name: dario&
Description En: Dario Breuer, the chef-patron behind the name, serves modern French dishes featuring international and Far Eastern influences and with a focus on seasonal produce. The "&" in the name deliberately leaves plenty of room for interpretation, because everyone should feel at home here, whether you go in for laid-back or ambitious cuisine – perfectly in step with its "casual fine dining" byline. The four- to seven-course set menu also has a vegetarian counterpart. Alternatively, you can pick à la carte. The well-curated wine list featuring 265 different labels encompasses big names as well as new finds and a fine champagne selection. The set menu can be accompanied by wine pairings served by the glass – "Élémentaire", "Par Excellence" or "Noble & Vieux" – or an alcohol-free equivalent. Service is pleasant, cordial and knowledgeable. The interior has a trendy, urban feel and, in summer, a handful of tables are laid out on the pavement in front of the restaurant. Being close to Synagogenplatz and not far from Elisenbrunnen, the cathedral and the town hall, the location is also of interest.

Name: fine.wine.dine.
Description En: Located in the pedestrian area, not far from the Rhine River, this modern yet cosy little restaurant serves ambitious seasonal cuisine in the evening. You can either order the set menu or choose à la carte; on Wednesday and Thursday evenings there is also an appealing sharing menu for two. Vegetarian options are also available if ordered in advance. For lunch, there are simpler, more moderately priced daily specials. Delicatessen goods and wine can be purchased to enjoy at home.

Name: Laesâ
Description En: Murrhardther Hof, a culinary institution since 1920, has launched an inspired new concept. What sets it apart is that all diners are seated at a long solid-beechwood table – perfect for mingling, but with enough space for this not to be obligatory. From your seat, you can even catch a glimpse of the open kitchen, where Moritz Bilsing and Emilio Löffler run the show. Dishes are clearly and thoughtfully composed – pared down to the essentials, almost to the point of minimalism. A fine example, with harmonious flavours and delicate contrasts, is the rolled turbot fillet: moist and tender, served with a dollop of wonderfully salty fine-beaded caviar, as well as aromatic barley, sweet apricots and a mild, buttery curry sauce. The single set menu comes in four to six courses, which are punctuated by refined little extras. The experience is complemented by the expert and friendly service, with sommelier Nikolas Reidt providing excellent wine recommendations. As an alternative to wine, there are interesting house-made alcohol-free pairings to go with the set menu.

Name: Zauberberg
Description En: The name translates as "magic mountain", and the name is fitting for a number of reasons. For one, dedicated host Claudia Kimbacher, who adds a pleasantly personal touch to the service with her remarkably warm manner and is also happy to assist you in choosing your wines. Then there is Sven Gerlach's cuisine, which comes in the form of a surprise menu comprising five to six modern and creative courses. If you would like a vegetarian option, please indicate this when making your reservation. From January to November, a three-course "Work Day Supper" set menu is also available Tue-Thu by advance booking. As for the restaurant itself, inside the atmosphere is friendly with an elegant feel to the decor; outside there is a lovely terrace that is very popular on warm summer evenings.

Name: The Wild Duck
Description En: This young and vibrant addition to the local fine dining scene is proving to be a hit – and with good reason. Part of the appeal is the upscale and tastefully trendy decor. And then there is the modern and pleasingly pared-down cuisine, in which French and Asian influences are deftly interwoven. Dishes are presented in the form of a five-course set menu, available in both a classic and a vegan version, with the option of an additional course. Their signature dish is "The Wild Duck, Thai curry, pear". The friendly waitstaff will gladly recommend the perfect wine pairing. Tip for getting there: The restaurant is just 20min from the city centre by tram.

Name: IL Sommelier
Description En: Behind the unassuming façade of a modern building in the Trudering district, this is a real gem of a restaurant. In the chic, contemporary space, diners are served authentic, flavoursome, down-to-earth cucina italiana. The dishes on the menu are sophisticated but not pretentious, and include tortelli with a cheese and aubergine filling or beef cheek braised with sweet potato mash. The wine list features Italian wines exclusively. In summer, the quiet terrace to the rear of the property beckons.

Name: Waldschlössle
Description En: After driving past seemingly endless rows of vines, you will eventually reach this small vineyard, where a traditional mountain inn has been reimagined as a trendy and modern dining destination. Floor-to-ceiling windows showcase breathtaking panoramic views of the region. There is also a terrace. "Fine Swabian cuisine" is the name of the game at this restaurant, which is run by a young couple – Annika Braun presides front-of-house and her husband, Manuel, is the chef. He mainly uses locally sourced ingredients, following the seasonal availability of produce, and also likes to incorporate elements of other cuisines. The menu includes dishes such as vitello forello (medium-rare boiled veal, smoked trout cream, Fellbach verjus) and Brunnenhof Mäusdorf rooster with crispy skin accompanied by a sour vegetable chutney, artichoke purée and polenta sticks.

Name: Kulinarium
Address: Friedrichsplatz 4, Röthenbach an der Pegnitz, 90552, Germany
Description En: This charming restaurant is housed in a spruce half-timbered building in the heart of Röthenbach an der Pegnitz, just outside Nuremberg, and proposes casual fine dining in a historic setting. Modern interior design incorporating a rustic beamed ceiling creates a cosy atmosphere. It is a place run with genuine passion and dedication. At the helm are Gerald and Melanie Hoffmann – he a well-known name in the region's culinary scene and she leads the service with exceptional warmth. There is a set menu prepared using regional and seasonal ingredients, with dedicated wine pairings available. In addition to the set menu, you can choose from a small selection of daily specials. In summer, head for the terrace in the front garden. There is also a small hotel in the building.

Name: Halbstück
Description En: The Knipsers, a well-known Laumersheim winemaking family, opened Halbstück back in 2014 as a Weinstube. Now it is Alsace native Christian Rubert – also known from Karlbacher, a restaurant in Großkarlbach – who is in charge in the kitchen. Influences from his homeland are evident in his dishes, which pair beautifully with the finest wines from Weingut Knisper. The appealing dinner menu includes French classics such as bouillabaisse, and halibut in lobster sauce. Or feel free to choose from the daily specials.
