At lunchtime, there is a three- to five-course menu. Laura Rubert ensures that guests receive a warm welcome in this cosy atmosphere. Lovely courtyard. Tip: They also offer interesting culinary events and wine tastings (for 10 people or more). In addition, rooms can be booked for weddings and conferences. A holiday flat is available to rent out, too.

Name: Stresa
Description En: A chic, modern and pleasingly neighbourly vibe makes itself felt in this restaurant in the attractive historical district of Striesen, which inspired the name of this place. Walls decorated with artwork by local artists, as well as the open kitchen draw the eye. In the evening, there is a choice of two set menus (omnivore and vegetarian/vegan) composed of three to six courses, or à la carte dishes. The menu changes regularly and takes its cue from the seasons. At lunchtime diners take their pick from a range of options on the "Bistro Menu". Friendly and relaxed service.

Name: Schlossberg
Description En: The location on the Schlossberg (castle hill) is fantastic in its own right: located right beside Vauban fortress, the business travellers' hotel that houses this restaurant towers over the city and affords a one-of-a-kind view – best enjoyed from the terrace. The interior is also delightful with its sleek contemporary design, coupled with panoramic vistas through generous windows. The menu changes with the seasons and features classic dishes with international twists. Order à la carte or opt for the set menu of the month (three or four courses).

Name: Ebanat
Description En: Surrounded by vineyards, this modern restaurant boasts a beautiful location on the premises of Weingut Kopp, a Demeter winery complete with its own wine shop. As you savour classic seasonal cuisine that draws on international influences, you can take in the view of the vines and the plain, to which the name makes reference (the village of Ebenung used to be called "Ebanat", a derivation of the Old High German word for "plain"). Made with locally sourced ingredients wherever possible, the excellent food can be accompanied by the restaurant's own wines. Friendly and professional service.

Name: Whiskyplaza
Description En: By the Nikolaifleet canal, one of the oldest buildings in Hamburg, which is located in the city's oldest street, is home to this appealing bar-cum-restaurant. Spanning a few floors, the space capitalises on the historical charm of the original structure (1697): Crystal chandeliers, wooden beams and modern furnishings as well as shelves lined with decorative bottles all come together to create a genuinely warm ambiance. The kitchen serves its modern take on classic cuisine as a sophisticated set menu or à la carte. Highlights include scallop with barley, salt marsh herbs, apple, seaweed caviar and beurre blanc, or flat iron steak with pumpkin seed dumplings, kalette, mushrooms, apple and cheese. Given the restaurant's name, it might come as no surprise that the extensive selection of spirits includes around 1 100 whiskies.

Name: Rebblick
Description En: Housed in Korb's Remstalhalle, this restaurant with an attractive glass façade has retained a certain 1970s feel, while incorporating chic modern design features. Jochen Gromann serves up flavoursome seasonal cuisine drawing on regional and international influences. In addition to à la carte options – including Swabian Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy), there are also set menus. The menu features a wine recommendation for each dish. Chef Nadine Gromann manages the friendly and professional front-of-house team. Delightful terrace – with a view of the vineyards, depending on where you sit.

Name: Ristorante Engel
Description En: With almost 200 years of gastronomic history to its name, this place has been in Italian hands for over 40 years. Following in his parents' footsteps, Franco Iaia now runs this ristorante with his wife Yvonne. With a tiled stove and warm wood, the inviting dining space is vibrant and charming. "La Piazza" is their lovely terrace shaded by mulberry trees. Highlights of the "cucina italiana strettamente classica" include homemade pasta, brasato and osso buco.

Name: Meilenstein
Description En: A listed building steeped in history is the attractive location that houses this chic restaurant with its bar and lovely terrace. Here, they propose a set menu that you can put together yourself and that draws on modern influences. The front-of-house team is friendly and accomplished. There is also an appealing selection of cocktails at this stylish venue with a variety of spaces you can hire for private events.

Name: bellasLOKAL
Address: Langstraße 15, Bad Soden am Taunus, 65812, Germany
Description En: In a narrow village lane in the Altenhain district, chef-owner Isabelle Pering welcomes you to her restaurant done out in a tasteful, clean-lined style. With her set menu, which also comes in a vegetarian version, she demonstrates a knack for creating harmonious flavour combinations – this is where her experience gained at top-flight establishments shines through. Pleasingly minimalist dishes such as "Beef - Carrot - Hay" or "Asparagus - Tomato - Pimentos" also whet the appetite. The majority of the ingredients come from the region and most are certified organic. There is a well-curated wine list, as well as a lovely selection of wines by the glass and alcohol-free pairings to go with the set menu. Pretty terrace.

Name: CARUSO Pastabar
Description En: Neapolitan-born Anna and Marcello Caruso, working with Emanuele Barbaro, have come up with a cool concept: a flavoursome, relaxed and lively dining experience, played out in a chic atmosphere. Service comes courtesy of a relaxed, attentive team under the tutelage of the charming proprietress. They serve a three-course set menu, which you can put together yourself and add to as you wish – the main course is flavoursome house-made pasta! N.B. You should allow about two hours for three courses. There are two seatings: 6pm and 8.30pm. Trendy drinks at the bar.

Name: La Mer
Description En: Having earned his spurs at some award-winning restaurants, most recently at Seesteg, owner and head chef Hilko Uphoffis, together with his partner Giulia Casto, is at the helm of this smart restaurant located right next to the Michels Thalasso Hotel Nordseehaus, on the edge of the pedestrian/shopping zone. His classically French cuisine also demonstrates the odd modern flourish, as in the North Sea ling, cooked in nut butter, with lobster ravioli. The restaurant itself is also inviting, with its beautifully bright, pared-down and modern interior, as well as its appealing terrace laid out in front of the large window façade.

Name: Goldene Sonne
Description En: A quaint historical half-timbered building provides the setting where Heiner Bohnet and Constanza Piccolo welcome diners into their inviting dining space, which has retained its traditional charm. The pair approach their work with tremendous dedication and enthusiasm – she provides friendly and attentive service, and he creates a new vegetable-forward set menu every week, always guided by what is in season. Ingredients are sourced almost entirely from the local area (except for the responsibly line-caught fish from the coast of Brittany). The chef-patron is a member of a farming collective and grows his own vegetables. A great deal of fermenting, pickling and preserving is done in-house, plus they bake their own bread. Tip: They offer three lovely double rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Baron.ess
Description En: This trendy and stylish restaurant occupies an old bridge structure on the premises of the Brückenbaron events venue. When you enter, you can take a peek into the glass-enclosed kitchen before being seated in the airy dining space. The large windows look out onto landscaped grounds, complete with a pond and fountain. Gorgeous terrace. The modern set menu is made using seasonal produce. Vegetables feature prominently throughout. The same ingredient is often presented in various forms and textures. The service is very friendly, attentive and professional – the chefs are on hand to talk you through the dishes. On the wine list: organic, ecological and natural Franconian wineries.

Name: Pizarro Fine Dining
Description En: Stylish, modern and upscale, this small restaurant accommodates just 14 diners. The open kitchen allows you to watch chef Julio Pizarro Villanueva at work as he creates inventive dishes shaped both by his Peruvian heritage and his many years of international culinary experience. This fascinating combination of traditional Peruvian cuisine and Japanese influences is presented in the form of a set menu centred on fish and seafood. "Dry-aged kingfish sashimi, yuzu and Kys oyster" is a fine example of excellent ingredients and beautifully balanced preparation. A wine pairing or alcohol-free drinks accompaniment is also available. Service is agreeably relaxed, personable and professional. The chef himself comes to the table to talk you through his dishes, and his passion for his homeland and outstanding produce is palpable. The terrace overlooking the old half-timbered town hall is a lovely spot for an aperitif. N.B. The menu starts at 7.15pm (please arrive 6.30-7pm).

Name: AIMY
Description En: Fans of Thai cuisine are in good hands at this restaurant with an attractive decor, where diners can enjoy flavoursome dishes made from high-quality produce – authentic Thai flavours are guaranteed here. The dishes are accompanied by a varied selection of wines including some rarities. And the cocktail menu is also worth a look. There is also a delightful bar at the back of the restaurant. In summer, the seats in the inner courtyard are especially inviting.

Name: BAR TATAR in der Schreiberei
Description En: In the heart of the city, just a stone's throw from Marienplatz, this restaurant is on the ground floor of Munich's heritage-protected chancery (Schreiberei), where the city's history has been recorded since 1552. The attractive interior has a certain brasserie feel and, in good weather, the quiet sheltered courtyard terrace is especially inviting. Made with select ingredients, such as the veal cheeks with truffle polenta, the food is bursting with flavour. The tartare – there are many different variations, including meat, fish and vegetarian options – is a must. Be sure to try one of the delicious desserts, too. The varied à la carte selection is also ideal for sharing. When it comes to the excellent wine list, ask for a recommendation for a glass or bottle to accompany your meal.

Name: Kevin Gideon
Description En: Kevin Gideon and his restaurant have moved to a location outside the city centre, into premises that previously housed VINEO. Diners will be pleased to hear that the concept remains the same in the new space. The team is unchanged and the pared-back, modern style of the interior and of the food is also still present and correct. In their kitchen, which is visible through a glass partition, Kevin Gideon and his small team serve up a creative set menu (vegetarian version available); updated on a regular basis, it comprises three, five or seven courses. Friendly and professional service. In short: a restaurant run with great dedication and where the cooking is ambitious.

Name: Danza
Description En: On the first floor of the culture and congress centre, Forum am Schlosspark, an interesting restaurant and wine bar concept awaits you. The cuisine is modern, seasonal and international, but also has classical influences; dishes can be ordered as a set menu or à la carte. Good wines, friendly, attentive service and a chic, light and airy space. The terrace with a view over Kastanienallee is delightful. If you are coming by car, you can park on the Bärenwiese opposite.

Name: BRIKZ
Description En: At this restaurant in the heart of Charlottenburg – which used to be a jazz café – Arne Anker and his team serve up cuisine that is inspired by the seasons. Choose the five- to seven-course set menu (water included) or go à la carte; you can also put together your own menu from the à la carte selection, and it is possible to make this vegan. The wafer-thin slices of tender entrecôte and spicy guanciale served on wooden skewers are excellent – described by the chef himself with a wink as "our version of a Berlin kebab". The restaurant is happy to cater for food intolerances – it is best to let them know in advance. The alcohol-free drinks are also fabulous, with house-made kombucha, kefir, syrup, tea etc. The ambience is characterised by striking exposed brick walls and decorative art. The service is friendly and well organised, the atmosphere relaxed and informal – even the chef sometimes comes to diners at their tables. Pleasant pavement terrace.

Name: Bernhardhof
Description En: This delightfully chic and modern restaurant is to be found at the foot of the hill on which Andechs's famous abbey stands. The Holzinger family used to run a farm here, but nowadays they welcome diners with warmth and dedication. While the father handles the service, the son runs the kitchen with his mother's assistance, preparing delicious dishes using fresh ingredients and drawing on regional and international influences. Think sous-vide neck of Bavarian free-range pork with mashed potatoes, Dijon mustard, onion and pork jus, or roasted root chervil, peanut curry crunch, black cumin mayonnaise and orange yoghurt. You can also stay overnight here in one of the really comfortable and spacious maisonettes or suites.

Name: Anglerstuben
Description En: On the banks of the Rhine, this restaurant is tucked away behind a somewhat unprepossessing exterior directly above the angling club. The cuisine, based on excellent ingredients and with fish as the centrepiece, is a master class in finesse. In the evening, there are two five-course menus to choose from (as well as à la carte options); on weekdays, there is a very reasonably priced "Business Lunch" deal. They stock only German wines and the selection is outstanding. There is also a children's menu. The delicious food is served by friendly and attentive staff. In summer, make a beeline for the small terrace with a view of the Rhine and its jetties. Conveniently, the restaurant has a few parking spaces of its own.

Name: sansaro
Description En: The minimalist Japanese-style interior of the restaurant is inviting, as is the lovely verdant inner courtyard terrace. As well as sushi and sashimi (which you can also order omakase), the menu offers a five-course set menu with drink pairings, dubbed "Journey to Japan", and a small à la carte selection of Japanese dishes. The short explanations on the menu are a nice idea. There is also a terrific selection of sake and Japanese whiskies.

Name: nagare
Description En: Don't be fooled by the rather unspectacular exterior of this corner-plot building! Once inside, you will be immersed in a Far Eastern-style minimalist setting and have the chance to savour Nakagawa's Japanese creative cuisine, which draws on contemporary and French influences. Choose from set menus and à la carte options – sushi and vegetarian dishes are also present and correct. Only fish of the finest quality makes the cut. Professional service comes courtesy of polite, friendly waitstaff, who will gladly provide sake recommendations.

Name: KOSTBAR
Description En: Following Marco Akuzun's departure, Daniele di Fabio is the new head chef. As well as a good à la carte selection, a five-course set menu is served in the evening (vegetarian version available on request) and there is an attractive "business lunch" formula comprising two or three courses. The mouthwatering options include ricotta gnocchi with summer truffle and Parmesan, or guinea fowl saltimbocca with olive marinara sauce and basil purée. Furthermore, a creative tasting menu can be ordered in the evening. The upscale interior is both stylish and cosy, featuring warm wood and a minimalist design that creates a welcoming atmosphere. Lovely covered terrace with a working water wheel as the standout feature!

Name: Restaurant Max'es
Description En: A chic bistro vibe, friendly hospitality and good food are the hallmarks of the restaurant of the Hotel Wegner, a family-run business since 1957. The cuisine is modern and takes its cue from the changing seasons. The chefs like to give their dishes the finishing touch at your table when they serve, for example, cheese wheel pasta, crêpes Suzette or fillet of sole. Tip: Pre-order beef Wellington, Chateaubriand or the monthly changing set menu. In summer, be sure to secure a table on the quiet, leafy terrace! You can also come for breakfast.

Name: Salt & Silver am Meer
Address: Zum Böhler Strand, Sankt Peter-Ording, 25826, Germany
Description En: This restaurant is housed in an 8m-high building on stilts right by the beach, within spitting distance of the sea – an impressive location in which to enjoy fresh cuisine featuring produce from the region. At this "Fish Grill & Beach Bar", the tempting menu includes dishes such as grilled turbot and "fish fingers royal". Good to know: The chicken nuggets on the children's menu are made from regional organic poultry. Wine connoisseurs are bound to find something to their liking on the well-selected wine list. The atmosphere is nice and lively both inside and out on the fabulous terrace. Another Salt & Silver in addition to the two Hamburg restaurants. During the high season and on weekends, be sure to make a reservation. Tip: Park behind the dunes and enjoy the lovely 15min walk to the restaurant.

Name: Atelier Tian
Description En: The setting in the historic Veitsburg is truly something special. Once you reach the castle, not only does a magnificent view of Ravensburg await you… Christian Ott's ambitious cooking is inspired by international influences and the seasons. You can choose between "The Vegan Menu" and the "Atelier Tian Menu". Flexibility is key here: dishes can be combined into a personalised set menu of three to seven courses. Service is professional and friendly. There is also a dedicated cigar list. Tip: Make your reservation in good time – this place is popular with more than just the local crowd!

Name: Momo Ramen
Description En: Fancy some Japanese ramen? Then look no further! This hip and laid-back spot serves fresh house-made noodles. The aromatic dishes draw on regional ingredients and dispense with any additives. Reduced menu at lunchtime. An amusing detail: the toilets are wallpapered with Japanese newspapers.

Name: Gasthaus zum Adler
Description En: In the centre of this village right on the German Wine Route, this traditional inn at the foot of Landeck Castle is now run by the fifth generation of the same family, with two sisters breathing new life into the place. Christine Baumann presides in the kitchen, putting a Latin-American spin on Palatinate cuisine; Franziska Baumann provides friendly service. There is a short à la carte menu, from which you can also put together a three- or four-course meal. Regional wines accompany the seasonal cuisine. The appealingly modern, minimalist design successfully incorporates exposed old sandstone walls and wooden ceiling beams.

Name: Löwengrube
Description En: Since chef-patron Amadeus Kura took over, this former wine tavern has had a makeover – with fantastic results. The traditional character of the historical building has been intentionally preserved, and combined with sleek, modern elements. The chef's culinary vision is just as contemporary: he primarily uses regional ingredients but also draws on international influences. Delicious dishes such as northern Black Forest salmon trout with peach, pepper and cashews, or veal loin with aubergine and polenta are available in the evening either à la carte or as part of a five-course set menu. A similar selection is often served à la carte for lunch. The well-curated wine list includes a good selection of Baden labels. The sheltered terrace is a lovely spot in which to soak up the Old Town atmosphere. Parking tip: The restaurant is a stone's throw from Schlossberggarage.

Name: Roussel's Restaurant La Bonne Adresse
Description En: Thierry Roussel and Jane Kölchens run this place with dedication. The elegant restaurant exudes cosiness, and the extremely friendly service, directed by your hostess, also contributes to the pleasant atmosphere. At beautifully laid tables, upscale classic cuisine is served in the form of set menus (one vegetarian) or à la carte. They are also happy to share their wine recommendations, including some from their own production. Plus: guestrooms where you will feel right at home.

Name: Oma Wilma Heimatküche
Description En: This historical thatched-roof house in the heart of Keitum has bags of charm. Inside, diners enjoy an appealing modern take on Frisian decor; outside the gorgeous garden terrace beckons. The friendly front-of-house team provides pleasingly informal but professional service. The concept is dubbed "Heimatküche" – an ambitious blend of traditional and modern styles. A crowd favourite is the madras currywurst. Shorter menu at lunchtime followed by tempting coffee and cake options until 5pm. Tip: Be sure to book (only possible for the evening). The restaurant’s name pays tribute to the chef's grandmother.

Name: Zur Waage M.E.B.
Description En: This long-established restaurant enjoys a charming location in the town centre, directly on the Leda River – in summer, the lovely terrace with a view of the museum harbour beckons! Inside, you can expect all the trappings of a traditional inn with the odd rustic maritime touch. Mario E. Brüggemann, who began his culinary career here as an apprentice, prepares fresh, flavoursome cuisine rooted in regional traditions and seasonal produce. The menu features items such as shrimp soup, North Sea plaice fillets or a duo of venison. Lunch options are a little more limited.

Name: THE CLOUD by Käfer
Description En: Chef Jens Madsen serves up his extraordinary concept of "Culinary Nomadism", in which local ingredients meet global influences, at the equally special – and architecturally impressive – BMW Welt. For a year at a time, the spotlight is shone on a specific region of the world, its culinary traditions and techniques, spices etc. Each season brings with it change and progression – like a cloud moving through the sky. Inspired by his own trip to Africa, the chef takes you on a voyage of discovery of the flavours of East and South Africa. Top-quality produce goes into a tasting menu made up of eight elaborate courses promising a unique and immersive experience. In addition to wine, there are truly fantastic alcohol-free pairings. Extremely professional service is provided by a well-staffed front-of-house team – restaurant manager Mona Röthig (previously at Tantris Maison Culinaire) and sommelier Luigi Pecchia deserve a special mention. The interior is airy, light and minimalist, with upscale design. The large glass façade affords a view of BMW Welt. An illuminated cloud floating in the middle of the room reflects the movement and evolution of the food.

Name: PINK - DAS RESTAURANT
Description En: Located in the Haus für Kultur und Sport, in a quiet yet easily accessible area in Schwalbach-Hülzweiler, this restaurant is very popular. The interior with modern lines is tastefully decorated in a palette of calm, cheerful colours, and the broad, glazed façade means the space is lovely and bright. The seasonal and Mediterranean-inspired food is cooked meticulously and with attention to detail. The excellent à la carte selection ranges from beef carpaccio to truffle pasta and fried halibut. There is also a children's menu. Attentive service with a personal touch comes courtesy of the competent team.

Name: Anders auf dem Turmberg
Description En: From this impressive location high up on the Turmberg, the view over Karlsruhe and the Rhine Valley to the Vosges mountains is magnificent. Add to that tasty tapas-style cuisine – the smaller portions are perfect for sharing and sampling a selection. The food is cooked with quality ingredients, some regional, others Mediterranean. Dishes such as braised ox ribs on a corn cream with chilli or tuna with buttermilk and lime are fun to eat and showcase the skills of chef-patron Sören Anders, who is no stranger to the dining scene. The pared-back, modern interior with its large windows is attractive – tip: Aim to sit side by side so that everyone can enjoy the great view. During the day, small plates are served from the food truck in the courtyard.

Name: Brasserie Barbara
Description En: Open from noon to 8.30pm, Brasserie Barbara is an appealing daytime alternative to the fine dining restaurant here at the Auerhahn "wellness hotel", which is just across the road from the lake, Schluchsee. The bright, friendly atmosphere is inviting. The completely open kitchen produces cleverly devised dishes that are both bold and pleasingly uncomplicated. Based on top-notch ingredients, they are deeply rooted in regional culinary tradition. Options on the appealing à la carte menu include starters such as "Black Forest croquetas" or beef tartare with french fries, followed by a main course of local trout with a pepper salsa or fried black pudding with apple and mashed potatoes.

Name: PEYSK
Address: Westendstraße 73, Frankfurt on the Main, 60308, Germany
Description En: The name of this restaurant in the well-heeled Westend district is a Proto-Indo-European word meaning "fish", so it will come as no surprise that the cuisine is fish- and seafood-driven. The chef-patron spent time in Asia (including Singapore and Japan), before setting up shop here, and influences from his travels are reflected in "hamachi, wasabi, kosho, radish" and "octopus, mussel, curry, coconut, chilli, egg", for instance. The dishes are clearly structured and harmonious in taste, with interesting flavour combinations. There are also a few smaller plates, including oysters or sardines. The selection varies between à la carte options and a tasting menu of four or five courses. In summer, food is served on the terrace in front of the building – a pleasant, quiet spot in the shade.

Name: Grill Royal Hamburg
Description En: Right on Ballindamm, with a view of the Binnenalster and its fountain, the restaurant boasts a superb location. Inside, the place has an appealingly relaxed yet stylish feel, and the service is friendly and professional. Top-notch ingredients are beautifully prepared to create attractively presented dishes – don't miss the steak cuts from the grill (eg Black Angus sirloin or a 900g porterhouse). There are also seasonal specials, and seafood such as oysters and grilled fish. Order sides and sauces of your choice to accompany the dishes – our top tip if you are having beef is the chimichurri! For fine weather, there is a small terrace on the pavement in front of the restaurant.

Name: Sonne
Description En: The Rombach family (the business is in its seventh generation!) offer a cosy atmosphere in pretty rooms with wood panelling and exposed floorboards. The food is really good – a mix of traditional and modern ideas; the focus is on regional produce. Beautiful terrace. For overnight stays, the hotel of the same name has appealing, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: The CORD
Description En: The centrepiece in this sleek, chic restaurant is the 1937 Cord 810/812 after which it is named. The choice to exhibit this car, which was the most advanced of its time, is no coincidence, as the restaurant is located on the future-oriented EUREF campus, a model district for climate protection and resource conservation. The cuisine, based on select ingredients, is also of interest, with a good selection of modern dishes, including vegetarian and "Grill & Share" dishes, as well as Imperial caviar and a four-course signature menu. Conveniently, the S-Bahn is only a few minutes away.

Name: Château Royal
Description En: The elegant hotel Château Royal stands near the Brandenburg Gate, behind a dapper historical façade. Combining classical elements, design highlights and contemporary art in its impressively high-ceilinged rooms, it also houses a stylish restaurant with a lovely bar. The atmosphere is pleasingly intimate, and the cuisine bears the hallmarks of both Mediterranean and classic influences – the freshly made pasta is particularly popular. At lunchtime, the reasonably priced lunch set menu is a winner.

Name: Kaufmannsladen
Description En: Located in a small park, the Kieler Kaufmann hotel is accommodated in a building that was originally a banker's mansion, the first iteration of which was built in 1859. This is the hotel's relaxed, laid-back restaurant alternative to Ahlmanns. Floor-to-ceiling windows offer a view out onto the greenery, and the service is friendly and competent. The menu is characterised by North German influences and inspired by modern cuisine. The lunch deal is also popular.

Name: merold
Description En: Merold promises "new German cuisine" – top-notch ingredients from Berlin and the surrounding Brandenburg region. Often pared back to just a few components, the dishes deliver a hit of flavour and intensity. The signature "onion, buckwheat, black garlic" is a particular highlight. In the four- or five-course set menu, each course consists of two dishes – optional add-ons include cheese or the superb house-made bratwurst. They also have a well-curated wine list. The modern, pared-back decor is inviting, and the service is attentive, knowledgeable and agreeably relaxed. Chef-patron Jonas Merold himself frequently puts in an appearance on the restaurant floor, greeting diners and introducing his creations.

Name: Auerhahn
Description En: Following the reopening of Hotel Auerhahn, owner Marius Tröndle (who also runs Mühle in Schluchsee) has appointed an ambitious new head chef to lead his fine dining restaurant. After stints at various MICHELIN-starred establishments, Yann Bosshammer now oversees a kitchen dedicated to modern, seasonally inspired dishes crafted from premium regional produce, such as "grilled salsify, quince, black garlic" or "Albbruck brook trout, tonka bean, pear". If you are not staying at the hotel, book your table for the "Fine Dining Menu" in advance. The setting is lovely; the beautifully modernised space has retained original features such as the wood-panelled ceiling and striking traditional tiled stove. Diners enjoy friendly service in comfortable alcoves that foster a certain sense of intimacy. The hotel itself, tastefully refurbished, is also an inviting option for an overnight stay.

Name: Dorf-Chronik
Description En: This attractive winegrower's house dating back to 1747 stands in the centre of the town. Stefan Püngeler and his wife Michela De Munno – well-known figures in the region – have taken over the reins here after a successful run at Restaurant Schneider in Dernbach. He is in charge of the kitchen, and she is responsible for the friendly service. On the menu: flavoursome Italian fare – the house-made pasta is a particular highlight. The tiramisu, presented on a dessert trolley and freshly portioned tableside, is truly delicious. Rump steak – practically a staple in the region – is also available. The wine list features moderately priced labels from the region. Sandstone and half-timbering create a cosy atmosphere, and the courtyard terrace is delightful in summer.

Name: Obere Mühle
Description En: From the outside, the carefully restored centuries-old farmhouse is really inviting; inside, wonderfully quaint rooms featuring rustic wood panelling ooze regional charm. The cuisine, too, is rooted in the Allgäu region, but with the occasional foray into the Mediterranean. The menu ranges from offal to various meats cooked on the charcoal grill, from locally farmed fresh fish to pasta and delicious desserts. Their commitment is plain to see, not least in the quality and provenance of the ingredients. In addition to the appealing à la carte selection, there is also a daily menu. The food is accompanied by good wines. Friendly, attentive service ensures a pleasant, family atmosphere. The restaurant also has its own organic cheese dairy. Tip: Bad Hindelang's local history museum is located here, too. Overnight guests staying in the holiday apartments enjoy access to the wellness area.

Name: RAUSCH
Address: Reuterweg 57, Frankfurt on the Main, 60323, Germany
Description En: Jochim Busch has established RAUSCH on the premises that used to house Gustav, the restaurant in which he made a name for himself with his MICHELIN-starred cuisine. Here, he serves up accessible modern food. The bold dishes are notable for their contrasting flavours, always judiciously pared back, and the ingredients are of excellent quality. This approach is evident, for instance, in the super-fresh and tender raw marinated white prawns accompanied by an aromatic buttermilk emulsion enriched with crisp salted cucumber brunoise and the citrus aromas of grand fir tree. The chef serves up a four- or five-course set menu, with two additional dishes to choose from. From some tables in the chic and minimalist space, the open kitchen is visible. Service is laid-back and attentive, with staff always on hand and attentive yet pleasantly unobtrusive. The well-stocked wine list with a penchant for German and French picks is excellent.

Name: GRETA OTO Frankfurt
Address: Thurn-und-Taxis-Platz 2, Frankfurt on the Main, 60313, Germany
Description En: Above the upscale bar on the ground floor of the JW Marriott Hotel Frankfurt in the city centre, you come to this stylish and elegantly designed restaurant on the first floor. The charming team serves up a slice of Latin America, from tacos and "ceviche GRETA OTO" (take your pick from salmon, sea bass or king prawns) to mushroom karaage, aji verde sauce and cashews. Pick your dishes à la carte – they are designed for sharing.

Name: Mokuli
Description En: Behind its orange façade with an original design, this trendy restaurant is chic and airy with its modern, minimalist look, three striking paintings, open kitchen and large floor-to-ceiling windows that make it wonderfully bright. The international seasonal dishes include "two types of yellowfin tuna, romanesco, cauliflower, artichoke" and "venison from Gutshof Polting, chanterelles, celery, watermelon". In the evening, two set menus are served, one of which is vegetarian and each comprising four or six courses. Alternatively, you can choose individual dishes à la carte. At lunchtime, the three-course lunch deal, available in an omnivore or vegetarian version, is reasonably priced and popular. There is also a bar where you are welcome to simply enjoy a drink. Lovely terrace in front of the restaurant.

Name: Bob & Thoms
Description En: Owner Oliver Körber, who treats diners to authentic Berlin-style hospitality, and chef Ruben Pahl cook up a pleasingly unaffected gastro concept as a two-man operation. Located in a quiet side street between the small Viktoria-Luise-Platz, laid out in 1899, and the department store KaDeWe, the restaurant delivers a five-course set menu, plus two dishes as an optional extra. Just a handful of components go into the fantastic, classically based dishes. Delicious examples include the flavoursome lobster soup with vanilla radish or the perfectly cooked saddle of venison with a robust venison jus and Brussels sprouts. The attractive interior is quite minimalist, with interesting photographs of Berlin and New York (taken by Oliver Körber's daughter) adding a decorative element. There are only a few spots up for grabs each evening, so be sure to book in good time! In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous little terrace!

Name: Chapeau La Vache
Description En: Housed in a stately villa in the Bürgerpark, this restaurant exudes elegance. The open reception area with its gorgeous wooden staircase creates an immediate welcoming impression. High stuccoed ceilings, lovely hardwood floors, muted colours, striking chandeliers and decorative modern pictures make for an atmospheric setting. Waitstaff are friendly and experienced. The menu features brasserie-style dishes inspired by classic French recipes – the bouillabaisse or beef bourguignon are a real treat!

Name: Schlosspark Restaurant by Tristan Brandt
Description En: Tristan Brandt has found a fantastic setting for his new fine dining concept here. The location right next to the castle park is wonderful – the terrace is a truly idyllic spot! Inside, mouldings are combined with modern elements to create a chic interior. The cuisine strikes a successful balance of diverse styles, with a menu that includes Flammkuchen and cake in the afternoon, as well as Tristan Brandt's specials such as truffle fries or caviar, alongside such classics as Wiener schnitzel with warm potato salad or char and beef fillet.

Name: Krone Schlier
Description En: In a charming location between Lake Constance and the Allgäu, just a few kilometres from Ravensburg, this lovely restaurant serving excellent cuisine is run by the Geßler family. Chef-patron Benedikt Geßler comes from a family of restaurateurs and has worked in several renowned kitchens. Here, he cooks modern, seasonal dishes, placing great importance on organic and Demeter produce. Choose one of two set menus ("Chef Menu" and "Végétal Menu"), from which, alternatively, you can order à la carte. The setting is extremely inviting, too, with friendly, professional staff serving you in a cosy interior with stylish details such as old oak floors, smart cherry-wood panelling and chic, comfortable seats. There is also a pretty terrace.

Name: O'NE
Description En: This appealingly lively restaurant is located inside the Marc O'Polo Strandcasino store, just a stone's throw from the sea and the promenade. Modern dishes with both regional and international influences are served in an attractive trendy setting. Tables are laid out on a mezzanine overlooking the store, with some seats offering a glimpse into the kitchen. Service is friendly and professional. During the summer, the terrace outside beckons.

Name: Kitten Deli
Description En: The atmosphere here is friendly and vibrant, both on the terrace, with tables laid out on the street in front of the restaurant, and inside, where diners are seated at small tables (no tablecloths here), and old floorboards, panelled walls and a counter make for a traditional tavern-like atmosphere. The restaurant serves vegetarian Levante cuisine, including dishes that are perfect for sharing, such as hummus with roasted cauliflower or shakshuka. The delicious pita (flatbread) and the aromatic challah (yeast-leavened bread) come fresh from the oven – both can also be purchased to take home.

Name: EGERN 51
Description En: The location on the promenade is fabulous – in summer, tables on the terrace overlooking Egerner Bucht (Egern Bay) are in great demand! But you can also take in the vista from indoors – the window seats in this cosy modern restaurant are popular, too. The kitchen draws its inspiration from Euro-Asian cuisine. Featuring a diverse range of options, from classic favourites to Mediterranean and Asian-influenced dishes, the menu has something for everyone. Friendly and adept service.

Name: Ambiente Italiano
Description En: Dating from 1902, this inviting villa entices guests with its scenic location and excellent cuisine that caters to all tastes. In the trattoria, the menu features Italian classics, pasta made in-house or freshly caught fish, as well as a selection of pizzas. Ristorante Ambiente Italiano, meanwhile, serves more sophisticated dishes that draw on Italian influences. The terrace with its stunning views of the Main River is a summer highlight! The service is friendly and attentive. Good to know: There is a car park directly in front of the building.

Name: HENSSLER
Description En: This location between Holzhafen and the Altona Fish Market can be aptly described as "typically Hamburg". The restaurant of the Henssler family stands amid countless fishmongers and seafood shops. The decor is minimalist and chic, and the atmosphere is informal and lively. In the 20m-wide kitchen, a diverse range of modern sushi creations are prepared, as well as dishes such as "Atlantic cod, black cod-style" or "US rumpsteak tataki". Senior chef Werner Henssler himself gets involved in the service. Booking ahead is recommended for both lunch and dinner.

Name: Cølbo
Description En: Armed with an impressive CV, chef-patron Moritz Techet presents his modern, creative concept here. Diners are treated to a surprise menu comprising 10 smaller or larger courses, each one technically polished and precisely executed. Each dish is pared down to the essentials and based on select, predominantly regional ingredients. The restaurant maintains its own herb garden, they forage for mushrooms and berries, and employ fermentation and preservation techniques. Vegetarian cuisine is at the fore. The charming and dedicated waitstaff are led by Jansý Frederiksberg and assisted by the chefs, who personally elaborate on their dishes. Both the wine and alcohol-free pairings match the set menu beautifully. The minimalist, clean-lined interior design is extremely chic – ask for a table with a view of the castle! Capacity is limited and in high demand, so booking is recommended. N.B. The meal begins at 7pm for all diners.

Name: Zum Ackerbürger Can Basar
Description En: This long-standing inn in Stuttgart's Bad Cannstatt district is in one of the area's oldest half-timbered buildings, dating back to the 15C. The setting is cosy and rustic, with lots of aged wood creating a charming, old-world atmosphere. The kitchen is headed by Can Basar, who previously worked at several renowned establishments. The menu includes seasonal and international cuisine alongside timeless classics – the roast beef is a favourite. In addition to an à la carte selection, there is also a four- or five-course set menu.

Name: WELA
Description En: This little restaurant in the city centre promises a truly authentic Thai dining experience. Premium ingredients are precisely prepared for optimum flavour – the chef hails from Thailand and brings experience from esteemed establishments. In the evenings, guests can choose between a five- or eight-course set menu. On Wed, Thu and Sat, a shortened menu is served at lunchtime. The setting is upscale and tastefully designed, enhanced by attractive Thai decorative elements. The two very cordial proprietors provide attentive and adept service. Travel tip: The restaurant is not far from the main railway station and is well connected to public transport. Drivers can use the multi-storey car park in Stresemannstraße.

Name: OTSUKA
Description En: In this tiny – perhaps even the smallest – restaurant in Berlin, authentic sushi is served in a minimalist setting as an affordably priced omakase menu. The nigiri are the highlight: crafted with excellent ingredients and impressive skill by the owner, who prepares them right before your eyes and presents them himself from behind the simple wooden counter. There are three seatings: 1pm, 5pm and 8pm. N.B. The restaurant is somewhat hidden inside a building directly at Nordbahnhof that also houses an organic supermarket.

Name: JAJA
Description En: The vibe here is lively, loud and hip, yet an intimate atmosphere reigns in the minimalist interior done out in a trendy rustic style. The menu revolves around modern plates for sharing – based on organic ingredients, dishes such as "mussels, spaghetti, XO sauce" or "pork belly, red cabbage, horseradish" are deliciously prepared and complemented by a fine selection of natural wines. The owner is a sommelier – let her guide you!

Name: Arc Restaurant
Description En: This small, tastefully designed restaurant with its modern, minimalist aesthetic is deservedly much sought after. Thanks to the fully open kitchen, you can watch at close quarters how a 10-course pescatarian menu takes shape. The modern, creative dishes may seem simple at first glance, but reveal remarkable complexity and detail. A fine example is the lightly cooked, meltingly tender fillet of brook trout, served with mushrooms, fresh horseradish and artichoke purée, accompanied by a creamy, aromatic mushroom sauce. Fermented and preserved elements are also incorporated. The attentive team will gladly tell you all about each creation. Information about the carefully selected seasonal produce – sourced largely from the surrounding Hamburg region – is presented in the restaurant's "Freundebuch". A vegetarian version of the set menu is also available. It is certainly worth perusing the nicely curated wine list. The set menu can be paired with wines or house-made alcohol-free accompaniments.

Name: Brasserie Tafern
Description En: Elegant yet accessible – a concept designed with your comfort and well-being in mind, and a wonderful alternative to Epicures, the fine dining restaurant here at the Boutique Hotel Residenz Winkler. Executive Chef Daniel Pape is the man responsible for both kitchens, and the classic and Mediterranean cuisine impresses with its finesse and lightness. It can be sampled from an appealing à la carte selection (eg "artichoke consommé, tomato concassé" or " Senfrostbraten (pork roast with mustard, rainbow vegetables, red onion"), which is complemented by seasonal daily specials. In fine weather, diners can enjoy the view of the Chiemgau Alps from the magnificent terrace (Bergterrasse). Good to know: It opens at 3pm, and at noon on Sundays. Fun fact: The name "Tafern" is a throwback to the establishment's roots – as far back as the early 15C there was a tavern on this site.

Name: Gestütsgasthof Offenhausen
Description En: On the idyllic grounds of Marbach stud farm, which is steeped in history, the centuries-old steward's house has been turned into a tasteful and cosy restaurant. Here, chef-patron Marc Winter serves up his regional and seasonal dishes, to which he adds just the right dose of modernity. Game is hunted by the chef or his hunter friends to appear in tempting dishes such as roast venison shoulder in juniper cream or cordon bleu of wild boar loin with a hazelnut crumb topping. The menu also includes smaller bites. The lovely terrace commands a view of the surrounding historical buildings including the 13C monastery church, which now houses the stud farm museum (Gestütsmuseum). Incidentally, the source of the Lauter River is also located on the site.

Name: Löwen
Description En: In Söflingen, a district of Ulm, the historic courtyard of a former Clarissan convent dating from 1258 is home to an attractive hotel with individually designed rooms and a lovely restaurant. In the modern setting that has been created within the old walls, a friendly, attentive team serves delicious dishes made with carefully sourced ingredients. The accomplished chef presents a focused à la carte selection of classics, including cheese spaetzle tartufo, roast beef, and caviar specialities. On Tue there is an additional three-course schnitzel menu; Wed-Sat, a fine dining set menu of four, six or seven courses – think "scallop, onion, hazelnut" or "veal neck, mushroom, cabbage, truffle". A vegetarian version is also available. Well-chosen wine list.

Name: Das Philippin
Description En: Café, bistro, restaurant – this family-run establishment in the compact pedestrian area of Rutesheim is all of the above. Opened in 1987 as a café by Mr & Mrs Striegel (both pastry chefs), it has since blossomed into a sophisticated restaurant. Breakfast and lunch, as well as coffee and cake are served during the day; in the evening, Tim Striegel (the son) serves up his fine dining concept. The set menu comprises three to five imaginative courses, each meticulously prepared using excellent ingredients – the "Norway lobster, cauliflower, yuzu, almond" and "venison from the Leonberg hunt, celery, cranberry, parsley" are two cases in point. Harmonious wine pairings are also available on request. The predominantly German wine list is appealing. N.B. In July and August, à la carte dishes and a small surprise menu are served on the terrace in the evening – the fine dining menu is suspended during this period.

Name: BRASSERIE Schwarzenstein
Description En: In this chic brasserie in a glass-paned pavilion at Burg Schwarzenstein, you can savour a wonderful view (also magnificent from the terrace!) and market-fresh French cuisine – from starters such as "escargots de vigne en cocotte" to meat and fish dishes such as "choucroute Schwarzenstein" or sole meunière, and, for dessert, île flottante. You also have the option of oysters and caviar. The well-stocked wine list homes in on German and French labels. Tip: For the optimum experience, consider staying overnight – there are lovely individually styled guestrooms distributed across the Parkresidenz, Burghotel and Guesthouse.

Name: Tante Anna
Description En: With experience under renowned chefs such as Heinz Winkler, Tohru Nakamura and Anton Gschwendtner under his belt, Thies Henkel, alongside his wife Pia, has taken over this restaurant in her hometown. Behind the traditional shingle-clad façade, guests dine in tasteful and charmingly elegant surroundings while enjoying service overseen by the proprietress, who is friendly, attentive and never overbearing. In the three- to five-course set menu, the chef-patron showcases outstanding ingredients in a modern, flavour-rich style shaped by numerous Japanese influences. Fine examples include "Balfegó tuna akami, assorted radishes, toro, dashi" and "Hereford beef short rib, shiitake, leek, bone marrow, smoked soy sauce". The Saturday lunchtime special "Schnitzel Mittach" is also of interest: Wiener schnitzel with potato salad and lingonberries. Tip: Ask for a table in the bright airy conservatory with its lovely garden view – in summer, the terrace is extremely popular too.

Name: mokum
Description En: This lovely little restaurant is right next to Theresienwiese. It only has eight tables, so it's best to book if you are keen to tuck into their excellent, reasonably priced cuisine in a wonderfully relaxed atmosphere. The small à la carte selection is tempting, with dishes such as "yellowtail, radish, leek, mild habanero" or "pâté en croûte, duck, pork, plum". The dishes are also ideal for sharing. There is an excellent wine selection, including wines by the glass. Tip: "Bites for Bubbles" are designed to pair with a glass of champagne. The fact that guests feel at home here is at least partly down to the warm, professional and approachable service team – everyone works together seamlessly, and the chefs serve their dishes themselves.

Name: the dune
Address: Paul-Ehrlich-Straße 9, Frankfurt on the Main, 60596, Germany
Description En: The fine dining restaurant of luxury hotel The Florentin has an urban and cosmopolitan feel. Its upscale and thoughtfully designed interior provides the perfect backdrop for Niclas Nußbaumer's set menu, which is built around excellent international ingredients. His cooking focuses confidently on the essentials. Technically accomplished and refreshingly direct in style, his dishes impress with elegant, beautifully harmonious flavours, "sea bream, teardrop peas & vin jaune" and "Théo Kieffer squab, salsify & red cabbage kosho jus" being two cases in point. A vegetarian version is also available – ideally, please mention this at the time of booking. Service is very warm and professional: charming and approachable, yet polished, the team led by restaurant manager Lea Rupp ensures a relaxed evening.

Name: Bornheimer Ratskeller
Address: Kettelerallee 72, Frankfurt on the Main, 60385, Germany
Description En: A fantastic concept showcasing regional cuisine at outstanding value for money. The kitchen takes its cue from the changing seasons, and the menu provides information about the restaurant's nose-to-tail approach and the provenance of the ingredients. The dishes change daily according to availability and are only revealed when the restaurant opens at 5pm. Many items are so popular that they appear time and again, such as Odenwälder Handkäse (a traditional Odenwald soft cheese) or a delicious pâté. The inviting tavern-style interior and very friendly service create a charming atmosphere in which to savour good food.

Name: Chobab
Description En: "Sushi meets Korean flavours" is the concept behind this centrally located restaurant near the pedestrianised zone. Expect expertly prepared nigiri and creative fusion sushi – the chef draws on experience gained at renowned locations such as Moriki in Baden-Baden, Feinkost Böhm in Stuttgart and the local restaurant named 5. The "Special Roll" is especially worth trying. The aesthetic is modern and minimalist, and from the counter you can watch the sushi master at work.

Name: Lisa Marie
Description En: A delightfully unpretentious restaurant run by a pleasant team in Coburg's old town. The modern interior is lovely, and the service is friendly, attentive and professional. Seasonal dishes with international influences are rustled up in the partially visible kitchen. The lunch menu is somewhat more limited. Tip: Visit the palace, Schloss Ehrenburg, opposite. For motorists: There are two underground car parks (Albertplatz and Mauer) underground car park just a four-minute walk from the restaurant.

Name: Kakehashi
Description En: This place is a mecca for good, authentic Japanese food. Top-notch fresh ingredients go into the set menus – a two-course sushi and sashimi set, six-course "Mini Omakase" and seven-course "Koichi's Special". Subtle Franconian elements also make occasional appearances. These dishes are accompanied by Japanese Kirin Ichiban beer on tap or sake from an enticing selection. The upscale interior has clean-lined Far Eastern aesthetics – the five tables at the counter with a view of the open kitchen are particularly prized. It is from this vantage point that diners can best observe the craftsmanship of chef Koichiro Yoshida. The extremely pleasant, almost family-like atmosphere is due in no small part to the truly cordial service, which ensures that you immediately feel at home.

Name: Landersdorfer & Innerhofer
Description En: With their delicious, classic-based cuisine, served in a pleasingly down-to-earth space, friends Johann Landersdorfer and Robert Innerhofer draw throngs of diners to their restaurant in Munich's city centre. Chef-patron Johann Landersdorfer ensures that dishes such as "guinea fowl and duck liver terrine with cranberries" or "cod medallions and patties, chive sauce and potato salad" are meticulously prepared using top-notch ingredients. In the evening, the four-course menu can be extended with add-ons. At lunchtime, choose between a two-course set lunch or eating à la carte. In addition, the experienced, ever-present front-of-house team provides pleasingly relaxed yet attentive service, as well as wine recommendations that pair harmoniously with the food. The wine list is terrific and includes a handful of rarities alongside an array of top-notch wines.

Name: Rive Gauche
Description En: This restaurant boasts a fantastic location on Lichtentaler Allee, right next to the Museum Frieder Burda and Museum LA8. In the clean-lined conservatory of the beautiful historic building, you can tuck into an appealing three-course lunch set menu as well as "petites bouchées" such as French onion tart or croque monsieur. In the evening, the cuisine moves up a gear, with dishes such as marinated venison loin with Waldorf salad or wild-caught monkfish with braised pointed cabbage and chorizo. Eduard Knecht, who previously cooked at Alte Baiz in Neuhausen, heads up the kitchen. In summer, the terrace is a real highlight.

Name: Fukagawa Ramen XBerg
Description En: You would be well advised to book at this Kreuzberg ramen restaurant, as it gets very busy at both lunchtime and in the evening. The focus is on tasty Japanese ramen, such as "shoyu ramen – matured soy sauce, chashu chicken, dashi, handmade noodles, marinated egg, nori". Tip: The gyoza are a great starter! There is also an interesting selection of drinks, including sake, wines and cocktails. The decor is pared back, in a minimalist urban style, and the service is quick and friendly.

Name: GenussWerkstatt
Description En: A unique concept for a business travellers' hotel. At this restaurant housed in the conveniently located Atrium Hotel in Mainz-Finthen, a single eight-course set menu is served simultaneously to all diners. The chefs finish the contemporary dishes in the dining room and explain them at the table. Wine pairings are also available to accompany their creations, which are crafted using predominantly regional ingredients. The setting is sleek and modern, and service is friendly and adept.

Name: EssKultur
Description En: With delicious food, friendly service, a welcoming and charming vibe, this restaurant in a residential area just outside the city centre is a magnet for diners. The contemporary cuisine makes use of predominantly regional produce. The meticulously prepared and beautifully plated dishes are served in the format of a four- or five-course set menu, with vegetarian alternatives for the meat/fish courses – and it is possible to opt for the "upgrade", an additional course. Wine or alcoholic drinks pairings are available. The space is sleek and modern yet cosy, and tables are set up on a terrace on the pavement outside.

Name: Winkler Bräu
Description En: The culinary tradition of this building dates back to 1428. Cosy traditional parlours are testament to its long history – heavy timber ceilings, dark wood-panelled walls, lovely hardwood floors and old paintings create a charmingly rustic setting. The old-world feel of the interior is complemented by a modern conservatory and a terrace. The regional, seasonal cuisine is based on carefully selected ingredients, with dishes such as Schneemühl char with garden herbs and potato salad, or the classic roast Swabian-Hall pork with crackling and potato dumplings. Diners can either opt for the four-course "Gutshof Menu" or order à la carte. A reduced menu is served at lunchtime and in the afternoon. The property also has its own brewery (showcased in the exhibition "TraditionsReich Kupfer") and a brewery shop. Comfortable accommodation is offered in the adjoining hotel, which includes spa facilities.

Name: Dopamin
Description En: The impressive location right on the banks of the River Saar is one draw; Axel Boesen's cuisine is another. He cooks in a modern, creative style, bringing in Asian and Nordic influences and dreaming up exciting combinations. He pulls it all together with surgical precision, for dishes that are robust and full of finesse. There is a four-, six- or seven-course set menu and, to go with it, wines from a selection dominated by Riesling and Pinot Noir from the Saar and Moselle regions. The small, high-ceilinged dining area has a sophisticated, chic, modern-elegant interior, which makes for a pleasingly relaxed atmosphere. The windows afford views onto the river and the imposing castle opposite – a fantastic backdrop, especially for al fresco dining on the balcony. If you wish to dine at the "Chef's Table" at the counter, the full set menu is the only option. The pleasant team provide polite and discreet, yet friendly and relaxed service. The restaurant is housed in the charming Villa Keller, dating from 1801, which also offers very tasteful overnight accommodation. This family-run establishment is the sister business of Erasmus hotel in Trassem.

Name: Der Philosoph
Description En: This welcoming restaurant established by a pair of chefs is set in the charming district of Neuenheim. Attractive decorative features such as large-format black-and-white photographs, bold red accents and the open-view kitchen all help to create an inviting atmosphere, complemented by exceptionally courteous service. There is a choice of three set menus, one of which is vegetarian, with the possibility to order dishes individually à la carte. The Chateaubriand set menu for two needs to be pre-ordered – the main course is presented with the classic béarnaise sauce and potato gratin. The restaurant takes its name from its location at the foot of the Philosophenweg, a well-known and much-loved walking path overlooking the Old Town and the castle across the Neckar River.

Name: bistro in der remise
Description En: The magnificent estate of Schloss Hugenpoet, which dates back to 1647, is a truly remarkable location. Here – in the converted coach house, to be precise – the atmosphere is relaxed and casual, yet the decor is stylish; listed elements of the former stables lend a special touch. From your table you can see into the open kitchen, where dishes are prepared with traditional, international and seasonal influences – from beef Bourguignon to flambéed salmon sashimi and mushroom and buckwheat risotto. In the afternoon, there is a selection of light snacks and cakes. The terrace in the courtyard with a view of the castle is lovely in summer. Planted with mature trees, the grounds are perfect for a stroll.

Name: elfbuchen
Description En: The appeal of the Waldhotel Elfbuchen goes beyond its superb tranquil location in a forest clearing at 536m above sea level – its restaurant draws visitors with fine cooking too. The kitchen presents modern dishes inspired by the seasons and the region, with game sourced from the hotel's own hunting grounds. Precisely prepared dishes packed with flavour are served either à la carte or as a set menu by an attentive and professional front-of-house team. Choose to dine in the cheerful modern interior or out on the lovely terrace. On Sundays, the café serves cakes and tortes from the family's own patisserie. Tip: The UNESCO World Heritage Site Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe and the famous Hercules Monument, both about a 20min walk away, are well worth exploring.

Name: Wirtshaus Huberwirt
Description En: With chef-patron Alexander Huber and hostess Sandra Huber at the helm, this long-standing family business is now run by the 11th generation. Regional cuisine is served either à la carte or as a three- to five-course "Wirtshausmenü", with optional wine pairings. Highlights include jellied catfish and sturgeon with herb sauce, cabbage and root vegetables, or boiled beef shoulder and bone marrow with roast potatoes, apple and horseradish sauce, and spinach. A children's menu is also available. The restaurant consists of two inviting dining rooms, their striking old wooden ceilings testament to over 400 years of history. Open for lunch at weekends – booking recommended. For a more elevated dining experience, the separate Restaurant Alexander Huber is located at the rear of the property.

Name: NICE
Description En: Housed in a newly built complex in the Werksviertel, a neighbourhood close to Munich's Ostbahnhof station, this restaurant presents a stylish, contemporary interior. Diners can sit at the counter overlooking the kitchen, at the bar, at high tables or in one of the booths. Floor-to-ceiling windows mean the space is flooded with natural light during the day. Dishes are freshly prepared with great care and technical skill. Mouthwatering examples include poulet noir with swede, cabbage and capers, or golden trout with borscht broth, sweet pepper, lángos and chervil. Lunch features a streamlined menu with daily specials; in the evening, there is a four-course set menu and an appealing à la carte selection. The wine list may be concise, but it is refined and well devised. Tip for motorists: PARK ONE underground parking facility. Thanks to the long opening hours (Mon-Fri 9am-midnight, Sat 6pm-midnight), a good option for weekday coffee and croissants or an after-work drink in the evening.

Name: Schlossschänke auf dem Johannisberg
Description En: In an annexe of the centuries-old Schloss Johannisberg – the world's first Riesling wine estate – this bright, friendly restaurant has a wonderful conservatory and terrace. Thanks to its elevated location, it commands a wonderful view of the region and the Rhine. The food is fresh, classic cuisine with seasonal and regional influences served in a four- or five-course set menu format or à la carte. Appetising options include "Schloss Bouillabaisse", beef tenderloin Wellington, braised beef roulade and crêpes Suzette flambéed tableside. Various types of caviar also feature on the menu. Simple regional plates such as Spundekäs (spiced cream cheese) or "Rheingauer Schnittchen" (crusty bread with spreads) are also delicious with a glass of wine. Tip: There is also a wine shop.

Name: Harzfenster by Johannes Steingrüber
Description En: An exclusive little area in Hotel Görtler has been carved out for this restaurant. Its colour scheme echoes the surrounding nature – the tables upholstered in forest-green Alcantara are particularly striking. There is an open kitchen area, where diners can see some of the dishes being finished and plated up. The atmosphere is cosy and intimate, and the service is charming and relaxed yet sophisticated – thanks to the team, from the sommelier to the chefs, including chef-patron Johannes Steingrüber himself. With its creative, pleasingly pared-back combinations, the seven- to 10-course menu makes an impression – bold dishes such as "Jerusalem artichoke, shiso, pepper" or "pigeon, papaya, Puy lentils" are full of personality and harmoniously balanced intensity. Clearly discernible Asian influences add refined touches. To go with the food, there are wine pairings or an alcohol-free alternative.

Name: Theodor's
Description En: This restaurant in the Beuel district has an inviting, chic and contemporary feel. At the helm are siblings Jana and Fritz Benson, who go about their work with palpable dedication. In the open kitchen, the chef-patron and his team put together a creative seasonal set menu, available in four to six courses, which can be supplemented with optional additional courses. The craftsmanship on display and the quality of the produce impress in equal measure – a case in point is the Dieppe scallops with a fruity, tangy pineapple vinaigrette, finished with a delicate mace-infused foam. Each dish is also presented in a pleasingly clean, unfussy style. The front-of-house team, headed up by the proprietress herself, provides attentive, expert service, with the chefs also known to lend a hand. Motorists can park at the Tiefgarage Rathausplatz.

Name: Das Palmberger - hoamART
Description En: In a pleasingly relaxed setting, diners are treated to dishes brimming with flavour and culinary flair. Alongside time-honoured classics such as Wiener schnitzel of veal with fried potatoes and cranberries or Zwiebelrostbraten (braised beef with onions and gravy) with cheese spaetzle and a rosemary and thyme jus, the kitchen also turns out more contemporary dishes: "Black salsify soup, beetroot, cream cheese, parsley" or "Zander, cucumber, mustard, dill". There is a three- or four-course set menu (meat/fish or vegetarian) as well as à la carte options. Clean lines, warm natural tones and tasteful floral touches create an inviting modern vibe. The professional and friendly service team is attentive but discreet. The restaurant is part of Das Palmberger hotel, which offers comfortable accommodation.

Name: Ente Wiesbaden - Pfortenhaus Kloster Eberbach
Description En: This restaurant steeped in tradition moved in March 2026 from the Nassauer Hof in Wiesbaden to Eberbach Monastery. It is in the historic gatehouse (Pfortenhaus) that Michael Kammermeier now serves up his modern-inspired cuisine in the form of considered, meticulously crafted and flavoursome dishes made with excellent-quality produce. Of the two set menus, "Küchenrunde" and "Querbeet", the latter is the vegetarian version. Both are available in a five- to eight-course format and include dishes such as "salmon trout from the Wispertal Forellenhof Seitz, horseradish, radishes, grapes, verjus, lovage". The service certainly lives up to the high standards set by the kitchen team: led by Jimmy Ledemazel, the waitstaff are attentive, personable and professional. A lovely touch: To make regulars feel at home, parts of the classic interior have been brought along, including pictures and the cheese trolley.

Name: The Tourist Trap
Description En: What a cool setting this is! On the upper deck of a historical museum ship moored on the Neckar River, this stylish space is imbued with vintage flair. The vibe is fresh, youthful and relaxed. Windows on all sides afford fantastic views, and in fine weather guests can sit out on the open deck. Dennis Maier, who most recently earned a MICHELIN star for Mannheim's Emma Wolf since 1920, has transformed the museum ship from the "tourist trap" (that inspired the name) into a culinary hotspot. He and his accomplished kitchen team serve two seven-course set menus (one of which is vegetarian), plus a number of little extras. The modern, seasonal dishes are inventive, technically precise and packed with flavour. Menu prices vary according to the day of the week. Guests simply dropping by for a glass of wine can order small bites from the "Munchies" menu. On Sundays, the three-course "Easy Sunday Menu" is available from 1pm. Tip: From 6pm, you can park for free near the jetty in the MVV car park.

Name: Restaurant Mohn
Description En: Laura Überschär and Joris Hogervorst have been running this charming country house since September 2024. Having worked at respected establishments in Germany and his native Netherlands, the chef showcases his talent through clever combinations of seasonal ingredients. Regional produce goes into delicious vegetable-forward dishes with a unique twist. The four- or five-course set menu comes either with fish and meat or in a vegetarian version. The wine list includes a selection of organic wines. To go with the set menu, there are wine pairings or an alcohol-free alternative. The front-of-house team is exceptionally friendly and professional; the chef, too, often puts in an appearance – they are happy to talk you through the dishes and provide information on the provenance of ingredients. Wood and a palette of muted tones make for a relaxed, cosy atmosphere.

Name: LAMENG Menue & Bistro
Description En: Two concepts under one roof. Menue is the cosy, modern little locale serving a six-course set menu that changes monthly, plus finger food to start and petits fours to finish. The delicious food is creative and ingredient-led – seasonal produce and a penchant for regional ingredients. You can also plump for the "sharing" format of the set menu. Service is friendly and attentive – the chef, too, serves up dishes himself. The second eatery is the Bistro, which delivers a slightly simpler culinary offering. In case you were wondering, the restaurant's name comes from the expression "aus der Lameng" and means "spontaneous, relaxed, off the cuff" – and that is indeed the motto by which they live here.

Name: BYBLOS
Description En: This appealing restaurant in Wilmersdorf is dedicated to Lebanese cuisine, with a menu that extends well beyond the classic mezze experience. The meticulously crafted and finely balanced dishes impress in terms of freshness and authenticity. Whether you opt for hummus, sambousek jebneh (fried filo pastry rolls filled with sheep's-milk cheese) or subtly spiced grilled specialities such as kafta meshwi (minced veal and lamb skewer), it's best to come with friends, as many of the dishes are ideal for sharing. Attentive service and Lebanese wines round off the Middle Eastern culinary experience. In the evenings, live piano music adds to the atmosphere.

Name: CYN CYN
Description En: A bright red frontage heralds this charming noodle bar with a lively, youthful atmosphere. Two German-Vietnamese chefs showcase the famous wide Biang Biang noodles from the Chinese province of Shaanxi, freshly prepared in the restaurant every day. Dressed with house-made sauces, their dishes deliver a rich and authentic taste experience. Their "Myx Myx" has become a signature dish, combining the wide, hand-pulled al dente "belt" noodles with hearty beef and lamb, as well as umami-rich soy sauce, to create a delicious dish. Vegetarian options are also available.

Name: Kluth
Description En: In the heart of the Ehrenfeld district, Hannes Radeck and Kevin Rademacker (formerly of Cologne's Ox & Klee) have struck out on their own. The ambitions of this chef-owner pair are evident in delicately composed, creative modern dishes, such as "Potato brioche, Comté, celery, grapes" or "Bresse chicken, hazelnut, leek". As an alternative to the à la carte selection, there is a six-course surprise menu dubbed "Et kütt wie et kütt" ("It is what it is"), available in a meat/fish or vegetarian version. Seasonality and organic produce are central to the concept, with many fermented and pickled ingredients being put to use – preserving jars serve as decorative touches throughout the trendy, Nordic-minimalist dining area. Seating options include standard tables, high tables, and spots at the service counter. The pleasingly relaxed, attentive and assured service also contributes to the appealing atmosphere. Don't forget to book.

Name: Rüpel
Description En: In this small restaurant in a bustling neighbourhood, a unique, cohesive concept is making waves: serving a modern vegan menu featuring seasonal produce from the region, they aim to use produce in its entirety; they also ferment and preserve ingredients. The chefs help serve the food, elaborating on the dishes and the ideas behind them. You get a real sense of the dedication of the owners, who are also often on site. There is a six-course set menu with optional add-ons, plus a good selection of organic wines. Staff are cordial and professional, contributing to the relaxed atmosphere in the pleasingly contemporary interior. Tip: It takes 15min to get here by tram from the main station.

Name: Weinforum Franken
Description En: This trendy, modern restaurant is perfectly summed up by its slogan of "French sophistication with a Franconian soul". The ambitious food, made with top-notch ingredients, is bold and expressive. The appealing menu includes a small à la carte selection (featuring dishes such as "Grass-fed beef tartare, crisps, wheat beer foam, mustard seeds, quail's egg, radishes"), a selection of dry-aged beef, and a weekly menu with dishes available individually or in a set menu format. It is no coincidence that they go by the name "Weinforum": on the premises, there is also an integrated wine shop with a good 120 wines from Main-Franconia and France available to buy and taste. In summer, al fresco dining on the terrace is highly enjoyable. Plus they have guestrooms for overnight stays. Tip: Events are held regularly – it's worth taking a look at the events calendar.

Name: ABC by Michi & Leo
Description En: A cool and rather unusual dining concept. In a round, glass-paned pavilion reminiscent of a beach bar, diners sit around the central counter in a relaxed, lively atmosphere. Pick from a modern tapas menu. Owner-sommelier Michi takes a friendly, laid-back approach to serving guests and always has the perfect wine recommendation up his sleeve. Chef Leo cooks up ambitious international-seasonal "freestyle" dishes, taking his cue from what the market has to offer and combining the selected produce with Latin American, Mediterranean, Asian, regional and even classic influences. You can look forward to the interesting flavours his menu has in store across up to 10 tapas dishes. Just as the menu changes, so too do the accompanying wines. Tip: The cocktails are also a good choice.

Name: jfk.
Description En: In a side room of Tim Mälzer's bustling Bullerei, the two hosts, Jule-Fee Poll and Kevin Bürmann – both previously employed at Haebel – bring their relaxed, modern concept to life. Jule-Fee Poll looks after diners in a laid-back manner, combining professionalism with a charming, personal touch. Meanwhile, the chef-patron prepares the surprise omakase menu, which comprises five courses and can be extended to include the classic "Toast Hawaii" – this nostalgic dish, presented with a humorous wink, is hugely popular. He is also happy to jump in and help serve dishes and talk diners through them. Fun fact: The restaurant is named after the owners, "jfk" being the initials of their first names (Jule-Fee and Kevin).

Name: Staderer
Description En: This restaurant in Das Altmühltal, a hotel right on the banks of the Altmühl River (after which it is named), is highly recommended! The stylish, modern interior is casual yet elegant. Laid out in front of the floor-to-ceiling windows, the lovely terrace boasts river views. Benjamin Schöneich, previously head chef at Restaurant Brogsitter in Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler, is in charge in the kitchen. He devises a five-course set menu that has its roots in French cuisine but also draws inspiration from further afield. Executed with great precision, his creative dishes are harmoniously balanced and make an impression: "Loup de mer from the Vendée, octopus, cannellini beans, fennel salami, tomato and feta fumet" or "Burgaud duck, beetroot, pistachio, sakura jus". The interesting wine list has a wealth of labels from renowned winemakers – principally German, Italian and French. You can opt for wine or alcohol-free pairings to accompany the set menu.

Name: Norms
Description En: In a side street, right next to the Volkspark am Weinbergsweg, this restaurant is run by a trio of owners: Björn Swanson, Norman Faust and Sabine Panzer-Faust. In a chic, modern setting with artfully laid tables, the concept is German cuisine "like grandma used to make" – only a little lighter and more refined. What better way to kick off the meal than with a delicious croquette filled with cured smoked pork loin, followed by smoked sprats from Kiel or flambéed turnip with wild garlic and sheep's yoghurt? Or perhaps Königsberger Klopse (meatballs in caper sauce)? The service is friendly and knowledgeable, and expert wine advice is provided. There is a small terrace on the pavement out front.

Name: Knausbira Stüble
Description En: This family-run business in the Hedelfingen district has been renowned for its fine cuisine for many years and is popular with older and younger diners alike. It all began in 1985 with Susanne and Hendrik Schallmeir, and now their son Gabriel and his wife Lia – the second generation – have joined the team. In the small open kitchen, father and son work like a well-oiled machine, upholding Swabian culinary traditions while embracing inspiration from modern international cuisine. Their menu ranges from classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (braised beef with onions and gravy) and Kässpätzle, to Kalbsleber Berliner Art (veal liver with onions and apple), or skrei with fregola sarda, Mediterranean vegetables and cavolo nero. Tip: Purchase house-made Maultaschen (Swabian pockets) to enjoy at home. In keeping with the traditional roots of the cuisine, this place oozes rustic charm and has a really cosy atmosphere. The leafy terrace is lovely in summer.

Name: GASSENHAUR
Description En: Despite looking quite unassuming from the outside, this first-floor bistro turns out to be a real little gem. Russet-red walls, beautiful hardwood floors and ornamental crystal chandeliers hanging from high ceilings make for a decidedly cosy ambience. The atmosphere is pleasingly laid-back, and that is in no small part thanks to the friendly and attentive service. Classic Viennese cuisine is the name of the game, offering the chance to try the original Wiener schnitzel made from veal loin – a freshly tapped beer is highly recommended to go with it. As an alternative to the à la carte selection, there is a three-course set menu. Tip: This place is very popular, so it's advisable to book!

Name: Salhino
Description En: This long-established family-run business serves up traditional Georgian cuisine. Specialities such as khinkali (dumplings filled with minced beef and pork) may seem simple at first glance, but there is more to them than meets the eye: wonderful textures, balanced flavours and harmonious seasoning. Let the cordial and attentive team guide you on how to get the most out of each dish – with the right technique, a truly comprehensive Georgian dining experience is guaranteed. These à la carte plates are ideal for sharing. Tip: Order a Georgian amber wine (orange wine) to accompany your food. The feast is to be savoured in a pleasant, cosy atmosphere, in an interior with lovely authentic decorative touches such as nostalgic photos and traditional accessories.

Name: Gasthaus Helmut
Description En: A place everyone would love to have in their neighbourhood. It is Andreas Reinke and Lisa Angermannin's second restaurant, after Frieda, which they also run in the city's Gohlis district. Within the walls of a beautifully maintained historical building, the setting is sleek and modern, with warm red tones enhancing the pleasant atmosphere. The menu features a tempting selection of delicious seasonal dishes, and the set menu on offer is also available in a vegetarian version. Pick a wine from the well-curated list. The restaurant is conveniently located about a 15min tram ride from the centre.
